Together, these strategies are argued to offer multimodal fungicidal mechanisms that lower the likelihood of resistance developing. Although the evidence base remains largely preclinical, the authors conclude that the convergence of repurposing and nanotechnology presents a promising pathway toward safer and more effective antifungal therapies, and they call for continued interdisciplinary effort to advance these approaches into clinical use.
items.citation: Zimeng You, Kaiwen Zhuang, Takashi Sugita et al.. Novel Strategies Against Fungal Infections: Repurposing Existing Drugs and Advancing Nanotherapeutics. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Dittany: Contribution-Guided Repair Framework for MAS Applications
items.summary: The paper investigates runtime repair of large language model-based multi-agent system applications, which often produce partial or flawed results that fail to fully satisfy task requirements. The authors developed a framework called Dittany that constructs a contribution graph by deriving expected contributions and acceptance conditions from task requirements and method specifications, then uses this graph at runtime to identify unmet conditions and determine which intermediate results remain valid. When failures are detected, the framework applies either action-level correction when sufficient inputs are available or graph-level recovery when prerequisites need revision, in both cases preserving validated contributions and verifying repaired outputs before downstream use. Evaluation across a large set of applications and tasks showed that the framework achieved substantially higher task accuracy than both native execution and competing recovery baselines, while keeping token consumption considerably lower than comparable repair approaches. Ablation studies confirmed that combining both repair scopes outperforms using graph-level repair alone in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
items.citation: Hanqi Sun, Yuchen Shao, Hanyi Si et al.. Dittany: Contribution-Guided Repair Framework for MAS Applications. arXiv. 2026

items.title: SATFRONT: Detecting Atmospheric Fronts with Satellite Data using Machine Learning
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of automatically detecting atmospheric fronts, which are major drivers of high-impact mid-latitude weather, without relying on the gridded reanalysis or forecast data that most existing deep learning approaches require. The authors developed SATFRONT, a machine learning framework that identifies cold, warm, and occluded fronts over Europe using geostationary satellite observations as its primary input, with reanalysis data available as an optional supplement. The model was trained on frontal analyses from multiple European national meteorological services and validated against independent analyses from the UK Met Office. Using satellite data alone, SATFRONT achieves detection skill that falls within the range of inter-agency agreement among human analysts and substantially outperforms an existing operational rule-based satellite-based front detector; incorporating reanalysis data further improves performance, particularly for the precise placement of individual fronts. The study demonstrates that automated, high-temporal-frequency frontal analysis directly from satellite imagery is feasible, opening pathways for near-real-time frontal detection in time-critical forecasting applications.
items.citation: Ioannis Dravilas, Miruna Stoicescu, Roope Tervo et al.. SATFRONT: Detecting Atmospheric Fronts with Satellite Data using Machine Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Soft X-Ray Detection Down to the Nitrogen K-Edge Using a Pixelated iLGAD Sensor
items.summary: This paper investigated inverse low-gain avalanche diode sensors designed to extend hybrid pixel detector technology into the soft X-ray energy regime, where achieving adequate quantum efficiency and signal-to-noise ratio has remained a longstanding challenge. The researchers integrated iLGAD sensors with thin entrance windows and systematically compared two gain layer designs — a standard gain layer and a shallow gain layer — evaluating their spectral response across photon energies and operating temperatures. Single-photon resolution was demonstrated at energies as low as the nitrogen K-edge region with a signal-to-noise ratio sufficient for practical detection. A notable double-peak feature was observed in the energy spectra, attributed to the dependence of charge multiplication on the depth at which photons are absorbed within the sensor. The study also developed a phenomenological spectral fitting model that allows quantitative extraction of key structural parameters, providing a foundation for scaling this technology into large-area, high-frame-rate detectors suitable for soft X-ray applications such as ptychography, spectroscopy, and resonant scattering at synchrotron and free-electron laser facilities.
items.citation: Shuqi Li, Anna Bergamaschi, Ashish Bisht et al.. Soft X-Ray Detection Down to the Nitrogen K-Edge Using a Pixelated iLGAD Sensor. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Tests of equivalence principle violation in doubly coupled dark energy
items.summary: This paper investigates a class of dark energy models in which dark matter couples to a scalar field while baryons do not, thereby violating the weak equivalence principle, and asks whether such violations can be detected using galaxy surveys. The authors generalize an existing coupled dark energy framework by introducing an additional nonminimal coupling between the scalar field and gravity, calling the result "doubly coupled dark energy," and define a parameter that quantifies equivalence principle violation on cosmological scales in a model-independent manner. Using forecasting methods applied to current and upcoming spectroscopic surveys, they assess the ability of these instruments to constrain the relevant coupling strengths while keeping the initial power spectrum shape and galaxy bias flexible across multiple bins. Among the surveys considered, the most futuristic radio telescope array is found to deliver the tightest constraints on the coupling strength, though the constraints degrade when both couplings are simultaneously varied and can be recovered by increasing the number of detected galaxies. The work demonstrates that large-scale structure surveys offer a viable route to testing equivalence principle violation in the dark sector.
items.citation: Yannick Kegel, Ziyang Zheng, Luca Amendola. Tests of equivalence principle violation in doubly coupled dark energy. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Proof-Carrying Evolution: Black-Box Search, White-Box Flight
items.summary: This paper investigates whether large language models can assist in designing control systems whose correctness can be formally verified. The authors introduce proof-carrying evolution, a framework in which a search process proposes controllers paired with mathematical certificates of their properties, with selection guided by whether candidates pass certificate checks and only certified designs deployed. Four language models were compared against classical search and synthesis methods across three control problems: spacecraft docking under a speed constraint, pursuit of a maneuvering target, and attitude control on a nonlinear manifold, with formal proofs generated in Lean 4 for the best solutions found. The strongest language models outperformed standard classical baselines on the linear problems, though a classical optimizer that jointly selects certificates largely closed this performance gap, and rankings among pursuit solutions were not robust to changes in the underlying dynamics model. On the nonlinear attitude control problem, language models did not consistently outperform classical evolutionary search, and all automated methods remained below a hand-tuned controller, while experiments confirmed that retaining certified candidates during search was essential for producing any certified final designs.
items.citation: Amit Jain, Sergio Sanchez-Hurtado, Victor Rodriguez-Fernandez et al.. Proof-Carrying Evolution: Black-Box Search, White-Box Flight. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A richness-sensitive Acoustic Biodiversity Index from species-level detections: classifier benchmarking, false-positive control and validation against standard soundscape indices in an African savanna and an urban zoo
items.summary: The paper develops and validates a revised Acoustic Biodiversity Index built from species-level detections rather than raw sound energy, addressing a known weakness of conventional acoustic indices in tracking species richness. The authors benchmarked four classifier approaches on a labelled tropical bird call dataset and found that BirdNET embeddings combined with logistic regression performed best, while also demonstrating that naive recording splits substantially inflate apparent classifier accuracy. They applied the best-performing classifier with location and season filtering to recordings from an African savanna and an urban zoo, incorporating a post-hoc plausibility filter that removed a substantial number of high-confidence but geographically implausible detections. The revised index, which expresses Shannon diversity of detections normalised against a regional species pool, correlated strongly with observed species richness across recorded hours, substantially outperforming six standard soundscape indices including the Acoustic Complexity Index. The authors conclude that species-level indices with explicit false-positive control, a declared regional reference pool, and effort standardisation offer a more interpretable and ecologically meaningful biodiversity indicator than energy-based acoustic indices.
items.citation: Muhammad Saeed, Dmitry Mikhaylov, Mohamed H. Alhosani et al.. A richness-sensitive Acoustic Biodiversity Index from species-level detections: classifier benchmarking, false-positive control and validation against standard soundscape indices in an African savanna and an urban zoo. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Multiplex molecular respiratory diagnostic panels and antimicrobial use in paediatric respiratory infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
items.citation: Bajaj R, Mehta P, Gopi A et al.. Multiplex molecular respiratory diagnostic panels and antimicrobial use in paediatric respiratory infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.. BMJ open. 2026

items.title: Syndromic Testing in Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases: An Updated Review of Diagnostic Performance, Clinical and Healthcare Impact, and Emerging Developments.
items.summary: This review examined the current state of syndromic testing in clinical microbiology, a diagnostic approach that simultaneously detects multiple pathogens and antimicrobial resistance determinants from clinical specimens using nucleic acid amplification. The authors surveyed available evidence across seven major clinical syndromes, covering commercially available panels cleared by regulatory authorities in the United States and their diagnostic performance, clinical applications, and limitations. Compared to traditional culture-based workflows with turnaround times of one to three or more days, syndromic panels deliver comprehensive pathogen identification within hours, enabling faster and more targeted antimicrobial therapy. Evidence supports that when integrated with antimicrobial stewardship programs, syndromic testing can reduce time to optimal therapy, decrease unnecessary antimicrobial use, and in some patient populations—particularly those with bloodstream infections—may confer a mortality benefit. The review also highlights that rapid results do not automatically translate into improved outcomes, and that challenges around appropriate panel utilization, evolving resistance epidemiology, and geographically variable pathogen distributions must be addressed to fully realize the technology's clinical potential.
items.citation: Wang G, Chen F. Syndromic Testing in Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases: An Updated Review of Diagnostic Performance, Clinical and Healthcare Impact, and Emerging Developments.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Development and validation of a multiplex TaqMan real-time quantitative PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of six major bacterial respiratory pathogens in goats.
items.summary: This study developed and validated two triplex TaqMan real-time quantitative PCR panels capable of simultaneously detecting six major bacterial and mycoplasmal respiratory pathogens in goats, including three Mycoplasma species and three bacterial species commonly associated with caprine respiratory disease. The assays were assessed for analytical specificity, sensitivity, and reproducibility using recombinant plasmid standards and nucleic acids from both target and non-target organisms, then evaluated on field-collected goat nasal swab samples. The panels demonstrated high specificity with no cross-reactivity against non-target organisms, low limits of detection for all six pathogens, and excellent reproducibility as indicated by low intra- and inter-assay coefficients of variation. When applied to clinical samples, the assay detected at least one target pathogen in more than half of the samples, with a substantial proportion showing co-infections involving two or more pathogens simultaneously. The authors conclude that this multiplex approach offers a rapid and reliable diagnostic tool suited for both clinical investigation and epidemiological surveillance of caprine respiratory disease.
items.citation: Fu M, Liu Y, Zhang Z et al.. Development and validation of a multiplex TaqMan real-time quantitative PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of six major bacterial respiratory pathogens in goats.. Frontiers in veterinary science. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy of rapid integrated molecular testing for major respiratory viral infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.citation: Liu C, Yu D. Diagnostic accuracy of rapid integrated molecular testing for major respiratory viral infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Clinical Relevance of Multiplex PCR for Respiratory Pathogens in Hospitalized Adults with Influenza-Like Illness.
items.summary: This study investigated the pathogens responsible for influenza-like illness in hospitalized adults and examined how molecular diagnostic results relate to clinical, laboratory, and radiological findings. Using a multiplex real-time PCR assay capable of detecting a broad range of viral and bacterial pathogens, researchers retrospectively analyzed adults admitted over two respiratory virus seasons at a single center. A pathogen was identified in fewer than half of patients, with *Streptococcus pneumoniae*, influenza viruses, and seasonal coronaviruses being the most commonly detected, and co-infection with influenza A and *S. pneumoniae* representing the most frequent combined finding. Among patients testing positive for *S. pneumoniae* by PCR, those with radiologically confirmed pneumonia were older, had greater disease severity by CURB-65 scoring, and more often had concurrent influenza infection compared to those lacking radiological evidence of pneumonia. The authors conclude that while multiplex molecular assays are valuable for pathogen detection, results for bacterial pathogens like *S. pneumoniae* must be interpreted alongside clinical and radiological data rather than in isolation.
items.venue: Journal of clinical practice and research
items.citation: Gülseren YD, Aydın D, Çetin Duran A. Clinical Relevance of Multiplex PCR for Respiratory Pathogens in Hospitalized Adults with Influenza-Like Illness.. Journal of clinical practice and research. 2026

items.title: ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
items.summary: This paper presents updated clinical guidelines from a major European gastroenterology organization addressing infection-related risks in patients with inflammatory bowel disease. The guidelines were developed in response to the rapid expansion of immunosuppressive and biologic therapies used to treat Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, including newer small molecules and advanced biologics that carry distinct infection risk profiles compared to older agents. The authors conducted a structured, evidence-based review covering risk stratification and the prevention, diagnosis, and management of viral, bacterial, mycobacterial, and vaccine-preventable infections in this immunocompromised patient population. The resulting recommendations update prior consensus statements and guidelines to reflect contemporary treatment paradigms, with an emphasis on preventative strategies tailored to the current therapeutic landscape. The guidelines aim to equip clinicians with practical, evidence-based tools for minimizing the morbidity and mortality associated with opportunistic infections in IBD patients receiving potent immune-modulating therapies.
items.venue: Journal of Crohn s and Colitis
items.citation: Henit A. Yanai, Pierre Ellul, Bram Verstockt et al.. ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease. Journal of Crohn s and Colitis. 2026

items.title: Small extracellular vesicle signaling and mitochondrial transfer reprogram T helper cell function in human asthma
items.summary: This study investigated the role of small extracellular vesicles derived from airway myeloid-derived regulatory cells in perpetuating asthmatic airway inflammation, with a focus on how these vesicles carry and transfer mitochondria to CD4+ T cells. The researchers used both in vitro approaches with human asthmatic airway cells and an in vivo murine asthma model to examine how vesicle-mediated mitochondrial transfer shapes T helper cell behavior. They found that these vesicles engage the T cell receptor and deliver mitochondria predominantly through membrane fusion, driving antigen-specific activation and polarization toward the pro-inflammatory Th17 and Th2 phenotypes that sustain chronic airway inflammation. Mitochondrial packaging into the vesicles depended on a Drp1-mediated fission mechanism in pro-inflammatory myeloid cells, and blocking reactive oxygen species signaling within the vesicles suppressed T cell activation. The authors conclude that sEV-mediated mitochondrial transfer represents a previously unrecognized pathway in asthma pathology and propose it as a potential novel therapeutic target.
items.citation: Kenneth P. Hough, Jennifer L. Trevor, Shaheer Ahmad et al.. Small extracellular vesicle signaling and mitochondrial transfer reprogram T helper cell function in human asthma. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Serologic Evidence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Infection in a Veterinary Professional Exposed to an Infected Domestic Cat — Los Angeles County, California, December 2024–January 2025
items.summary: This report investigated potential human infection with highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) virus following an outbreak among domestic cats in Los Angeles County that became ill after consuming raw animal products. Public health authorities monitored all persons exposed to the infected cats and later conducted a serosurvey to detect antibody evidence of infection, including among those who had no symptoms. Among the subset of exposed individuals who participated in serological testing, one asymptomatic veterinary professional showed antibodies specific to the H5N1 strain matching that found in the cats; this individual had not used respiratory or eye protection during exposures and had no other known risk factors. Although no exposed person tested positive by molecular testing during the monitoring period, the serological finding represents evidence of possible cat-to-human transmission of H5N1 virus. The findings underscore concerns about transmission of H5N1 from infected domestic cats to humans and emphasize the importance of infection control measures in veterinary settings.
items.venue: MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
items.citation: Aisling Vaughan, Allison Joyce, Elizabeth Traub et al.. Serologic Evidence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Infection in a Veterinary Professional Exposed to an Infected Domestic Cat — Los Angeles County, California, December 2024–January 2025. MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review examines hantaviruses, rodent-borne pathogens responsible for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, with a focus on how environmental and ecological changes are driving their emergence and spread. The authors synthesize current knowledge across virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnostics, and surveillance, with particular attention to how climate change, urbanization, and land-use transformation alter rodent reservoir dynamics and increase spillover risk to humans. The review identifies critical gaps in surveillance and diagnostics, especially in tropical and Caribbean regions where hantavirus circulation is likely underrecognized. Advances discussed include molecular and genomic diagnostic tools, vaccine development, monoclonal antibody therapies, and climate-based early warning systems. The authors argue that integrated One Health surveillance frameworks combining human, animal, and environmental monitoring, alongside strengthened laboratory capacity and regional collaboration, are essential for improving outbreak preparedness and reducing the global burden of hantavirus disease.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Skuas as sentinels of high pathogenicity avian influenza H5N1 on the Antarctic Peninsula in the 2024/2025 austral summer
items.summary: This study investigated the presence of highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 in wildlife on the Antarctic Peninsula and South Shetland Islands during the austral summer following the virus's first confirmed Antarctic incursion. Researchers conducted multiple sampling expeditions using cruise ship support, collecting environmental faecal samples from apparently healthy penguins and marine mammals, as well as sampling skua carcasses found near penguin colonies. No evidence of H5N1 was found in the faecal samples from live animals, but the virus was detected in nearly all skua carcasses tested. Genomic sequencing revealed that the viruses from skuas clustered within a single lineage distinct from those detected in the previous austral summer, indicating a new introduction rather than persistence of the earlier strain. The findings confirm that H5N1 is recurring in Antarctica despite its extreme geographic isolation, underscoring the importance of sustained wildlife surveillance even in the world's most remote regions.
items.citation: Michelle Wille, Will Abbott, Darrel Day et al.. Skuas as sentinels of high pathogenicity avian influenza H5N1 on the Antarctic Peninsula in the 2024/2025 austral summer. Microbial Genomics. 2026

items.title: Inflammation-driven immune reprogramming in sepsis: from cytokine storm to immunoparalysis
items.summary: This narrative review examines sepsis as a dynamic immune reprogramming disorder rather than a uniform inflammatory syndrome, arguing that this reconceptualization is essential for understanding why past therapeutic trials have failed. The authors synthesize recent advances in human immune profiling to describe how sepsis follows time-resolved trajectories and biologically distinct subtypes, in which hyperinflammatory and immune-suppressed states can occur simultaneously across different compartments rather than sequentially. They trace the core mechanisms connecting early innate immune sensing, endothelial injury, and coagulation-inflammation coupling to later immune paralysis, lymphocyte loss, and functional exhaustion, culminating in a chronic critical illness phenotype. From this mechanistic foundation, they propose a practical framework for dynamic immune monitoring that emphasizes longitudinal trends and composite signals rather than single biomarkers, and they explain past trial failures as a consequence of mismatched patient state, therapeutic direction, and timing. The review concludes by advocating for bidirectional, time-stamped immunomodulation strategies guided by repeated immune phenotyping, enriched patient enrollment, and outcome measures that capture secondary infections, organ recovery, and longer-term functional status.
items.citation: Sha Zhu, J Inghorn He. Inflammation-driven immune reprogramming in sepsis: from cytokine storm to immunoparalysis. Frontiers in Immunology. 2026

items.title: GazeRIB: Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Reader Gaze-Guided Chest X-ray Learning
items.summary: This paper investigated how the composition of radiologist reader panels affects the utility of gaze-based supervision for training chest X-ray classification models. The researchers developed and evaluated GazeRIB, a method that masks image regions not viewed by radiologists during training while using full images at inference, testing it across eight expert readers organized into panels of varying sizes, multiple neural network architectures, and random seeds. Panel-based gaze guidance consistently improved four-class severity prediction over a no-gaze baseline, with even a three-reader panel capturing the majority of the benefit achieved by the full eight-reader group. External validation revealed that performance gains transferred to one external dataset but not another, demonstrating that generalization depends on cohort characteristics. The findings establish that reader panel composition meaningfully influences model performance and that small panels may offer a practical compromise between annotation cost and classification benefit.
items.citation: Nattakorn Kittisut, Roy M. Gabriel, Marly van Assen et al.. GazeRIB: Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Reader Gaze-Guided Chest X-ray Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Grid-Refinement SBL for AFDM Channel Estimation Under Fractional Delay and Fractional Doppler Channels
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of channel estimation in affine frequency division multiplexing systems when channels exhibit fractional delay and fractional Doppler shifts, which complicate the delay-Doppler coupling in the received signal. The authors first established an exact channel model capturing these fractional characteristics and derived the corresponding input-output relationship. They then developed two sparse Bayesian learning approaches: a first-order linear approximation grid-refinement method and a more robust two-dimensional grid-approximation algorithm that iteratively refines the delay-Doppler grid to overcome convergence and stability limitations of the first approach. Simulation results show that both proposed algorithms substantially outperform existing on-grid and off-grid sparse Bayesian learning benchmarks in normalized mean square error and bit error rate performance.
items.citation: Qu Luo, Limin Liu, Zhe Li et al.. Grid-Refinement SBL for AFDM Channel Estimation Under Fractional Delay and Fractional Doppler Channels. arXiv. 2026

items.title: "Existential dread": Student and faculty views on the impact of changes in federal science funding to physics research
items.summary: This paper examined how changes to federal science funding in the United States beginning in early 2025 affected academic physics researchers across multiple career stages. The researchers administered surveys to physics undergraduate students, graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, and faculty at the associate professor level to capture perceptions of the funding disruptions, which included grant cuts, delayed or canceled review panels, and hiring and spending freezes at some universities. The majority of respondents perceived the impacts on their research as negative, with the most commonly reported consequences being loss of existing funding, anxiety about securing future funding, and job insecurity. The study also identified differences in how these impacts were experienced depending on career stage, raising concerns about the downstream effects on the pipeline that trains the next generation of scientists.
items.citation: Meagan Sundstrom, Ian Olivant, Eric Brewe. "Existential dread": Student and faculty views on the impact of changes in federal science funding to physics research. arXiv. 2026

items.title: QBX: A Compiler for Well-Formed, Auditable Alpha Programs
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of reproducibility and comparability in formulaic alpha mining, where different systems couple their own representations, evaluators, and selectors into incompatible pipelines. The authors present QBX, a compiler that defines a well-formed and auditable space of alpha programs through a versioned block registry and a directed acyclic graph language, producing a structured intermediate representation carrying type information, time-availability effects, executable linkage, and content identities for deduplication and provenance tracking. A key feature is an availability-effect system that automatically rejects proposals containing look-ahead bias while permitting legitimate point-in-time forecasts. Evaluated on Chinese A-share equity panels, the compiler dramatically increases the proportion of evaluation-valid proposals compared to free-text or grammar-only baselines, while incremental evaluation substantially accelerates search replay with numerical equivalence, and the availability checker eliminates look-ahead violations across tens of thousands of candidates. The authors emphasize that these gains concern validity, computational reuse, and search efficiency within a registered vocabulary rather than any increase in the underlying market information available.
items.citation: Yichong Bai, Kaigui Bian. QBX: A Compiler for Well-Formed, Auditable Alpha Programs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Co$^2$ODE: Conditionally Coarse-Grained Model Discovery for Rewiring in Biochemical Networks
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of learning how cellular signaling networks are rewired when biological context changes, a problem where mechanistic models are unreliable due to incomplete knowledge of interaction structures and where standard model discovery approaches are hampered by sparse, correlated measurements. The authors developed conditionally coarse-grained ODEs (Co²ODE), a framework that combines a conditional masking mechanism to isolate context-dependent rewiring with a variational autoencoder that compresses the remaining network markers into a learned closure term, enabling focused modeling of the rewired portion. Applied to single-cell phosphoproteomic data spanning many cancer-relevant genetic overexpressions, the method successfully compressed a large marker panel into a substantially lower-dimensional state while retaining the predictive accuracy of a full neural ODE fitted to all markers. Notably, the learned closure compensated for whichever markers were excluded by the mask, making accuracy robust to marker selection. The authors also found that adding biological prior information to the objective shifted marker selection without degrading model fit, suggesting the data lack sufficient interventional richness to uniquely identify the underlying biological mechanisms on their own.
items.citation: Theodore de Pomereu, Fabian Fröhlich. Co$^2$ODE: Conditionally Coarse-Grained Model Discovery for Rewiring in Biochemical Networks. arXiv. 2026

items.title: GESIS Surf: An Open-Source Infrastructure for Privacy-Preserving Longitudinal Web Browsing Data Collection
items.summary: This paper presents GESIS Surf, an open-source research infrastructure designed to collect longitudinal web browsing data from large panels of participants while preserving privacy. The system addresses limitations of both commercial tracking tools, which lack transparency, and academic tools, which are typically narrow in scope, by providing a general-purpose platform for studying naturalistic digital behavior over time. GESIS Surf comprises a browser extension for Chrome and Firefox, a REST API backend, and a relational database that passively captures user interactions, page metadata, and full HTML snapshots organized within a hierarchical session model. Privacy is enforced through opt-in participation, per-domain collection rules, and client-side data minimization so that sensitive information is controlled before transmission. The infrastructure has been deployed with a large panel of participants in an academic setting that combines behavioral data collection with participant surveys, enabling reproducible, content-level analysis of digital behavior.
items.citation: Mario Alberto Ramirez, Frank Mangold, Sebastian Stier. GESIS Surf: An Open-Source Infrastructure for Privacy-Preserving Longitudinal Web Browsing Data Collection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Two Pentaplex Real-Time Fluorescent PCR Assays for Simultaneous Detection of Ten Ovine Respiratory and Reproductive Pathogens.
items.summary: This study developed and validated two pentaplex real-time PCR assays designed to simultaneously detect ten important pathogens affecting sheep, covering both respiratory and reproductive diseases in a single workflow. The two panels collectively target viruses and other pathogens including Bluetongue virus, Foot-and-mouth disease virus, Peste des petits ruminants virus, Brucella, and Toxoplasma gondii, among others, using six fluorescent detection channels per panel. Analytical validation demonstrated very low limits of detection, excellent linearity, and minimal variability between and within runs, while cross-reactivity testing confirmed that each assay detected only its intended targets without interference from the others. Testing against a large set of clinical samples from multiple regions showed strong agreement with established reference diagnostic methods. The authors conclude that these multiplex assays offer a rapid, sensitive, and specific approach for differential diagnosis and surveillance of major ovine pathogens in field settings.
items.citation: Wang S, Bai Z, Wan B et al.. Two Pentaplex Real-Time Fluorescent PCR Assays for Simultaneous Detection of Ten Ovine Respiratory and Reproductive Pathogens.. Viruses. 2026

items.title: Nanobodies: A Promising Toolkit for Diagnostic Applications
items.summary: This review examines nanobodies — single-domain antigen-binding fragments derived from camelid heavy-chain-only antibodies — as tools for diagnostic applications. The authors summarize the structural and biochemical properties of nanobodies, including their small size, high solubility, and stability, which enable recognition of less accessible epitopes and improved tissue penetration compared to conventional antibodies. The paper surveys how nanobodies have been integrated into a range of detection platforms, including ELISA, lateral flow immunoassays, biosensors, and in vivo imaging modalities such as PET and SPECT. The authors also review advances in multivalent designs, site-specific conjugation, and expression systems that have improved nanobody performance in clinical diagnostics, as well as ongoing clinical trials. Finally, the review discusses emerging strategies for developing scalable and sensitive nanobody-based diagnostic platforms suitable for practical clinical deployment.
items.citation: Wei Wu, Abid Ali, Li Sun et al.. Nanobodies: A Promising Toolkit for Diagnostic Applications. SmartMat. 2026

items.title: Machine-learning-integrated NLRC3 and cardiac troponin T dual-analyte lateral-flow biosensor for point-of-care acute coronary syndrome screening and acute myocardial infarction-unstable angina discrimination.
items.summary: This paper developed a point-of-care lateral-flow biosensor designed to simultaneously detect two biomarkers—NLRC3, an inflammatory marker, and cardiac troponin T, a myocardial injury marker—to improve diagnosis of acute coronary syndromes. The biosensor uses europium nanoparticle time-resolved fluorescence in a dual-channel format and delivers quantitative results within twenty minutes from serum samples. A Naïve Bayes machine-learning classifier was integrated to combine signals from both analytes, addressing the challenge of distinguishing acute myocardial infarction from unstable angina, a discrimination that neither biomarker alone could accomplish reliably. Clinical evaluation showed that while NLRC3 alone achieved moderate accuracy for identifying acute coronary syndrome, the dual-analyte machine-learning approach substantially improved sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy for separating the two conditions. The authors propose this dual-pathophysiology platform as a practical decentralized triage tool that bridges inflammatory risk assessment and myocardial injury detection in a single rapid test.
items.citation: Gu X, Teng P, Li X et al.. Machine-learning-integrated NLRC3 and cardiac troponin T dual-analyte lateral-flow biosensor for point-of-care acute coronary syndrome screening and acute myocardial infarction-unstable angina discrimination.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: Smartphone AI-Enabled Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform Using Advanced Quantum Dots for Intelligent Quantitative Diagnostics.
items.citation: Atta S, Thorsen TL, Vasse T et al.. Smartphone AI-Enabled Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform Using Advanced Quantum Dots for Intelligent Quantitative Diagnostics.. ACS applied materials & interfaces. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.
items.summary: This review examines lateral flow immunoassay technology as a diagnostic platform for viral infectious diseases, reframing it not merely as a point-of-care tool but as a point-of-need self-testing platform capable of supporting large-scale epidemic surveillance and pandemic preparedness. The authors systematically survey recent advances across three main dimensions: signal generation and transduction strategies employing diverse nanomaterials such as colorimetric, fluorescent, magnetic, surface-enhanced Raman scattering, and photothermal systems; multimodal and multiplex detection approaches aimed at improving sensitivity, accuracy, and throughput; and the integration of machine learning for signal interpretation and system optimization. Applications in detecting viral antigens, antibodies, and nucleic acids are comprehensively reviewed alongside current limitations including sensitivity constraints, target specificity issues, and practical challenges related to cost, usability, and stability. The review proposes future directions centered on advanced nanomaterials, intelligent data processing, and multi-target detection strategies to overcome these shortcomings. Overall, the authors argue that lateral flow immunoassay, particularly colorimetric formats, holds transformative potential as an emergency screening tool and for strengthening decentralized routine testing within global public health systems.
items.citation: Li L, Liu F, He X et al.. Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Rational Control of Antibody Orientation for Enhancing Sensitivity and Specificity in Lateral Flow Immunoassays With Clinical Validation.
items.summary: This paper investigated strategies to improve the sensitivity and specificity of lateral flow immunoassays (LFAs), which are commonly used for point-of-care diagnostics but are limited by inefficient antibody orientation on immunoprobes. The researchers developed a universal approach combining orientation-controlled antibody conjugation on immunoprobes with a biotin-streptavidin-modified test line to maximize antigen accessibility and suppress nonspecific binding. This optimized configuration dramatically improved detection limits for lung cancer biomarkers compared to conventional randomly conjugated probes, with sensitivity enhancements achieved across multiple clinically relevant cancer antigens including AFP, CA125, CA15-3, and PSA, demonstrating the strategy's broad applicability. The study also revealed that probe performance rankings can invert depending on the capture chemistry used, highlighting the importance of controlling antibody orientation at both the probe and test line simultaneously. Multiplexed detection of two biomarkers was further demonstrated using fluorescent polymer dot probes with minimal cross-reactivity, and the platform was validated against a hospital reference method using clinical serum samples.
items.citation: Wang PH, Shunmuga Nainar SN, Zhuang BH et al.. Rational Control of Antibody Orientation for Enhancing Sensitivity and Specificity in Lateral Flow Immunoassays With Clinical Validation.. Advanced healthcare materials. 2026

items.title: Ligand-directed Janus self-assembly with dual-aggregation enabling magneto-optical switching for enhanced lateral flow immunoassay.
items.citation: Liu T, Sun J, Huang J et al.. Ligand-directed Janus self-assembly with dual-aggregation enabling magneto-optical switching for enhanced lateral flow immunoassay.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Beyond lateral flow: vertical flow immunoassays as thermodynamically assisted rapid diagnostics.
items.summary: This review examines vertical flow immunoassays (VFAs) as an alternative to the dominant lateral flow immunoassay (LFA) format used in point-of-care diagnostics. The authors analyze how the single-pass capillary architecture of LFAs imposes fundamental physical limitations, including poor analyte capture efficiency, high non-specific background, constrained multiplexing, and unreliability at high analyte concentrations. VFAs address these shortcomings through a stacked-membrane design that separates convective delivery from immunoreaction kinetics, enabling effective thermodynamic washing, two-dimensional multiplexing arrays, and elimination of the hook effect. Head-to-head comparisons against chemistry-matched LFAs demonstrate substantial improvements in detection limits, and integration with surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy, electrochemical transduction, nanoparticle amplification, and deep-learning analysis pushes sensitivity into the sub-picogram-per-milliliter range. Despite this demonstrated performance advantage, the review maps the engineering and commercialization barriers that have prevented VFAs from achieving broad clinical and industrial deployment, and proposes a realistic pathway toward practical implementation.
items.citation: Nainar SNS, Chu YY, Lin HC et al.. Beyond lateral flow: vertical flow immunoassays as thermodynamically assisted rapid diagnostics.. Chemical communications (Cambridge, England). 2026

items.title: Recent advances in Alzheimer’s disease: From molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies
items.summary: This review examines the current state of Alzheimer's disease research, encompassing both the molecular mechanisms underlying the disease and emerging therapeutic approaches. The authors synthesize recent advances across several domains, including the biology of apolipoprotein E, neuroimmunology, and biomarker discovery, situating these within the broader context of established hallmarks such as amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles. The review also discusses early clinical experience with new disease-modifying therapies that can slow cognitive decline by clearing amyloid from the brain, while acknowledging that treatments capable of preventing or halting cognitive impairment altogether have not yet been achieved. The authors conclude that these converging discoveries are transforming how Alzheimer's disease is diagnosed and treated, offering optimism for future strategies aimed at both treatment and prevention.
items.citation: Michelle Diane Rudman, Jason D. Ulrich, David M. Holtzman. Recent advances in Alzheimer’s disease: From molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies. Cell. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review examines hantaviruses, rodent-borne pathogens responsible for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, in the context of a rapidly changing global environment. The authors synthesize current knowledge across virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnostics, and prevention, with particular attention to how climate change, urbanization, and land-use transformation drive shifts in rodent reservoir populations and increase spillover risk to humans. The review highlights significant surveillance and diagnostic gaps in tropical and Caribbean regions where hantavirus circulation is likely underappreciated. Advances in molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance, vaccine development, monoclonal antibody therapies, and climate-based early warning systems are identified as promising tools for improving outbreak detection and response. The authors conclude that integrated One Health surveillance frameworks combining human, animal, and environmental monitoring, alongside strengthened laboratory capacity and regional collaboration, are essential for reducing the global burden of hantavirus disease and preparing for future zoonotic threats.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: The Oral–Gut–Brain Axis: From Periodontal Dysbiosis to Neuroinflammation—Mechanistic Pathways, Salivary and Intestinal Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Targets: A Narrative Review
items.summary: This narrative review examines the mechanistic connections linking periodontal disease, gut microbiome disruption, and neuroinflammation within what the authors term the oral–gut–brain axis. The authors synthesized evidence from a broad literature search, focusing on how periodontal dysbiosis may propagate systemic inflammation through disruption of intestinal homeostasis and ultimately contribute to neurodegenerative processes. Key periodontal pathogens have been detected ectopically in the gut and associated with reduced tight junction protein expression, altered microbial composition, increased blood–brain barrier permeability, microglial activation, and amyloid-beta accumulation in preclinical and observational work. Salivary and intestinal biomarkers, including various cytokines, matrix metalloproteinases, short-chain fatty acids, and calprotectin, are proposed as non-invasive tools for monitoring inflammatory burden across this tripartite axis. The authors conclude that while the oral–gut–brain axis offers a plausible unifying framework for understanding comorbidities spanning periodontal, cardiometabolic, and neurodegenerative diseases, current evidence remains predominantly associative and mechanistic claims require validation through longitudinal human studies.
items.citation: Caterina Nela Dumitru, Alina Oana Dumitru, Gabriel Valeriu Popa et al.. The Oral–Gut–Brain Axis: From Periodontal Dysbiosis to Neuroinflammation—Mechanistic Pathways, Salivary and Intestinal Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Targets: A Narrative Review. Dentistry Journal. 2026

items.title: Genomic insights into multidrug-resistant bacteria: Emergence of mcr-1.1 in Escherichia coli , bla KPC-2 in Klebsiella pneumoniae and Serratia marcescens from clinical settings
items.summary: This study conducted detailed genomic characterization of multidrug-resistant clinical bacterial isolates from a hospital setting in China, examining strains of *Escherichia coli*, *Klebsiella pneumoniae*, and *Serratia marcescens*. Whole-genome sequencing and analysis were used to identify resistance genes, virulence determinants, plasmid types, and sequence types across these isolates. The *E. coli* strain was found to co-harbor the colistin resistance gene *mcr-1.1* alongside multiple other resistance determinants carried on several plasmid types, representing a concerning combination of mobile resistance elements. The *K. pneumoniae* isolates, spanning two sequence types, all carried the carbapenemase gene *blaKPC-2* together with various additional resistance genes on diverse plasmid backgrounds, and *S. marcescens* was notably identified as a carrier of *blaKPC-2* as well. The authors conclude that these findings reveal broad genomic diversity among clinical multidrug-resistant pathogens and underscore an urgent need for enhanced surveillance to monitor the spread of these resistance mechanisms.
items.citation: Muhammad Fazal Hameed, Muhammad Shoaib, Kai Peng et al.. Genomic insights into multidrug-resistant bacteria: Emergence of mcr-1.1 in Escherichia coli , bla KPC-2 in Klebsiella pneumoniae and Serratia marcescens from clinical settings. Virulence. 2026

items.title: Quantum dot biosensors for highly sensitive and multiplex detection in biomedical diagnostics
items.summary: This review examines quantum dot-based biosensors as a platform for biomedical diagnostics, focusing on their potential to overcome the limitations of conventional immunoassays such as low sensitivity, photobleaching, and poor optical penetration in biological tissues. The authors survey recent advances across fluorescent, photoelectrochemical, and electrochemiluminescent biosensor formats, connecting quantum dot surface engineering strategies—including functionalization with antibodies, aptamers, peptides, and nucleic acids—to their underlying sensing mechanisms. Near-infrared-emitting quantum dots receive particular attention for their ability to reduce tissue autofluorescence and enable deeper in vivo imaging for real-time molecular tracking. The review covers the detection of pathogens, cancer biomarkers, and metabolites while also addressing challenges of toxicity and biocompatibility, discussing mitigation approaches such as surface passivation, cadmium-free compositions, and biocompatible coatings. The authors position their contribution as a mechanistically integrated perspective that links material design to clinical translational relevance, intended to guide the development of next-generation diagnostic tools.
items.citation: Soumendu Patra, Harshita Shand. Quantum dot biosensors for highly sensitive and multiplex detection in biomedical diagnostics. Discover Sensors. 2026

items.title: Secret-shared teleportation of a two-qudit gate with a deferred recipient
items.summary: This paper investigates whether the capability to apply a specific quantum gate can be distributed across multiple parties in a secret-sharing framework, rather than being committed to a fixed destination at the time the resource is created. The authors devise a protocol in which a provider encrypts half of a Bell pair into shares distributed among candidate nodes in advance, and a later key release designates exactly one node to complete a non-local entangling gate with a user's data. The scheme guarantees that any coalition smaller than the full set of candidate nodes, or the key register alone, gains no information about the gate, unselected nodes cannot detect whether a selection occurred, and the key cannot be used twice. The construction works for arbitrary qudit dimension and allows the user to choose the gate's power parameter independently, with encoder and decoder circuits that scale linearly in the number of shares. The authors claim this advances distributed quantum computing by enabling jointly authorized and anonymous gate application across quantum networks.
items.citation: Tanay Roy. Secret-shared teleportation of a two-qudit gate with a deferred recipient. arXiv. 2026

items.title: RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory
items.summary: This paper investigates whether the design of agent harnesses — control code wrappers that orchestrate when a frozen robot policy queries vision tools, moves the arm, or makes decisions — can be automated rather than hand-crafted for each new robot or task. The proposed system, RoboArchitect, uses a coding model to observe a robot's rollouts, diagnose failure modes, and iteratively revise the harness around a frozen underlying policy, without updating any model weights. The harness is optimized on a set of training episodes and then evaluated on held-out scenes and tasks to assess generalization. RoboArchitect substantially improves success rates on both unseen scenes and unseen tasks across multiple benchmarks and policies, with gains being largest when the benchmark is distant from the policy's original training distribution, where the evolved harness can outperform even finetuned versions of the policy. The system also autonomously develops interpretable control strategies and a persistent memory mechanism that carries learned experience, such as effective grasp depths, across decisions, suggesting that significant untapped performance in robotic manipulation resides in harness design rather than model weights alone.
items.citation: Shengguang Wu, Suning Huang, Cherie Ho et al.. RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Gradient Descent on Two ReLU Neurons: Global Landscape and Bifurcation Dynamics
items.summary: This paper investigates how gradient descent learns features in a minimal neural network setting, using a two-neuron ReLU teacher-student model with isotropic Gaussian inputs trained via population gradient flow from small initialization. The authors characterize the full loss landscape and prove that every critical point where both student weights are nonzero is either a global minimum or a saddle point. They identify two key directions organizing the dynamics — an "easy" bisector direction that captures the leading signal and a "hard" splitting direction that governs neuron specialization — and show that the gradient-flow trajectory passes through a multi-phase process in which student neurons first collapse toward a bisector saddle before escaping and specializing to match the teacher neurons. Together, these results provide a unified landscape and dynamical account of symmetry breaking in a simple but nontrivial multi-index model under standard architectural and algorithmic conditions.
items.citation: Binghua Li, Mengzhe Li, Denny Wu et al.. Gradient Descent on Two ReLU Neurons: Global Landscape and Bifurcation Dynamics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Charge Pumping Leptogenesis from the Symmetric Mass Generation Phase on a Four-Leg Ladder Lattice
items.summary: This paper investigates what happens to quantized charge pumping in quantum Hall-like systems when the boundary is rendered gapped through symmetric mass generation (SMG), an interaction-driven mechanism that gaps fermion edge modes without breaking symmetry. Using density-matrix renormalization group simulations of a four-leg ladder lattice realizing a quasi-two-dimensional chiral fermion model with multi-fermion interactions at one edge, the authors map out three distinct boundary phases: gapless regimes at weak and strong coupling, a fully gapped SMG phase at intermediate coupling, and a spontaneous symmetry-breaking phase above a critical interaction strength. Across all three phases, quantized charge pumping persists with the same pumped charge per flux quantum, though the spatial distribution of the pumped charge differs between phases. In the SMG phase specifically, an interaction-induced flavor-mixing current emerges at the endpoints of the gapped edge when a single fermion is injected, revealing a charge-redistribution mechanism unique to that phase. The authors further propose an analogy between this charge pumping scenario and a topological leptogenesis mechanism in the Standard Model, drawing a parallel between the anomaly-free chiral symmetries of their lattice model and the baryon-minus-lepton symmetry, suggesting that charge pumping tied to a quantum-anomalous classical direction with an exact discrete quantum subgroup may have broader physical relevance.
items.citation: Runze Chi, Meng Zeng, Tao Xiang et al.. Charge Pumping Leptogenesis from the Symmetric Mass Generation Phase on a Four-Leg Ladder Lattice. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On nowhere-zero ${3}$-flows in Cayley graphs on groups of order ${p^2n}$
items.summary: The paper investigates Tutte's 3-flow conjecture, which posits that every bridgeless graph with no cut edge admits a nowhere-zero 3-flow, within the specific class of Cayley graphs constructed on finite groups whose order has the form p²n, where p is prime and n is square-free and coprime to p. Building on prior results that established the conjecture for special subcases, the authors extend the proof to the situation where p is an odd prime and either the Sylow p-subgroup or the Hall n-subgroup of the group is cyclic. Their work thus advances the verification of this long-standing conjecture by covering a broader family of group structures within this order class.
items.citation: Milad Ahanjideh, István Kovács. On nowhere-zero ${3}$-flows in Cayley graphs on groups of order ${p^2n}$. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Dirichlet form approach to stochastic thin-film equations
items.summary: This paper studies the stochastic thin-film equation, which models the evolution of a thin liquid film under capillarity and viscosity while accounting for thermal fluctuations via the fluctuation-dissipation principle. The authors apply the mathematical framework of Dirichlet forms and associated Markov process theory, identifying this as a natural fit for overdamped continuum evolution equations with thermal noise that possess a gradient flow structure. Working in the one-plus-one-dimensional setting—where a Gibbsian equilibrium measure is available—they establish existence and uniqueness of the evolution of probability laws on configuration space and show that the regularity of the resulting Markov process aligns with physical expectations. In a simplified setting with a Gaussian reference measure and non-degenerate mobility, they characterize the process as an energy solution, providing a pathwise decomposition of forces into deterministic and thermal components. Extending these techniques to a spatially discretized setting, they prove uniform tightness of Galerkin and spectral approximations in optimal topologies and establish Mosco convergence of the associated Dirichlet forms, thereby obtaining convergence of these numerical approximations.
items.citation: Benjamin Gess, Felix Otto, Max Sauerbrey. Dirichlet form approach to stochastic thin-film equations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Validation and performance of a rapid HIV-1 viral load assay.
items.summary: The paper evaluated the Xpert HIV-1 Viral Load XC assay as a candidate for primary nucleic acid testing within HIV-1 diagnostic workflows, with the goal of enabling both diagnosis and viral load measurement in a single clinical encounter at the point of care. Researchers assessed the assay's analytical range, precision, and agreement against a standard-of-care quantitative platform, as well as four other HIV assays including a qualitative nucleic acid test. The assay demonstrated strong linearity across its measurable range, full detection at tested concentrations, and complete agreement with the reference quantitative assay on a panel of positive and negative plasma samples. However, positive agreement with other comparator assays was incomplete, with most discrepancies arising in samples below the lower limit of quantification, and a notable invalid result rate was observed. Although turnaround time was substantially faster than conventional batch testing, the findings underscore ongoing limitations in sensitivity and reliability that must be addressed before rapid molecular diagnostics can be confidently integrated into HIV-1 diagnostic algorithms.
items.citation: Uhteg K, Bayan MH, Boudreau A et al.. Validation and performance of a rapid HIV-1 viral load assay.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Patient perspectives on point-of-care HIV nucleic acid tests for viral load monitoring in Seattle, WA.
items.summary: This study examined the acceptability of point-of-care nucleic acid testing for HIV viral load monitoring among people with HIV in Seattle, Washington. Participants enrolled in the GAIN Study received semi-quantitative point-of-care testing using the SAMBA II HIV-1 Semi-Quantitative Whole Blood Test and were then invited to complete acceptability surveys and in-depth interviews about their experiences. Participants generally preferred the point-of-care approach over standard laboratory testing, particularly appreciating the faster turnaround time and the convenience of a fingerstick sample collected within the clinic visit. However, participants expressed a desire for an even shorter turnaround time than the approximately two hours the test required, as well as a lower limit of detection than the current threshold. The authors conclude that point-of-care nucleic acid testing is acceptable to people with HIV and may be especially beneficial for those with inconsistent engagement in care, though improvements in speed and sensitivity would better support implementation in United States clinical settings.
items.citation: Niemann LA, Murphy M, Violette LR et al.. Patient perspectives on point-of-care HIV nucleic acid tests for viral load monitoring in Seattle, WA.. AIDS care. 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article addresses the longstanding question in exercise immunology of whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. There is broad agreement that regular moderate-intensity exercise supports immune defense, particularly in vulnerable populations, whereas high-performance athletes and military personnel appear to experience elevated infection burdens. The central controversy examined is whether arduous exercise directly impairs immunity or whether confounding factors common to these populations—such as psychological stress, sleep disruption, travel, nutritional deficits, and environmental extremes—are responsible for the increased infection rates observed. Opposing groups contested the evidence on athlete infection susceptibility, the validity of biomarkers used to assess immune health, and the quality of scientific data underpinning claims about exercise-induced immunosuppression. Both sides agreed that infection susceptibility is multifactorial, but whether exercise itself is a causative factor remains unresolved, with the authors calling for further empirical research to clarify these complex relationships.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review paper examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and translational medicine. The authors synthesize how genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic approaches provide deep insight into disease mechanisms, and how deep learning architectures can decode these complex biological datasets to identify patterns and build predictive models. The review covers the application of this combined approach across the drug development pipeline, including target identification, drug repositioning, de novo compound design, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Disease areas explored include oncology, neurodegeneration, and cardiovascular conditions, and the authors highlight the capacity of this technological convergence to accelerate and refine clinical trial design. The review also acknowledges persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate data streams, ensuring reproducibility, and addressing algorithmic bias, while arguing that overcoming these obstacles will define a new era of bench-to-clinic therapeutic innovation.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Trial design and end points in hepatocellular carcinoma: an EASL–AASLD–ILCA consensus statement
items.citation: Josep Maria Llovet, Ezequiel Mauro, Lorenza Rimassa et al.. Trial design and end points in hepatocellular carcinoma: an EASL–AASLD–ILCA consensus statement. Nature Reviews Clinical Oncology. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges
items.summary: This systematic review examined the potential of CRISPR-Cas systems as precision antimicrobials against multidrug-resistant bacteria, which have increasingly undermined the effectiveness of conventional antibiotics. The authors synthesized preclinical and experimental evidence on how different CRISPR effectors, primarily Cas9 but also Cas12 and Cas13, can kill bacteria or restore antibiotic sensitivity through mechanisms such as chromosomal double-strand break induction, resistance plasmid elimination, and RNA-targeted cleavage. Delivery strategies evaluated included bacteriophages, conjugative plasmids, and nanoparticle systems, with phage-mediated delivery showing the most consistent efficacy across complex environments and animal models. The review found broad support for CRISPR-Cas antimicrobials as a promising approach, noting that at least one CRISPR-enhanced engineered bacteriophage cocktail has progressed to clinical evaluation. However, the authors identified substantial remaining barriers, including limited bacterial host range, physiological instability, emergence of escape mutations, and insufficient long-term safety data, concluding that optimized delivery platforms, multiplex targeting, and standardized regulatory frameworks will be necessary for successful clinical translation.
items.citation: Maha S.I. Wizrah. CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline for invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. Part 1: Diagnostics and prevention – Update 2026
items.summary: This paper presents an updated European consensus guideline on the diagnostics and prevention of invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, one of the most frequent cancers in white populations. A multidisciplinary collaboration of European oncology and dermatology organizations revised previous recommendations based on current literature and expert consensus. The guideline introduces a new classification system dividing cases into easy-to-treat and difficult-to-treat categories, with the latter further subdivided into five groups reflecting clinical complexity, ranging from common but challenging cases through locally advanced disease to locoregional and distant metastases. Diagnosis follows a structured three-step approach encompassing clinical and dermatoscopic assessment, histopathological confirmation, and staging using established systems such as the American Joint Committee on Cancer eighth edition and the Brigham and Women's Hospital systems, with imaging reserved for indicated cases. Prevention recommendations include sun protection measures and oral nicotinamide, and the guideline addresses both immunocompetent and immunosuppressed patient populations.
items.citation: Alexander J. Stratigos, Clio Dessinioti, Claus Garbe et al.. European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline for invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. Part 1: Diagnostics and prevention – Update 2026. European Journal of Cancer. 2026

items.title: APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update
items.summary: These clinical practice guidelines address the ongoing burden of chronic hepatitis B infection in the Asia Pacific region, where the disease continues to drive substantial morbidity and mortality through complications such as acute-on-chronic liver failure, end-stage cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. The guidelines were developed by a dedicated Viral Elimination Taskforce assembled by the APASL, bringing together key opinion leaders from across member countries and regions to produce updated, consensus-based recommendations. The taskforce incorporated evolving epidemiological trends, socioeconomic changes, and technological advances into its deliberations. The resulting guidelines span thirteen major areas encompassing screening, vaccination, antiviral treatment, and hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance, with the aim of supporting healthcare professionals, policymakers, and patients in making practical and cost-effective management decisions. The overarching goal is to translate these recommendations into meaningful progress toward eliminating the disease burden of chronic hepatitis B across the Asia Pacific region.
items.citation: Hong You, Rakhi Maiwall, Jing Chen et al.. APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update. Hepatology International. 2026

items.title: Co-sufficient weighting: leveraging sparsity for more powerful variable selection in the linear model
items.summary: The paper addresses controlled variable selection in the Gaussian linear model, asking whether informative weights for weighted multiple testing can be derived from the data alone, without external side information. The authors introduce co-sufficient weights, which exploit sufficient statistics and a sparsity assumption to construct weights that are independent of the p-values being tested. Applying these weights within weighted versions of Holm's procedure and the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure yields substantially greater statistical power than the unweighted counterparts when the true coefficient vector is sparse, while preserving the exact or highly robust error control guarantees of those procedures regardless of whether sparsity actually holds. The approach is validated across a broad range of simulation settings and an application to HIV drug resistance data, where it outperforms both unweighted analogues and other competing methods.
items.citation: Souhardya Sengupta, Lucas Janson. Co-sufficient weighting: leveraging sparsity for more powerful variable selection in the linear model. arXiv. 2026

items.title: System-Level Factors Influencing AGC Cyber-Attack Success and RAS Vulnerability in Multi-Area Grids
items.summary: This paper investigates how coordinated cyberattacks on automatic generation control systems can destabilize grid frequency in multi-area power grids while evading remedial action schemes designed to protect against such events. The researchers developed a feedback-based attack policy to manipulate AGC signals and drive system frequency into unsafe ranges, then conducted a massive parametric sweep across millions of scenarios varying factors such as inertia distribution, AGC capacity, tie-line loading, load damping, and update rate. A decision tree classifier was applied to this large scenario dataset to extract interpretable guidelines distinguishing conditions under which attacks succeed from those where they fail. The resulting vulnerability criteria were validated on a three-area test system using detailed phasor-domain simulations incorporating turbine-governor dynamics and frequency-triggered load and generation shedding. The findings demonstrate that particular combinations of AGC capacity relative to tie-line transfer limits, inertia imbalance between areas, and pre-attack tie-line loading levels are the dominant factors that increase attack success, providing grid operators with actionable criteria for identifying and potentially mitigating vulnerable operating conditions.
items.citation: Abdulmannan Ajabnoor, Zhi Jin Zhang, Maryam Saeedifard et al.. System-Level Factors Influencing AGC Cyber-Attack Success and RAS Vulnerability in Multi-Area Grids. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice
items.summary: This paper investigates whether large language models provide consistent smoking-cessation advice regardless of who is asking, auditing six widely deployed models across twelve user personas that vary in life stage, expertise, and smoking history. The researchers posed the same four cessation questions to each persona combination, generating thousands of responses that were then analyzed for content differences. They found substantial persona-dependent variation across all models, most notably that FDA-approved prescription medications were mentioned far less frequently to teen personas than adult personas, and that personas presenting healthcare expertise paradoxically received fewer factual details than lay personas. The study also tested a system-prompt intervention designed to establish a minimum factual floor for all users, finding it reduced persona-based disparities but with effects that varied enough across models to preclude assuming transferability between systems. The authors caution that equal response rates are not always the appropriate clinical standard, since some persona-specific adaptation is clinically defensible, and call for age-aware rather than uniform consistency requirements.
items.citation: Artin Yousefi, Aizierjiang Aiersilan, Lorien C Abroms et al.. Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Shock Loading Accesses Reaction Pathways beyond Accelerated Thermolysis
items.summary: This paper investigated whether shock loading and thermolysis in energetic materials follow the same chemical reaction pathways or merely differ in rate. The researchers developed a reactive machine-learning interatomic potential capable of simulating both thermolysis and shock-induced decomposition across a broad range of carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, and oxygen containing energetic materials on a common energy surface. By comparing the two processes at equivalent stages of reaction progress, they found that chemical states and local structural environments diverge substantially as reactions advance, with the majority of shock-induced local environments falling outside the reference domain established by thermolysis. Structural and reaction-network analyses revealed that shock loading accesses additional association and rearrangement pathways and promotes greater intermolecular reorganization compared to thermolysis, even though the earliest decomposition steps are partially shared. The central conclusion is that mechanical loading history fundamentally shapes the reaction pathways accessed during decomposition, rather than simply accelerating the same chemistry that occurs during heating.
items.citation: Mingjie Wen, Jiahe Han, Zihan Zhou et al.. Shock Loading Accesses Reaction Pathways beyond Accelerated Thermolysis. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Existence of the thermodynamic limit for the Hopfield model
items.summary: This paper addresses a foundational question in the statistical mechanics of associative memory networks by proving that the quenched pressure of the Hopfield model possesses a well-defined thermodynamic limit. The model considered stores a number of random binary patterns scaling linearly with system size, and the result holds at any finite load, inverse temperature, and uniform external field without requiring replica symmetry, order-parameter concentration, or non-condensation assumptions. The proof strategy uses a Hubbard–Stratonovich transformation to isolate the few patterns with large hidden coordinates, replaces the remaining binary patterns with Gaussian ones via a collective interpolation incurring only a small, volume-uniform error, and controls the disorder-dependent pattern selection through convex concentration on the discrete cube. For the resulting mixed models, the authors establish a Gaussian hidden-spin truncation bound uniform in volume and Ising potential, then reduce convergence to existing results on non-convex vector spin glasses with compact spins, also showing that the pressure converges almost surely with exponentially small deviations and that thermodynamic quantities such as internal energy and entropy converge wherever the limiting pressure is differentiable. The paper additionally establishes ordering relations between pressures for different pattern distributions and notes that the proofs were developed through extensive interaction with large language models under the authors' guidance.
items.citation: Adriano Barra, Fabrizio Durante. Existence of the thermodynamic limit for the Hopfield model. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Multimodal Type 2 Diabetes Registry on DHIS2: A Design and Feasibility Study with the AI-READI Dataset
items.summary: This paper investigated whether DHIS2, a widely deployed open-source health information system, can serve as a multimodal registry for type 2 diabetes by storing diverse data types — including continuous glucose monitor readings, wearables, home sensors, clinical records, and retinal images — for the same individuals. The researchers designed a registry consisting of dozens of program stages and hundreds of data elements, then loaded a large publicly available diabetes dataset into the system and verified the stored values against source files. Because DHIS2's row-per-event data model cannot accommodate raw high-frequency sensor streams, the team stored dense wearable and glucose data as hourly summaries, which substantially reduced data volume, while retinal images and discrete clinical records were stored one event per record. Verification of tens of millions of stored values revealed only a small number of defects, all involving missing, duplicated, or artifactual records rather than incorrect values, and these were resolved upon repair; an independent recomputation of glucose summaries confirmed full agreement. The paper concludes that an unmodified DHIS2 Tracker can represent multimodal diabetes data and offers practical implementation lessons, while acknowledging that clinical use, analytics at scale, and live device integration remain to be demonstrated.
items.citation: Saptarshi Purkayastha, Aiswarya Nandan Perumbilly, Zhenan Yin et al.. A Multimodal Type 2 Diabetes Registry on DHIS2: A Design and Feasibility Study with the AI-READI Dataset. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Evaluating long-term programmatic outcomes of patients with advanced HIV disease: Insights from 12 years of antiretroviral therapy scale-up in rural KwaZulu-Natal.
