items.summary: This study examined long-term treatment outcomes among people with advanced HIV disease initiating antiretroviral therapy in rural KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, a setting with high HIV prevalence and limited longitudinal programmatic data. Using a retrospective cohort design drawing on routine data from public health facilities over a twelve-year period, researchers assessed retention in care and virological suppression at multiple time points, as well as factors associated with loss to follow-up and viral load outcomes. Retention in care was high across all follow-up intervals, and virological suppression exceeded eighty-three percent among those with available viral load data, with outcomes improving notably under the Universal Test and Treat era compared to earlier treatment periods. However, viral load testing completion declined substantially over time, leaving a meaningful gap in achieving fully undetectable viral loads across the cohort. Men and individuals with very low CD4 counts faced greater risk of loss to follow-up, while women and those initiating treatment rapidly were more likely to achieve virological suppression, pointing to the need for targeted male-focused interventions and earlier treatment initiation to further close outcome gaps.
items.citation: Kitenge MK, Fatti G, Laxmeshwar C et al.. Evaluating long-term programmatic outcomes of patients with advanced HIV disease: Insights from 12 years of antiretroviral therapy scale-up in rural KwaZulu-Natal.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: An Evaluation of Perinatal Human Immunodeficiency Virus Transmissions in New York State, 2007-2020.
items.summary: This population-based retrospective cohort study examined predictors of perinatal HIV transmission and unsuppressed viral load near delivery among birthing parent–infant dyads in New York State over a roughly fourteen-year period. Researchers linked data from state health surveillance systems and medical record abstraction to build multivariable models identifying factors associated with both transmission and viral non-suppression. The overall rate of perinatal HIV transmission was very low, yet having an unsuppressed viral load at the test closest to delivery was by far the strongest predictor of transmission. Key drivers of unsuppressed viral load included illicit substance use during pregnancy, not using antiretroviral therapy during pregnancy, and later initiation of prenatal care. The findings highlight that while perinatal transmission has become rare, targeting viral suppression through early prenatal engagement and antiretroviral use remains essential to eliminating the remaining cases.
items.citation: Swain CA, Wong C, Stolz A et al.. An Evaluation of Perinatal Human Immunodeficiency Virus Transmissions in New York State, 2007-2020.. O&G open. 2026

items.title: Testing for Recent HIV Infections: A Conceptual Review.
items.summary: This review examined the development, validation, and application of HIV recency assays, which are laboratory-based or point-of-care tests designed to distinguish recent from long-standing HIV infection for the purpose of estimating HIV incidence in cross-sectional studies. The authors conducted a narrative synthesis drawing on foundational methodological papers, validation studies, international technical guidance, and programmatic evaluations to trace the evolution of these tools across four generations, from early detuned enzyme immunoassays through avidity-based assays, rapid point-of-care tests, and emerging genomic approaches. Performance of these assays is governed primarily by two metrics—mean duration of recent infection and false-recent rate—both of which are influenced by viral subtype, antiretroviral therapy exposure, and host factors. The review found that recency assays are now applied across national surveys, routine testing services, key-population surveillance, and outbreak detection, but are hampered by biological variability, misclassification related to treatment, and operational and ethical challenges. The authors conclude that the future utility of these tools depends on improved assay design, integration with genomic and programmatic data, real-time surveillance infrastructure, and sustained attention to ethical safeguards and community engagement.
items.citation: Suligoi B, Galli C. Testing for Recent HIV Infections: A Conceptual Review.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: A Multistate Analysis of Longitudinal Care Outcomes Among People Newly Linked to Human Immunodeficiency Virus Care in Missouri.
items.summary: This study examined longitudinal patterns of HIV care engagement and viral suppression among people newly linked to HIV care in St. Louis, Missouri, a priority state for the Ending the HIV Epidemic initiative. Using multistate analytic methods, researchers tracked patients over three years following clinic linkage, categorizing them across nine mutually exclusive states defined by clinic engagement and viral load status. The analysis revealed that by one year after linkage, roughly half of patients were continuously retained while nearly a third had disengaged, and viral suppression was substantially lower among reengaged individuals compared to those continuously retained. Younger individuals and those from historically marginalized communities faced greater risks of disengagement, reengagement, and viremia. The authors conclude that longitudinal multistate methods expose clinically important gaps obscured by routine cross-sectional reporting, and that HIV care programs should prioritize sustaining long-term engagement rather than focusing narrowly on preventing isolated missed appointments.
items.citation: Ramakrishnan A, Vo D, Barrette EP et al.. A Multistate Analysis of Longitudinal Care Outcomes Among People Newly Linked to Human Immunodeficiency Virus Care in Missouri.. Open forum infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: A qualitative study exploring factors associated with the accuracy of recording malaria rapid diagnostic test results in two high-burden regions of Côte d'Ivoire.
items.summary: This study investigated why healthcare workers in two high-burden regions of Côte d'Ivoire sometimes fail to accurately record malaria rapid diagnostic test results, a problem that undermines malaria surveillance. Using a qualitative approach embedded within a broader mixed-methods evaluation, researchers photographed RDTs performed by healthcare workers and had an independent panel read them, then conducted semi-structured interviews with workers showing high versus low agreement between their recorded and independently verified results. The primary factor distinguishing the two groups was not knowledge gaps or resource constraints but rather differing levels of confidence in negative RDT results, particularly fear that a negative result in a symptomatic patient could lead to severe harm if antimalarials were withheld. Workers with low recording accuracy more often reported deliberately falsifying registers—changing negative results to positive or omitting antimalarial prescriptions—to align documentation with treatment decisions made despite negative results. The authors conclude that interventions should focus on building clinical decision-making confidence for RDT-negative fevers, expanding non-malarial diagnostic options, and redesigning documentation systems to allow transparent recording of non-adherence without creating incentives for misreporting.
items.citation: Kouakou OMA, Bédia-Tanoh VA, Arnzen A et al.. A qualitative study exploring factors associated with the accuracy of recording malaria rapid diagnostic test results in two high-burden regions of Côte d'Ivoire.. Malaria journal. 2026

items.title: Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multi-antigen rapid diagnostic test for malaria in a region of southern Ethiopia where both *Plasmodium falciparum* and *Plasmodium vivax* co-circulate, and where limitations such as low parasite density and gene deletions can compromise conventional testing. Researchers enrolled febrile patients at health facilities during peak transmission season and compared the new Bioline Malaria multi-antigen RDT, which detects HRP2 alongside dual pLDH markers for both species, against expert microscopy and quantitative PCR as reference standards. The multi-antigen RDT showed high specificity and strong agreement with microscopy, but its sensitivity declined notably when qPCR served as the reference, indicating that submicroscopic and low-density infections were frequently missed. The findings confirm the clinical utility of the multi-antigen RDT for routine case management but underscore its limitations for detecting the full burden of infection in an endemic setting. The authors conclude that more sensitive diagnostic approaches are needed to support malaria surveillance and control efforts in such co-endemic environments.
items.citation: Bogale A, Mitiku A, Tefera S et al.. Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.. Scientific reports. 2026

items.title: The spatial proteome of the Plasmodium falciparum schizont illuminates the composition and evolutionary trajectories of its organelles
items.summary: This paper investigated the spatial organization of proteins within the malaria parasite *Plasmodium falciparum* during its invasive erythrocytic stage, aiming to resolve the cellular locations of a large fraction of the parasite proteome that had previously been functionally and spatially uncharacterized. The researchers applied a high-resolution spatial proteomics approach called hyperLOPIT, combined with supervised machine learning, to map the subcellular localization of thousands of proteins expressed in late schizont stages. The resulting dataset resolved dozens of distinct cellular compartments, including sites within the infected host cell, and assigned a substantial portion of the detected proteome to specific organelles or niches. By integrating these spatial data with comparative genomic analyses, the study illuminated the evolutionary trajectories of *Plasmodium* organelles and revealed patterns of adaptive evolution relevant to understanding how the parasite responds to ongoing selective pressures, including those posed by disease management efforts.
items.citation: Scott A. Chisholm, Victor Flores, Alison Kemp et al.. The spatial proteome of the Plasmodium falciparum schizont illuminates the composition and evolutionary trajectories of its organelles. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Real‐world comprehensive care of people living with schizophrenia: recommendations across different settings and clinical stages
items.summary: This paper addressed the global challenge of managing schizophrenia by developing the first comprehensive, real-world care recommendations spanning diverse clinical stages, resource settings, and geographic contexts. The authors conducted a critical review of scientific literature combined with collaborative input from clinical academics treating people with schizophrenia worldwide, including those in the Global South, as well as experts by experience. The resulting recommendations cover a broad spectrum of care components, including early detection, measurement-based monitoring, pharmacological and psychological treatments, psychosocial interventions, community and inpatient care, peer support, and population-level prevention. A central overarching recommendation is to implement evidence-based, culturally sensitive care that reduces disparities between high- and low-resource settings through early intervention, task-sharing models involving non-professional workers and traditional healers, and scalable digital solutions. The authors conclude that meaningful progress requires strengthened mental health funding, improved access to care, and systematic attention to the social determinants of health across all settings.
items.citation: Paolo Fusar‐Poli, Toby Pillinger, Robert Ali McCutcheon et al.. Real‐world comprehensive care of people living with schizophrenia: recommendations across different settings and clinical stages. World Psychiatry. 2026

items.title: ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
items.summary: These guidelines address the growing challenge of managing infection risk in patients with inflammatory bowel disease who are treated with increasingly potent immunosuppressive and biologic therapies. The guidelines were developed by a European professional organization to update previous consensus documents in light of the rapid expansion of available treatments, including newer small molecules and advanced biologics, each carrying distinct infection risk profiles. The document provides structured, evidence-based recommendations covering risk stratification and the prevention, diagnosis, and management of viral, bacterial, mycobacterial, and vaccine-preventable infections in this immunocompromised population. A central emphasis is placed on preventative strategies tailored to the contemporary therapeutic landscape, recognizing that opportunistic infections pose significant morbidity and mortality risks when immune modulation is profound. The update reflects the imperative to equip clinicians with current guidance as treatment paradigms for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis continue to evolve.
items.venue: Journal of Crohn s and Colitis
items.citation: Henit A. Yanai, Pierre Ellul, Bram Verstockt et al.. ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease. Journal of Crohn s and Colitis. 2026

items.title: Clinical profile and genomic characterization of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus index case in Uganda
items.summary: This paper reports on Uganda's index case of Bundibugyo virus disease identified in 2026, describing the clinical course and genomic characteristics of the causative pathogen. The patient, who had traveled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, presented with prolonged gastrointestinal symptoms and rapidly deteriorated with multiorgan failure before dying within days of hospital admission. Posthumous testing confirmed orthoebolavirus RNA, and whole-genome sequencing revealed that the 2026 strain constitutes a distinct viral lineage with roughly equal genetic distance from two previously described variants, exhibiting approximately one percent sequence divergence from those earlier strains. The authors highlight how fatality surveillance, private-sector health facility engagement, national specimen referral networks, and rapid genomic diagnostics collectively enabled pathogen identification and public health response. The case underscores the ongoing risk of cross-border Bundibugyo virus transmission in the region and the challenges posed by nonspecific early symptoms in recognizing high-consequence infections promptly.
items.citation: Andrew Nsawotebba, Isaac Ssewanyana, Alisen Ayitewala et al.. Clinical profile and genomic characterization of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus index case in Uganda. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments
items.summary: This paper investigates intrinsic alignments of galaxies, which pose systematic uncertainties for weak gravitational lensing measurements and probe galaxy formation physics. The authors conducted model-agnostic tests to examine how density-weighting affects intrinsic alignment signals, and to evaluate whether the tidal alignment paradigm accurately describes galaxy orientations, using both the IllustrisTNG cosmological hydrodynamical simulation and observational data from SDSS-III. They found that density-weighting primarily amplifies alignment signals at large scales, while its effect at small scales depends on the specific galaxy sample. Additionally, using two-point correlation functions of galaxy shapes and tidal fields, they found that central galaxies align linearly with the underlying tidal field even deep into the one-halo regime, suggesting the tidal alignment framework remains a valid description well into nonlinear scales.
items.citation: Paul Rogozenski, Sukhdeep Singh, Jonathan Blazek et al.. Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary: This paper investigates why Unified Multimodal Models struggle to effectively apply chain-of-thought reasoning to image generation, identifying the core problem as a modality mismatch between discrete token-space reasoning and continuous image generation spaces. To address this, the authors propose LARC (Latent Reasoning in Continuous space), a framework that performs reasoning directly over continuous hidden states rather than discrete tokens. The training approach proceeds in two stages: a curriculum supervised fine-tuning stage that gradually transitions token-level reasoning into latent reasoning, followed by an information-gain reinforcement learning stage that allows the model to self-improve without ground truth supervision. Evaluated across multiple text-to-image generation benchmarks, LARC improves generation quality, prompt following, and compositional fidelity, achieving state-of-the-art performance with a notable gain over a strong baseline. Importantly, the framework also recovers test-time scaling behavior, outperforming token-based generation under both parallel and sequential scaling strategies.
items.citation: Byungwoo Jeon, Yoonwoo Jeong, Hyunseok Lee et al.. Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently running decision models—a class of lightweight language model systems designed for rapid categorical reasoning in agent pipelines—on existing inference infrastructure. The authors identify that current generation-oriented inference engines struggle with these workloads, either incurring excessive prefix recomputation costs or introducing distortions in output probabilities. To solve this, they developed Flide, an inference engine that separates the logical tree structure of decision requests from their physical execution within a single flattened token stream, using a mechanism called ForkAttention to navigate branching dependencies via GPU-resident indices across both standard attention and recurrent network layers. This design guarantees that each query branch produces results arithmetically identical to an isolated forward pass, while accommodating varied request mixtures through compact pre-recorded execution graphs. Evaluations on hybrid and decision models show that Flide achieves substantially faster query answering than existing engines while maintaining the closest fidelity to a high-precision numerical reference.

items.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of long-horizon planning for embodied agents, where cumulative errors and search complexity degrade performance in world model-based approaches. The approach was evaluated across navigation and manipulation benchmarks, yielding substantial performance improvements over both state-of-the-art policy and diffusion-based planners and over single-level world model model-predictive control, with the largest gains observed on complex, previously unseen configurations.
items.citation: Gaoyue Zhou, Yvonne Wu, Zichen Jeff Cui et al.. Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Approximate Polynomial Satisfiability and Integral Closure Membership in the Counting Hierarchy
items.summary: This paper studies the computational complexity of two algebraic problems: approximate polynomial satisfiability (APS), which asks whether a polynomial system is nearly satisfiable in a suitable sense, and integral closure membership, which asks whether a polynomial is integral over a given polynomial ring. Their approach combines classical algebraic geometry tools—specifically Noether normalization and a geometric restriction on how points in the image of a polynomial map approach the origin—to reduce APS to a decision problem on multivariate resultants, which is then solvable within the Counting Hierarchy. Additionally, they place integral closure membership testing in the Counting Hierarchy by using a global annihilator criterion and an effective degree bound to reduce non-integrality to APS in polynomial time. These results have implications for geometric complexity theory, as APS was previously used to construct hitting sets for the closure of the algebraic complexity class VP.

items.title: Instance-dependent sequential limits as an exact information ledger
items.summary: This paper studies the theoretical foundations of instance-dependent lower bounds that arise across several sequential decision-making problems, including bandit regret, sequential hypothesis testing, best-arm identification, and Markov decision processes. The authors unify these bounds through a single analytical chain that connects divergence decompositions, data processing inequalities, sufficient statistics, and optimization over alternative instances and allocation strategies. A key contribution is expressing this chain as an exact "ledger" that tracks precisely where information is lost at each step, showing for instance that data processing loses exactly a conditional divergence that vanishes for natural exponential family reward distributions when conditioning on per-arm counts and reward sums. Applying the ledger to seven published empirical datasets, the authors find that the dominant gap between standard algorithms and classical limits is most often attributable to the uniform quantification step, particularly in model selection and Wald's sequential test settings.
items.citation: Akshay Balsubramani. Instance-dependent sequential limits as an exact information ledger. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic performance and testing costs of pooled testing for molecular detection of tuberculosis in seven countries: a prospective, observational, diagnostic accuracy study.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether pooling multiple sputum specimens together for molecular tuberculosis testing could expand diagnostic access without requiring additional laboratory infrastructure. Conducted prospectively across seven countries spanning multiple continents, the study enrolled individuals with presumptive tuberculosis through both facility-based and community-based case finding, testing sputum specimens individually and in pools of two, three, or four samples using Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, with culture serving as the reference standard. Pooled testing demonstrated slightly higher specificity but modestly lower sensitivity compared to individual testing, with the performance gap most pronounced for specimens yielding very low or trace-level results on individual testing. Crucially, pooling reduced cartridge consumption by approximately half compared to individual testing, representing a substantial resource saving. The authors conclude that pooled tuberculosis testing is a viable strategy to expand access to WHO-recommended molecular diagnostics in low-to-moderate positivity settings without requiring new infrastructure investment.
items.citation: Garg T, Sander M, Byrne RL et al.. Diagnostic performance and testing costs of pooled testing for molecular detection of tuberculosis in seven countries: a prospective, observational, diagnostic accuracy study.. The Lancet. Global health. 2027

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviews advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research from 2020 to 2025, synthesizing evidence that has informed updated WHO policy guidance consolidating recommendations for tuberculosis disease detection and drug-resistance testing into a single framework. Key developments include the expanded role of digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection as a screening and triage tool, and the diversified deployment of decentralised molecular diagnostics such as low-complexity automated and manual nucleic acid amplification tests across a wider range of specimen types, including stool, gastric aspirate, nasopharyngeal samples, and tongue swabs, improving bacteriological confirmation particularly in children. Rapid molecular drug-resistance testing has been strengthened, and targeted next-generation sequencing is now endorsed for comprehensive drug-susceptibility testing at reference laboratory level, while urine lipoarabinomannan assays offer diagnostic benefit primarily in people with HIV and advanced disease. Host blood transcriptomic and other biomarker signatures show promise for prognosis and triage, but no biomarker has yet met WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis. The paper concludes that substantial gaps in performance, implementation, and equity remain and identifies these as developmental priorities.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: Diagnosis of Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis at the Interface of Pathogen Detection and Host Response: Molecular, Microbiological, and Histopathological Advances.
items.summary: This review examines the persistent diagnostic challenges posed by extrapulmonary tuberculosis, which disproportionately affects children and immunocompromised individuals and is complicated by low bacterial burden, anatomically diverse disease sites, and nonspecific clinical presentations. The authors synthesize evidence across microbiological, molecular, sequencing-based, and histopathological approaches, situating them within the context of site-specific immunopathology including granuloma biology and caseous necrosis. Comparative analysis spans multiple anatomical forms of the disease, evaluating tools such as Xpert MTB/RIF and Ultra, targeted and metagenomic next-generation sequencing, emerging host-response biomarkers, and artificial intelligence-assisted histopathology. The review proposes pragmatic, tiered diagnostic algorithms tailored to resource-limited settings where most cases occur, and identifies gaps in current international guidance. The authors conclude that aligning diagnostic modality selection with anatomical site, specimen quality, pathological subtype, and available laboratory capacity has the potential to reduce time to diagnosis and support host-directed diagnostic strategies.
items.citation: Liu Q, Jiang Y. Diagnosis of Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis at the Interface of Pathogen Detection and Host Response: Molecular, Microbiological, and Histopathological Advances.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.
items.summary: This narrative review examines how the diagnosis of HIV-associated tuberculosis has evolved from the early antiretroviral therapy era to the present day. The authors trace the limitations of historical diagnostic approaches, particularly smear microscopy, which has reduced sensitivity in people with HIV due to lower bacillary loads, frequent extrapulmonary disease, and nonspecific clinical presentations that overlap with other opportunistic infections. The review describes how the introduction of nucleic acid amplification tests and the urine lipoarabinomannan lateral flow assay, alongside widespread antiretroviral therapy use, has substantially transformed the diagnostic landscape and contributed to reductions in tuberculosis incidence and mortality. Despite these advances, no currently available rapid test achieves ideal sensitivity, and only urine lipoarabinomannan detection combines affordability with point-of-care suitability. The authors conclude that further development of accurate, affordable, and simple point-of-care diagnostics remains an urgent priority.
items.venue: South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde
items.citation: Maartens G. The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.. South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde. 2026

items.title: Mycobacteriophages: An Integrated Platform for Rapid Diagnosis and Targeted Therapy of Tuberculosis Infection.
items.summary: This paper developed and evaluated a dual-purpose platform based on the lytic mycobacteriophage D29 to address the growing challenge of multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis. The platform combines a rapid diagnostic module using multiplex real-time PCR to detect phage replication in drug-resistant mycobacterial isolates, enabling phenotypic drug susceptibility testing across multiple antibiotics within five days, alongside a liposomal therapeutic formulation designed to deliver the phage directly to the site of pulmonary infection. In a mouse model of experimental pulmonary tuberculosis, both aerosol and intranasal delivery of liposomal D29 significantly reduced bacterial burden in the lungs compared to untreated controls, with aerosol administration showing a trend toward superior efficacy. Pharmacokinetic studies demonstrated exclusive lung tropism, rapid peak concentrations following administration, and evidence of preferential in vivo phage replication in infected compared to uninfected lungs, while safety assessments revealed no significant toxicity or immunogenicity. The authors conclude that this integrated diagnostic-therapeutic platform offers a clinically promising, personalized medicine approach covering the full cycle from rapid drug susceptibility profiling to targeted phage therapy for tuberculosis.
items.citation: Avdeev VV, Vladimirsky MA, Eliseev PI et al.. Mycobacteriophages: An Integrated Platform for Rapid Diagnosis and Targeted Therapy of Tuberculosis Infection.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of performing differential expression analysis on large-scale single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomics datasets spanning hundreds of subjects and millions of cells. The authors developed an open-source R package called dreamlet, which employs a pseudobulk approach combined with precision-weighted linear mixed models to identify differentially expressed genes associated with traits across subjects for each cell cluster. The method is designed to handle complex statistical models while controlling false positive rates, and it achieves substantially faster computation with reduced memory requirements compared to existing workflows. The authors validated dreamlet's computational and statistical performance on previously published datasets and demonstrated its capabilities on a novel dataset of over a million single nuclei from postmortem brain tissue of Alzheimer's disease cases and controls. Overall, the work presents dreamlet as a scalable and statistically rigorous solution for differential expression analysis in large cohort-scale single-cell studies.
items.citation: Gabriel E. Hoffman, Donghoon Lee, Jaroslav M. Bendl et al.. Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Synthesis and multilevel evaluation of benzimidazole-based anticancer compounds: DNA/serum albumin interaction, and in-depth theoretical insights
items.summary: Two novel benzimidazole-based compounds were synthesized and evaluated for their potential as anticancer agents against multiple cancer cell lines, including lung, breast, and liver cancer, alongside a healthy kidney cell line as a control. One compound demonstrated particularly potent cytotoxic activity against liver and breast cancer cell lines, and mechanistic investigations revealed that both compounds shifted gene expression toward apoptosis by downregulating anti-apoptotic genes while upregulating pro-apoptotic ones, alongside elevating oxidative stress markers and inducing cellular senescence. Fluorescence spectroscopy showed that both compounds bind strongly to DNA via an intercalative mechanism, with the more active compound exhibiting a higher binding constant, while moderate binding to serum albumin suggested favorable transport properties without excessive nonspecific protein interactions. Computational analyses including density functional theory calculations and molecular docking supported the experimental observations regarding compound reactivity and binding behavior. Taken together, these findings identify the synthesized benzimidazole derivatives as promising candidates for further development as anticancer therapeutics.
items.citation: Sevgi Kundu, Senem Akkoç, Yalçın Erzurumlu et al.. Synthesis and multilevel evaluation of benzimidazole-based anticancer compounds: DNA/serum albumin interaction, and in-depth theoretical insights. Molecular and Cellular Biochemistry. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic review examined how different forms of exercise influence the expression of Toll-like receptors, a family of immune cell receptors that trigger inflammatory signalling when activated, and whose dysregulation has been linked to sedentary behaviour and chronic non-communicable diseases. The authors searched multiple major databases for human studies in which exercise was the sole intervention, ultimately including a substantial body of literature spanning acute and chronic resistance, aerobic, and combined exercise modalities. Key patterns emerged across categories: acute resistance exercise tended to upregulate TLR expression, while acute aerobic exercise more often produced neutral or downregulatory effects, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined training programs generally left TLR levels unchanged or reduced them, whereas chronic aerobic training yielded mixed results with the majority of measurements showing no significant change. The authors conclude that exercise modality and characteristics shape TLR responses in meaningful ways, but caution that high heterogeneity in study designs limits firm conclusions and that further mechanistically focused research is needed.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Flooding spread of manipulated knowledge in LLM-based multi-agent communities
items.summary: This paper investigates security vulnerabilities in large language model-based multi-agent systems, specifically focusing on how manipulated knowledge can spread through communities of interacting agents. The researchers designed a two-stage attack methodology combining Persuasiveness Injection and Manipulated Knowledge Injection, which causes agents to propagate both counterfactual and toxic information during communication without relying on explicit adversarial prompt attacks and without visibly degrading the agents' general capabilities. Experiments demonstrated that the manipulated knowledge persists even through retrieval-augmented generation frameworks, where agents store and later retrieve corrupted conversation histories for future use. To counter these threats, the authors proposed two defense strategies involving specially designed system prompts that encourage critical verification of shared knowledge and the incorporation of supervisory agents to monitor interactions, both of which meaningfully reduced the rate at which manipulated knowledge spread. The work calls attention to the urgency of adopting targeted, cost-effective defenses in platforms built on multi-agent systems.
items.citation: Tianjie Ju, Yiting Wang, Yi Hua et al.. Flooding spread of manipulated knowledge in LLM-based multi-agent communities. Science China Information Sciences. 2026

items.title: Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments
items.summary: This paper investigates the intrinsic alignments of galaxies, which introduce systematic uncertainties in weak gravitational lensing and probe galaxy formation physics. The authors developed model-agnostic tests to examine how density-weighting affects intrinsic alignment signals, using both the IllustrisTNG cosmological hydrodynamical simulation and observational data from the BOSS survey. They found that density-weighting primarily amplifies alignment signals at large scales, while its effects at small scales depend on the particular galaxy sample being studied. Additionally, by correlating galaxy shapes with tidal fields through two-point statistics, the authors assessed how well the tidal alignment paradigm describes galaxy orientations in IllustrisTNG, finding that central galaxies align linearly with the underlying non-linear tidal field even deep within the one-halo regime. These results provide important model-independent constraints on the physical drivers of intrinsic alignments and have implications for how they are modeled in weak lensing analyses.
items.citation: Paul Rogozenski, Sukhdeep Singh, Jonathan Blazek et al.. Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary: This paper investigates how to improve reasoning capabilities within Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs), specifically addressing the challenge of applying chain-of-thought reasoning to image generation tasks. The authors identify a fundamental modality mismatch as the root cause of failure: reasoning typically occurs in discrete token space while image generation operates in continuous space. To resolve this, they propose LARC (Latent Reasoning in Continuous space), a framework that performs reasoning directly over continuous hidden states rather than discrete tokens, trained through a two-stage process combining curriculum supervised fine-tuning and information-gain reinforcement learning. Evaluated across multiple text-to-image generation benchmarks, LARC demonstrates consistent improvements in generation quality, prompt following, and compositional fidelity, achieving state-of-the-art results and exhibiting test-time scaling behavior superior to token-based approaches under both parallel and sequential scaling strategies.
items.citation: Byungwoo Jeon, Yoonwoo Jeong, Hyunseok Lee et al.. Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently running decision models—a class of lightweight language model systems designed for rapid categorical reasoning in AI agent pipelines—on existing inference infrastructure. Evaluations show Flide achieves substantially faster query answering than existing engines such as vLLM and SGLang while maintaining the closest match to a high-precision numerical reference, offering both throughput and mathematical exactness for latency-sensitive agent systems.
items.citation: Bobo Li, Jiajia Song, Hao Fei et al.. Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Current Data to Inform Point-of-Care Testing for Sexually Transmitted Infections in United States Healthcare Settings: A Narrative Review.
items.summary: This narrative review examined the current evidence base for point-of-care testing for sexually transmitted infections, including gonorrhea, chlamydia, trichomoniasis, and syphilis, across a range of United States healthcare settings. The authors reviewed literature from emergency departments, sexual health clinics, primary care and gynecology clinics, and urgent care centers, incorporating data from other high-income countries where domestic evidence was sparse, and stratified findings by clinical setting, priority patient groups, and sex. They found some evidence that point-of-care testing improves clinical outcomes, particularly for symptomatic women presenting to emergency departments, but noted that most studies failed to stratify results by priority population. A further limitation was that the majority of studies evaluated tests requiring ninety minutes or more to return results, meaning results often became available only after the clinical encounter had ended, reducing their actionability. The authors conclude that additional research is needed on faster tests, workflow strategies to ensure results are returned before patients leave, and updated cost-effectiveness analyses tailored to United States clinical contexts.
items.citation: Otsyina BE, Lorenz ZW, Widdice LE et al.. Current Data to Inform Point-of-Care Testing for Sexually Transmitted Infections in United States Healthcare Settings: A Narrative Review.. Sexually transmitted diseases. 2026

items.title: Interventions to Improve Care for Bacterial Sexually Transmitted Infections in Emergency Departments: A Narrative Review.
items.summary: This narrative review examined how emergency departments in the United States can better diagnose and treat bacterial sexually transmitted infections, specifically chlamydia, gonorrhea, and syphilis, given that these settings serve patients with limited access to routine sexual health care. The authors searched the published literature over several decades, identifying studies that evaluated interventions targeting testing, diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up within emergency department contexts. They found that universal screening substantially increased case detection, electronic health record prompts enhanced screening uptake, and point-of-care testing enabled same-day treatment while reducing unnecessary antibiotic use. Bundled interventions that addressed multiple steps across the care pathway appeared to produce the greatest overall impact, though variability among the interventions studied made direct comparisons challenging. The authors conclude that future research should prioritize implementation feasibility, sustainability, health equity, and cost-effectiveness across diverse emergency department settings.
items.citation: Andonian KS, Giri H, Goodman GR et al.. Interventions to Improve Care for Bacterial Sexually Transmitted Infections in Emergency Departments: A Narrative Review.. Sexually transmitted diseases. 2026

items.title: Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).
items.summary: This pilot study examined the utility of point-of-care testing for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis among men who have sex with men attending a non-governmental organisation-led clinic near Beirut, Lebanon, while also assessing their sexual health knowledge, attitudes, and practices. A cross-sectional design was used over four months, combining STI and HIV testing with an anonymous questionnaire covering demographics, condom use, chemsex, sexual violence, and perceived HIV-related stigma. The study found that high levels of STI and HIV awareness among participants coexisted with condomless sex and recreational drug use, and that stigma and community beliefs acted as significant barriers to testing-seeking behaviour. A notable proportion of participants were living with HIV, and point-of-care testing enabled same-day counselling and linkage to care for those with positive results. The authors conclude that integrating point-of-care testing into sexual health services is an effective approach for this population, facilitating rapid diagnosis and immediate support within a context of substantial HIV-related stigma.
items.citation: Abou Shahla W, Rossoni I, Padovese V. Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Mean-Field Limit of Non-exchangeable Multi-agent Systems Over Hypergraphs with Unbounded Rank
items.summary: This paper studies interacting particle systems where agents interact in groups rather than just pairwise, a setting naturally described by hypergraphs rather than ordinary graphs. The authors consider dense but nonuniform hypergraphs of unbounded rank, meaning the size of interacting groups is not fixed and can grow without bound. They derive the mean-field limit of such multi-agent systems as the population becomes large, proving rigorously that the limiting behavior is governed by a Vlasov-type equation. The hypergraph structure in this limit is encoded by a novel mathematical object called an unbounded-rank hypergraphon, and the resulting mean-field force incorporates infinitely many orders of interaction. This constitutes the first rigorous derivation of a mean-field limit for multi-agent systems on hypergraphs with unbounded rank, provided the interaction kernels satisfy sufficient regularity conditions.
items.citation: Nathalie Ayi, Nastassia Pouradier Duteil, David Poyato. Mean-Field Limit of Non-exchangeable Multi-agent Systems Over Hypergraphs with Unbounded Rank. Journal of Nonlinear Science. 2026

items.title: Flatline constructs : Gothic materialism and cybernetic theory-fiction
items.summary: This thesis examines cyberpunk fiction's relationship to postmodernism and late capitalism by reframing it through three interlocking conceptual lenses: cybernetics, the Gothic, and fiction. The central argument is that postmodernism has been preoccupied with cybernetic themes, that cybernetics has been persistently haunted by the Gothic, and that the Gothic maintains a uniquely intimate relationship with the fictional. Drawing primarily on Deleuze-Guattari's materialist reworking of the Gothic — derived from Worringer's concept of nonorganic continuum rather than from supernatural literary tradition — the thesis analyses key cyberpunk texts including Blade Runner, Videodrome, Neuromancer, and The Atrocity Exhibition as works fundamentally concerned with the collapse of the boundary between animate and inanimate. The study proposes the concept of the "flatline," borrowed from Gibson, to describe the convergence of Gothic and cybernetic concerns in cyberpunk, encompassing both a state of "unlife" or "undeath" and a condition of radical immanence. Across four chapters, the thesis pursues this concept through the flatlining of cybernetics and postmodernism, of the body, of reproduction, and of fiction itself, ultimately engaging Baudrillard's claim that the era of cybernetic simulation dissolves both science fiction and theory as distinct genres.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Mark Fisher. Flatline constructs : Gothic materialism and cybernetic theory-fiction. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: The many behind the few : the lives and emotions of Erks and WAAFs of RAF bomber command 1939-1945
items.summary: This thesis investigates the experiences of male and female ground personnel who served in RAF Bomber Command during the Second World War, a group that constituted the large majority of the service yet has been largely overlooked in favour of aircrew and strategic narratives. Drawing on a range of sources, the research examines how a gendered hierarchy of trades was constructed within Bomber Command through interacting discourses of class, gender, fear, heroism, and stoicism, alongside specific features of RAF institutional culture such as trade selection, pay scales, and dialect. The study explores how this hierarchy shaped individual experiences, leaving some personnel overstretched while others felt unable to contribute meaningfully, and it analyses the emotional lives of ground personnel who lived and worked within a community suffering high rates of aircrew loss. The thesis also addresses the RAF medical services' responses to psychological breakdown among ground personnel. By giving voice to this underrepresented group, the work contributes to broader histories of the RAF, military medicine and psychiatry, the emotional dimensions of wartime service, and understandings of work and citizenship on the home front.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Dan Ellin. The many behind the few : the lives and emotions of Erks and WAAFs of RAF bomber command 1939-1945. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update
items.summary: These guidelines address the ongoing burden of chronic hepatitis B infection in the Asia Pacific region, where the disease continues to drive significant morbidity and mortality through complications such as acute-on-chronic liver failure, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma despite decades of scientific progress. A regional task force comprising key opinion leaders was convened to synthesize current evidence while accounting for shifts in hepatitis B epidemiology, socioeconomic factors, and technological advances. The resulting clinical practice guidelines provide updated recommendations across thirteen major domains encompassing screening, vaccination, antiviral treatment, and hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance. The guidelines are intended to support healthcare professionals, policy-makers, and patients in making practical and cost-effective management decisions, with the overarching goal of reducing the disease burden attributable to chronic hepatitis B across the Asia Pacific region.
items.citation: Hong You, Rakhi Maiwall, Jing Chen et al.. APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update. Hepatology International. 2026

items.title: Girls, gifts, and gender : an ethnography of the materiality of care in rural Mpumalanga, South Africa
items.summary: This ethnographic thesis examined social relations of care involving young people in rural South Africa during the AIDS epidemic and a period of growing economic inequality, with a particular focus on how material exchanges shape care practices. Drawing on fieldwork conducted with non-profit organisations serving orphans and vulnerable children, participant households, and various stakeholders including government workers and tourist-philanthropists, the research analysed three distinct gift-exchange relationships: children's labour in exchange for guardian care, girls' labour and sexual favours exchanged for material support from males, and the local production of an "orphan" identity to attract charitable giving from tourist donors. The study developed the concept of the "materiality of care" to theorise how Western and local constructions of childhood, orphanhood, and care interact on the ground through orphan-targeted assistance programmes. The research found that understandings of care must be situated within both local cultural perspectives and the broader historical and political-economic context, and that the experiences of orphaned and non-orphaned children are shaped by overlapping conditions of poverty and AIDS rather than orphan status alone. The thesis contributes to critical scholarship on orphan-targeted interventions in sub-Saharan Africa, arguing that such interventions fail by overlooking the familial context of parentless children and the shared vulnerabilities of all young people affected by AIDS and poverty.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Annalise Weckesser. Girls, gifts, and gender : an ethnography of the materiality of care in rural Mpumalanga, South Africa. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: Hydrogels: current biomedical applications and future directions
items.summary: This review paper examines hydrogels as multifunctional biomedical materials, focusing on their design principles, engineering strategies, and therapeutic applications across a wide range of human diseases. The authors systematically cover structural construction and functional regulation concepts, including advances in polymer chemistry, crosslinking strategies, stimuli-responsive design, and fabrication technologies that have transformed hydrogels from simple soft materials into sophisticated biomedical systems. The review surveys current applications spanning drug delivery, tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, biosensing, diagnostic platforms, and organoid systems. Particular attention is given to hydrogel-based therapeutic strategies for conditions including wound healing, musculoskeletal repair, cancer, neurological and cardiovascular diseases, autoimmune disorders, and reproductive system diseases. The authors conclude by discussing the clinical translation prospects of hydrogels, arguing that their biocompatibility, tunability, and capacity to mimic extracellular matrix environments position them as promising solutions to limitations faced by conventional therapeutic approaches.
items.citation: Haoming Wu, Guanghao Piao, Qiuqi Chen et al.. Hydrogels: current biomedical applications and future directions. Molecular Biomedicine. 2026

items.title: Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments
items.summary: This paper investigates intrinsic alignments of galaxies, which represent both a systematic contaminant in weak gravitational lensing surveys and a probe of galaxy formation physics. The authors developed model-agnostic tests to examine how density-weighting affects intrinsic alignment signals, applying these tests to data from the IllustrisTNG cosmological hydrodynamical simulation and an observational galaxy survey. They found that density-weighting primarily amplifies the alignment signal at large scales, while its effect on small scales depends on the particular galaxy sample being studied. Additionally, by comparing two-point correlation functions of galaxy shapes with tidal fields, they assessed the validity of the tidal alignment framework and found that central galaxies align linearly with the underlying nonlinear tidal field even down into the one-halo regime.
items.citation: Paul Rogozenski, Sukhdeep Singh, Jonathan Blazek et al.. Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary: This paper investigates why Unified Multimodal Models struggle to effectively apply chain-of-thought reasoning to image generation, attributing the failure to a fundamental mismatch between discrete token-based reasoning and the continuous space in which image generation operates. To address this, the authors propose LARC (Latent Reasoning in Continuous space), a framework that shifts reasoning from discrete tokens to continuous hidden states. The training pipeline consists of two stages: a curriculum supervised fine-tuning stage that gradually transitions token-level reasoning into latent reasoning, followed by an information-gain reinforcement learning stage that refines latent reasoning without requiring ground-truth supervision. Evaluated across multiple text-to-image generation benchmarks, LARC improves generation quality, prompt following, and compositional fidelity, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the GenEval benchmark with a notable gain over a strong baseline. The framework also demonstrates test-time scaling behavior under both parallel and sequential strategies, a property previously absent in reasoning-augmented image generation models.
items.citation: Byungwoo Jeon, Yoonwoo Jeong, Hyunseok Lee et al.. Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of long-horizon planning for embodied agents using world models, where cumulative errors and search complexity degrade performance. The authors propose ID-WM (Implicit Dynamics World Models), a hierarchical framework that separates high-level state-space reachability from low-level control by using a high-level model to sample feasible transitions across the state manifold and a low-level inverse dynamics model to translate those transitions into precise actions. This decoupling allows the planner to identify reachable subgoals without being constrained by low-level execution details, enabling the synthesis of novel long-horizon plans from short behavioral segments that generalize beyond training distributions. The approach was evaluated across navigation and manipulation benchmarks, demonstrating substantial performance improvements over both state-of-the-art policy and diffusion-based planners, as well as over single-level world model model-predictive control, particularly in complex and previously unseen configurations.
items.citation: Gaoyue Zhou, Yvonne Wu, Zichen Jeff Cui et al.. Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Approximate Polynomial Satisfiability and Integral Closure Membership in the Counting Hierarchy
items.summary: This paper studies the computational complexity of two algebraic problems: approximate polynomial satisfiability (APS), which asks whether a system of polynomials is nearly satisfiable in a suitable sense, and integral closure membership, which asks whether a polynomial is integral over a given polynomial ring. The authors place APS for rational polynomials specified by arithmetic circuits into the Counting Hierarchy, improving the previously known upper bound of polynomial space. Their proof strategy combines Noether normalization with a geometric analysis of how points in the image of a polynomial map approach the origin, ultimately reducing APS to a question about multivariate resultants that can be decided within the Counting Hierarchy. Building on this result, they also place integral closure membership testing in the Counting Hierarchy by using a global annihilator criterion together with an effective degree bound to reduce non-integrality to APS in polynomial time. These results tighten complexity-theoretic understanding of fundamental algebraic decision problems and have implications for geometric complexity theory, where APS was previously used to construct hitting sets in polynomial space.
items.citation: Sanyam Agarwal, Archit Hari, Anurag Pandey et al.. Approximate Polynomial Satisfiability and Integral Closure Membership in the Counting Hierarchy. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Instance-dependent sequential limits as an exact information ledger
items.summary: This paper studies instance-dependent lower bounds that govern the difficulty of sequential decision-making problems, including bandit regret, sequential hypothesis testing, best-arm identification, and Markov decision processes. The authors unify the derivation of these classical limits through a single proof chain that proceeds from a divergence decomposition, through data processing inequalities, to a testing step and optimization over alternatives. A key contribution is casting this chain as an exact ledger, tracking precisely where information is lost at each step: the chain rule reveals that data processing loses exactly a conditional divergence, which vanishes for natural exponential family rewards at sufficient statistics, and a family of martingale identities extends the decomposition across all tilts between problem instances. Classical lower bounds then emerge as relaxations of this exact accounting, each with an explicitly named and computable defect. Applying the ledger to seven published empirical sources, the authors show that for best-arm identification among trained models and for Wald's sequential test, the dominant gap between standard algorithms and classical limits typically arises from the uniform quantification step.
items.citation: Akshay Balsubramani. Instance-dependent sequential limits as an exact information ledger. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Co-sufficient weighting: leveraging sparsity for more powerful variable selection in the linear model
items.summary: The paper addresses controlled variable selection in the Gaussian linear model, specifically seeking ways to improve statistical power without sacrificing error rate control. The authors develop a weighting scheme called co-sufficient weights, which are derived purely from the data's sufficient statistics and an assumption of sparsity, requiring no external side information and remaining independent of the p-values being weighted. These weights are then incorporated into weighted versions of established multiple testing procedures, including Holm's method and the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure. The approach provably retains the exact validity of Holm's procedure and the empirical validity of the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure regardless of whether the true signal is actually sparse, while delivering substantially greater power when sparsity does hold. Simulations across varied settings and an application to HIV drug resistance data demonstrate that the proposed weighted methods outperform their unweighted counterparts and other competing approaches.
items.citation: Souhardya Sengupta, Lucas Janson. Co-sufficient weighting: leveraging sparsity for more powerful variable selection in the linear model. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Clinical utility of nucleic acid amplification testing for detection of sexually transmitted infections in women with symptomatic bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis identified by conventional versus molecular diagnoses.
items.summary: This study examined whether using molecular nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) for bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis diagnosis improves the detection of co-occurring sexually transmitted infections compared to conventional diagnostic methods. Researchers analyzed a large cohort of women with symptomatic vaginitis, comparing STI NAAT positivity rates across three diagnostic approaches: clinician clinical assessment, conventional laboratory methods, and molecular vaginitis testing. Women with a positive molecular diagnosis of bacterial vaginosis had significantly higher rates of co-detected sexually transmitted infections—including *Trichomonas vaginalis*, *Chlamydia trachomatis*, *Neisseria gonorrhoeae*, and *Mycoplasma genitalium*—compared to those diagnosed by conventional or clinician-based methods, and a positive bacterial vaginosis NAAT result conferred significantly elevated relative risk for any STI. A similar trend was observed for vulvovaginal candidiasis, though the difference did not reach statistical significance. The authors conclude that an all-molecular testing strategy using a single specimen improves STI case-finding and risk stratification over traditional diagnostic approaches, supporting its adoption to streamline clinical workflows and guide comprehensive patient care.
items.citation: Getman D, Seña AC, Nenninger A et al.. Clinical utility of nucleic acid amplification testing for detection of sexually transmitted infections in women with symptomatic bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis identified by conventional versus molecular diagnoses.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: Pre-exposure prophylaxis adherence and risks of HIV and sexually transmitted infection among adult men before vs during the COVID-19 pandemic.
items.summary: This study examined how the COVID-19 pandemic affected pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) adherence, HIV incidence, and sexually transmitted infection rates among adult men who newly initiated PrEP. Using a retrospective cohort design drawing on a large commercial insurance claims database, the researchers applied group-based trajectory modeling and weighted regression approaches to compare outcomes between men who started PrEP before versus during the pandemic. They found that men initiating PrEP during the pandemic were more likely to fall into poorer adherence categories, particularly early discontinuation, compared to the pre-pandemic group, which showed higher rates of consistently high adherence. Pandemic-era initiation was associated with a meaningfully elevated risk of HIV acquisition, while STI rates were similar between the two groups. The authors conclude that disruptions to HIV prevention services during public health emergencies can have serious consequences for HIV risk, and that targeted strategies are needed to maintain continuity of PrEP access during such crises.
items.venue: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy
items.citation: Unigwe IF, Jenjai C, Goodin AJ et al.. Pre-exposure prophylaxis adherence and risks of HIV and sexually transmitted infection among adult men before vs during the COVID-19 pandemic.. Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy. 2026
