items.title: Next-generation CRISPR-based molecular diagnostics for veterinary parasitology: From laboratory innovation to one health surveillance.
items.summary: This review examines the application of CRISPR-based diagnostic technologies to the detection of veterinary parasites, addressing limitations of conventional methods such as poor sensitivity, low specificity, and dependence on centralized laboratory infrastructure. The authors critically survey how CRISPR systems utilizing Cas12, Cas13, and the emerging Cas14 proteins can be deployed to identify protozoan, helminthic, and arthropod-borne parasites in livestock, companion animals, and wildlife. The review describes how these platforms are enhanced through integration with isothermal amplification, lateral flow assays, fluorescence detection, and portable biosensors to produce rapid, field-deployable tools. Obstacles to broader adoption—including assay standardization, multiplexed detection, regulatory pathways, and commercialization—are discussed alongside future directions such as amplification-free formats and artificial intelligence-assisted interpretation. The authors conclude that CRISPR-based diagnostics hold substantial promise for transforming parasite surveillance within a One Health framework, linking veterinary, wildlife, and public health applications.
items.citation: Basit A, Hanif M. Next-generation CRISPR-based molecular diagnostics for veterinary parasitology: From laboratory innovation to one health surveillance.. Molecular and biochemical parasitology. 2026

items.title: Scaffold RNA Reengineering for a Leakage-Suppressed CRISPR/Cas12a Cascade System Toward Precise Nucleic Acid Diagnostics.
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of high background signal (leakage) in amplification-free CRISPR-based nucleic acid detection, which limits sensitivity and diagnostic precision. The researchers engineered the CRISPR RNA of the Cas12a system by adding a DNA extension to the scaffold RNA's 3' end, creating a conformational switch that introduces steric hindrance to keep the system in an inhibited state until a target nucleic acid triggers precise activation. This allosteric regulation mechanism was incorporated into a cascade-activatable architecture, termed CALCas, which amplifies signal upon target recognition while suppressing background noise inherent to other Cas cascade approaches. The system achieved femtomolar sensitivity and enabled rapid detection of HPV16 and HPV18 within thirty minutes without nucleic acid amplification. The study demonstrates that rationally reengineering guide RNA structure can reprogram Cas12a enzymatic activity, providing a generalizable strategy for highly sensitive and quantitative nucleic acid diagnostics.
items.citation: Li X, Hu H, Jiang X et al.. Scaffold RNA Reengineering for a Leakage-Suppressed CRISPR/Cas12a Cascade System Toward Precise Nucleic Acid Diagnostics.. Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany). 2026

items.title: Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.
items.summary: This review paper examines the current landscape of molecular diagnostic technologies applied to the detection and characterization of infectious disease pathogens. The paper covers nucleic acid amplification approaches, including polymerase chain reaction in its various forms (real-time, digital, and microfluidic), as well as isothermal amplification methods such as loop-mediated isothermal amplification and recombinase polymerase amplification, which are particularly suited to point-of-care settings due to their simplified temperature requirements. CRISPR-based detection systems are also discussed as an emerging approach frequently combined with isothermal amplification for identifying amplified nucleic acids. Next-generation sequencing is highlighted for its capacity to detect novel pathogens, diagnose complex infections, trace outbreak transmission routes, monitor pathogen evolution, and analyze microbiomes as potential disease biomarkers. The authors conclude that future progress in infectious disease molecular diagnostics will come from addressing current limitations and integrating multiple technologies into hybrid platforms.
items.citation: Takata M, Chikumi H, Yoshifuji A. Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.. Yonago acta medica. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review paper examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and translational medicine. The authors synthesize current knowledge across multiple omics layers — including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics — and assess how deep learning architectures can extract meaningful biological patterns from these complex, high-dimensional datasets. The review covers the application of this combined approach throughout the drug development pipeline, including target identification, drug repositioning, de novo compound discovery, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Disease areas explored include oncology, neurodegenerative disorders, and cardiovascular conditions, with attention to the technological infrastructure supporting these advances. While highlighting the transformative potential of merging multiomics with artificial intelligence, the authors also acknowledge persistent challenges such as data harmonization, reproducibility, and algorithmic bias that must be addressed to fully realize the promise of data-driven therapeutic innovation.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges
items.summary: This systematic review examined the potential of CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials against multidrug-resistant bacteria, motivated by the growing global failure of conventional antibiotics. The authors synthesized preclinical evidence across studies evaluating different CRISPR effectors, including Cas9, Cas12, and Cas13, assessing their mechanisms of antibacterial action and the platforms used to deliver them into bacterial targets. The review found that CRISPR-Cas systems can effectively kill or resensitize resistant bacteria through mechanisms such as chromosomal double-strand break induction, resistance plasmid elimination, and RNA-targeted cleavage, with phage-mediated delivery showing the most consistent efficacy across complex environments and animal models. One CRISPR-enhanced engineered bacteriophage cocktail has progressed to clinical evaluation, underscoring the translational momentum in this field. Nevertheless, the authors highlight substantial remaining barriers, including limited bacterial host range, physiological instability, emergence of escape mutations, and insufficient long-term safety data, concluding that advances in delivery optimization, multiplex targeting, and regulatory frameworks will be essential for clinical translation.
items.citation: Maha S.I. Wizrah. CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Influence of protein aggregates, extracellular vesicles, and lipoprotein fusion on ionizable lipid nanoparticles protein corona analysis
items.summary: This perspective paper examines the protein corona that forms around ionizable lipid nanoparticles used in nucleic acid therapeutics, focusing on the analytical challenges that complicate accurate characterization of this corona. The authors argue that extrahepatic delivery of these nanoparticles remains difficult because apolipoprotein adsorption drives rapid hepatic uptake, making it essential to understand which proteins genuinely associate with the nanoparticle surface to engineer organ-specific tropism. A central problem identified is that blood-borne contaminants such as extracellular vesicles and lipoproteins co-isolate with the nanoparticles during analysis, obscuring the true composition of the protein corona. The authors propose that the protein corona on ionizable lipid nanoparticles is fundamentally different from the rigid shells seen on inorganic nanoparticles due to its fluid, dynamic nature, and they advocate for tailored proteomic strategies capable of distinguishing genuine corona constituents from these impurities.
items.citation: Babak Borhan, Amanda M. Murray, Amir Ata Saei et al.. Influence of protein aggregates, extracellular vesicles, and lipoprotein fusion on ionizable lipid nanoparticles protein corona analysis. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: MXene quantum dot polymer nanocomposites as smart platforms for targeted drug delivery and multifunctional biomedical applications: an updated review
items.summary: This review examines MXene quantum dot polymer nanocomposites and their applications in targeted drug delivery and multifunctional biomedical systems. The paper surveys how MXenes and their composites leverage exceptional electrical conductivity, flexibility, and biocompatibility to enable smart microrobots capable of precise navigation and therapeutic release, particularly in cancer treatment. The review further explores how combining MXenes with quantum dots in polymer matrices merges electrical, optical, and catalytic properties to advance applications spanning tissue engineering, flexible electronics, and energy storage. Stimuli-responsive polymers embedded within these composites allow controlled activation of therapeutic agents, and co-delivery of multiple drugs offers potential for synergistic treatment strategies. The authors conclude that while these nanocomposites hold considerable promise for driving innovation in biomedicine and sustainable technologies, challenges related to scalable production, long-term stability, and clinical translation remain to be addressed.
items.citation: Mohammad Hossein Karami, Omid Moini Jazani. MXene quantum dot polymer nanocomposites as smart platforms for targeted drug delivery and multifunctional biomedical applications: an updated review. Discover Nano. 2026

items.title: Direct cell-to-cell transmission of retrotransposons
items.summary: This paper investigated how certain retrotransposons spread between cells, challenging the assumption that transposable elements are restricted to the cell in which they are expressed. The researchers studied a group of long terminal repeat retrotransposons in the Drosophila ovary that move from somatic cells into the germline despite lacking the Envelope protein conventionally required for retroviral cell entry. Using genetics, imaging, and electron microscopy, they discovered that these elements instead encode a short transmembrane protein called sORF2, which has structural features resembling viral cell-cell fusogens and localizes to invasive somatic protrusions that physically contact the oocyte membrane and carry retroviral capsids. Eliminating sORF2 abolished both protrusion formation and soma-to-germline capsid transmission, demonstrating its essential role in this process. The authors further show that sORF2-like proteins are broadly distributed across insect retrotransposons and appear in certain fish and bird viruses, suggesting this represents a widespread, Envelope-independent mechanism of intercellular transmission shared between retrotransposons and non-enveloped viruses.
items.citation: Maya Voichek, Andreas Bernhard, Lea Lauterjung et al.. Direct cell-to-cell transmission of retrotransposons. Cell. 2026

items.title: Metabolic determinants of cancer immunotherapy outcomes identified by plasma profiling
items.summary: This study investigated the metabolic factors that determine whether cancer patients respond to immune-checkpoint inhibitor therapy. Using targeted metabolomics and metagenomics on a large, multi-cohort collection of plasma samples drawn from patients with five different tumor types across Europe and North America, the researchers profiled metabolites longitudinally across multiple treatment modalities including fecal microbiota transplantation. A multimodal machine-learning framework integrating metabolite data with clinical variables identified a small set of metabolites alongside age, body mass index, and renal function as predictors of twelve-month progression-free survival, with the model generalizing across several external cohorts. Histidine emerged as a favorable prognostic metabolite, while long-chain fatty acids and succinate were negatively associated with outcomes; supplementing histidine enhanced antitumor immunity in mice, and histidine-rich diets improved progression-free survival in patients who lacked dysbiotic microbiome signatures linked to histidine catabolism. Together, these findings reveal plasma metabolic signatures of immunotherapy response and highlight histidine as a candidate for therapeutic intervention.
items.citation: Déborah Suissa, Marine Fidelle, Ella Reich et al.. Metabolic determinants of cancer immunotherapy outcomes identified by plasma profiling. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental limitation of Unified Multimodal Models, namely their inability to effectively apply chain-of-thought reasoning to image generation due to a mismatch between discrete token-based reasoning and the continuous space required for image generation. To overcome this, the authors propose LARC, a Latent Reasoning in Continuous space framework that shifts reasoning from discrete tokens to continuous hidden states through a two-stage training process: curriculum supervised fine-tuning that gradually transitions token-level reasoning into latent reasoning, followed by an information-gain reinforcement learning stage that refines latent reasoning without requiring ground truth supervision. Evaluations across multiple text-to-image generation benchmarks demonstrate that LARC consistently improves generation quality, prompt adherence, and compositional accuracy, achieving state-of-the-art results and outperforming prior token-based approaches under both parallel and sequential test-time scaling strategies. The work suggests that performing reasoning in continuous latent space not only resolves the modality mismatch problem but also enables the test-time scaling behavior previously observed only in large language models to extend to multimodal generation.
items.citation: Byungwoo Jeon, Yoonwoo Jeong, Hyunseok Lee et al.. Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of long-horizon planning for embodied agents, where cumulative errors and search complexity degrade performance in world model-based approaches. The authors introduce a hierarchical world model framework called ID-WM that separates high-level state reachability reasoning from low-level action execution by pairing a high-level model for sampling feasible state transitions with a low-level inverse dynamics solver that grounds these transitions into concrete actions. This decoupling allows the planner to identify achievable subgoals without being constrained by low-level execution details, and by prioritizing local physical feasibility the framework can compose novel long-horizon plans from short segments that generalize beyond behaviors seen during training. The approach was evaluated across navigation and manipulation benchmarks, where it substantially outperformed both state-of-the-art policy and diffusion-based planners as well as single-level world model model predictive control, with particularly large gains on complex, unseen configurations requiring long-horizon reasoning.
items.citation: Gaoyue Zhou, Yvonne Wu, Zichen Jeff Cui et al.. Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: SemEllipsoid: Semantic-aware Shape Abstraction with Ellipsoid
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of shape abstraction, where three-dimensional shapes are represented compactly using geometric primitives, by introducing a new task called semantic-aware shape abstraction. Unlike prior work that focuses solely on geometric fidelity, the authors identify that existing methods often produce primitives that straddle multiple semantic parts, causing problems for downstream tasks like part-level editing. To solve this, they propose SemEllipsoid, a method that uses ellipsoidal primitives and injects semantic constraints into the optimization process by leveraging semantic cues from large-scale foundation models. The approach employs a fully differentiable projection-blending-evaluation scheme to measure semantic divergence against input semantic masks, combined with an alternating optimization strategy that jointly refines semantic assignments and primitive configurations without requiring any training data or learned networks. Experiments across multiple shape collections demonstrate that the method produces abstractions that are both geometrically faithful and semantically consistent, generalizing across arbitrary object categories and supporting user-controlled levels of abstraction.
items.citation: Kuankuan Cheng, Haocheng Yuan, Changjian Li. SemEllipsoid: Semantic-aware Shape Abstraction with Ellipsoid. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Dittany: Contribution-Guided Repair Framework for MAS Applications
items.summary: The paper investigates runtime repair of large language model-based multi-agent system applications, which often produce partial results that fail to fully satisfy task requirements. The authors developed a framework called Dittany that constructs a contribution graph by deriving expected contributions and acceptance conditions from task requirements and method specifications, using this structure to identify which completed results remain usable and what work still needs to be done. At runtime, the framework performs targeted corrections at either the action level, when sufficient inputs are available, or the graph level, when prerequisites or incomplete work require broader revision, while preserving already-validated outputs throughout. Evaluated across a large set of applications and tasks spanning multiple multi-agent frameworks, the system achieved strong failure detection performance and substantially improved task accuracy compared to unassisted native execution and several recovery baselines. The approach also demonstrated favorable token efficiency relative to competing repair methods, and ablation studies confirmed that combining both repair scopes outperforms relying on graph-level repair alone.
items.citation: Hanqi Sun, Yuchen Shao, Hanyi Si et al.. Dittany: Contribution-Guided Repair Framework for MAS Applications. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Value of Adding AI Weather Model Ensembles to a Multi-model Probabilistic Blend
items.summary: This study investigated whether incorporating an ensemble artificial intelligence weather model into a multi-model probabilistic blend improves forecast skill, a question not previously explored despite known benefits of blending deterministic AI models with physics-based systems. The researchers blended an ensemble AI-based forecasting system with a convection-permitting physics-based ensemble to produce site-level temperature and wind speed forecasts over the United Kingdom, examining performance across lead times, spatial domains, and exceedance thresholds. They found that blending ensemble AI and physics-based models consistently improved forecast skill, particularly when the component models had differing error characteristics, and demonstrated through decomposition of forecast skill scores that assigning greater weight to more skillful models and combining models with complementary errors produces the most accurate blends. A key finding was that model diversity matters greatly, such that pairing either the AI ensemble or a physics-based global model with the regional convection-permitting ensemble outperformed blending the two more similar global systems together. The study also showed that calibrating the AI ensemble yields skill comparable to calibrated physics-based ensembles, and that calibrating both before and after blending further improves accuracy, with implications for pursuing diverse parallel approaches in weather model development.
items.citation: Harris Sop Nkuiate, Gavin Evans, Christopher A. T. Ferro et al.. Value of Adding AI Weather Model Ensembles to a Multi-model Probabilistic Blend. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Subquadratic Attention with a Hierarchical Tree-Structured Indexer
items.summary: This paper addresses the quadratic computational cost of attention in large language models, which fundamentally limits how long a context these models can process. The authors propose a sparse attention method called Zyphra Hierarchical Attention, which builds a tree of recursively compressed key summaries over the key-value cache, allowing queries to traverse the tree top-down to retrieve only a relevant sparse subset of keys. By growing the tree depth iteratively, the total routing and attention cost scales sublinearly in sequence length, yielding overall subquadratic rather than quadratic scaling. The method can be applied to already-trained models through a short distillation fine-tuning stage on a modest number of tokens, and it preserves performance on long-context retrieval, reasoning, mathematics, and agentic coding tasks while remaining robust to varying tree geometries. The authors further show through performance modeling that their approach substantially outperforms competing methods at very long contexts and theoretically enables effective context windows extending to hundreds of millions or even billions of tokens.
items.citation: Leon Lufkin, Cutter Dawes, Alexander Speicher et al.. Subquadratic Attention with a Hierarchical Tree-Structured Indexer. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Multiplexed Nucleic Acid Detection Using Sequence-Specific Cleavage Mediated by Repair Endonucleases.
items.summary: This paper presents TIMBER, a nucleic acid detection platform that uses repair endonucleases to cleave abasic-site-containing probes only when hybridized to a matched target sequence, offering an alternative to CRISPR-based diagnostic systems. Unlike CRISPR approaches, TIMBER avoids collateral nonspecific nuclease activity, which simplifies multiplexing and point-of-care integration. The system achieves single-nucleotide polymorphism discrimination and can detect targets at very low concentrations without preamplification, or at near-single-copy sensitivity when paired with RT-PCR or RT-LAMP amplification, with results readable by fluorescence or lateral flow. The authors validated TIMBER by detecting SARS-CoV-2 in clinical saliva samples and demonstrated simultaneous multiplexed detection of four targets, including the identification of cancer-relevant EGFR mutations in lung cancer samples. The platform is presented as a flexible, rapid, and low-instrument-burden solution applicable across infectious disease surveillance and precision oncology.
items.citation: Garden PM, Li Y, Murugan V et al.. Multiplexed Nucleic Acid Detection Using Sequence-Specific Cleavage Mediated by Repair Endonucleases.. ACS sensors. 2026

items.title: The Oral–Gut–Brain Axis: From Periodontal Dysbiosis to Neuroinflammation—Mechanistic Pathways, Salivary and Intestinal Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Targets: A Narrative Review
items.summary: This narrative review examined the biological connections linking periodontal disease, gut health, and brain function through what the authors term the oral–gut–brain axis. The authors conducted a structured literature search across major databases to synthesize evidence on the molecular mechanisms by which periodontal dysbiosis may propagate systemic inflammation through the gut to the brain, as well as the utility of salivary and intestinal biomarkers for monitoring this pathway. Periodontal pathogens, particularly Porphyromonas gingivalis and Fusobacterium nucleatum, have been detected in the gut and are associated with disrupted intestinal barrier integrity, altered microbial composition, increased blood–brain barrier permeability, microglial activation, and amyloid-beta accumulation in preclinical and observational studies. Salivary markers such as matrix metalloproteinases and interleukins, alongside intestinal markers including short-chain fatty acids and calprotectin, are proposed as non-invasive tools for assessing systemic inflammatory burden across the entire axis. The authors conclude that while this tripartite framework offers a plausible mechanistic account of comorbidities spanning periodontal, cardiometabolic, and neurodegenerative diseases, current evidence remains largely associative and requires validation through longitudinal human studies before causal claims or clinical interventions can be firmly established.
items.citation: Caterina Nela Dumitru, Alina Oana Dumitru, Gabriel Valeriu Popa et al.. The Oral–Gut–Brain Axis: From Periodontal Dysbiosis to Neuroinflammation—Mechanistic Pathways, Salivary and Intestinal Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Targets: A Narrative Review. Dentistry Journal. 2026

items.title: Consented Universal Newborn Screening for Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection Using Dried Blood Spot and Dried Saliva Spot Specimens: Implementation and Relative Programmatic Accuracy.
items.summary: This study evaluated two specimen types — dried blood spots and dried saliva spots — for use in universal newborn screening for congenital cytomegalovirus infection, a condition that can cause significant developmental harm if undetected. A prospective pilot study was conducted across multiple birthing centers, using quantitative PCR assays on both specimen types, with confirmatory urine testing offered to those who screened positive. Although dried saliva spots showed a trend toward higher sensitivity, the difference was not statistically significant, and saliva-based screening produced a substantially higher false positive rate, generating multiple additional false positives for each additional true case detected. Saliva specimens also extended turnaround times, frequently missing the window required to offer confirmatory diagnostic testing within the critical early period of life. Based on this performance profile, the investigators concluded that dried saliva spot screening did not support population-wide implementation within their program.
items.citation: Santander E, Reuvers E, Lacaria M et al.. Consented Universal Newborn Screening for Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection Using Dried Blood Spot and Dried Saliva Spot Specimens: Implementation and Relative Programmatic Accuracy.. International journal of neonatal screening. 2026

items.title: Vitamin D<sub>3</sub> oral rinsing reduces salivary SARS-CoV-2 antigen detectability: a clinical trial with public health implications.
items.summary: This clinical trial investigated whether rinsing the mouth with a Vitamin D₃ solution could affect the accuracy of saliva-based rapid antigen tests (RAT) for SARS-CoV-2. Adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection provided paired saliva samples immediately before and after a one-minute Vitamin D₃ oral rinse, with samples analyzed by both RAT and rapid RT-PCR under blinded conditions. The rinse converted a large majority of RAT-positive specimens to RAT-negative, substantially reducing antigen positivity, while RT-PCR positivity and viral RNA levels remained largely unchanged. This discordance indicates that viral RNA persisted in saliva despite the reduction in detectable antigen, suggesting the rinse interfered with antigen detection rather than eliminating the virus. The findings identify Vitamin D₃ oral rinsing as a previously unrecognized pre-analytical variable that can produce false-negative results in saliva-based antigen testing, with potential implications for infectious disease screening and public health surveillance.
items.citation: Feteih SMN, Heaphy ELG, Aljagthmi A et al.. Vitamin D<sub>3</sub> oral rinsing reduces salivary SARS-CoV-2 antigen detectability: a clinical trial with public health implications.. Frontiers in oral health. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Molecular Testing on Saliva and Oral Swabs for Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether molecular testing on saliva and oral swabs could serve as accurate, nonsputum alternatives for diagnosing pulmonary tuberculosis. Using a nested case-control design within a prospective cohort of adults and children at primary care centers in Colombia, researchers tested paired saliva and nylon-flocked oral swab samples from culture-confirmed tuberculosis cases and matched culture-negative controls using Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra. Saliva demonstrated higher sensitivity than oral swabs, exceeding the World Health Organization's target threshold for nonsputum diagnostic tests, while both specimen types achieved high specificity for culture-confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis. Saliva outperformed swabs in sensitivity by a clinically meaningful margin, though no significant difference in specificity was observed between the two collection methods. Patient acceptability was high for both collection procedures, supporting the feasibility of these approaches as practical, nonsputum tuberculosis diagnostic tools.
items.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
items.citation: Vargas DA, Fuertes-Bucheli JF, Sanchez-Hidalgo A et al.. Diagnostic Accuracy of Molecular Testing on Saliva and Oral Swabs for Pulmonary Tuberculosis.. Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America. 2026

items.title: Bioactive Gold Plasmonic Interfaces Meet Artificial Intelligence: Advancing Saliva-Based Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy Diagnostics.
items.summary: This review examines the integration of gold plasmonic nanostructures, surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy, and artificial intelligence for non-invasive diagnostic applications using saliva as a liquid biopsy. The authors analyze how physical and chemical properties of gold nanostructures—including geometry, surface functionalization, antifouling strategies, and protein-corona formation—control molecular access to electromagnetic hot spots and thereby govern spectral reproducibility and the reliability of computational analysis. Saliva is presented as a cross-disease diagnostic medium relevant to a broad range of conditions including oncological, infectious, inflammatory, metabolic, neurodegenerative, and pulmonary disorders. Case studies across these disease categories are used to illustrate how substrate engineering and dataset construction together determine diagnostic performance and clinical portability. The authors conclude that clinically viable saliva-based diagnostics will require coordinated co-design of bioactive plasmonic interfaces and computational pipelines, alongside standardized sample preparation, reproducible substrates, and rigorous multicenter patient-level validation.
items.citation: Dhal A, Aviña AE, Hang NLT et al.. Bioactive Gold Plasmonic Interfaces Meet Artificial Intelligence: Advancing Saliva-Based Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy Diagnostics.. Small (Weinheim an der Bergstrasse, Germany). 2026

items.title: Lethal hantavirus at sea: Infectious disease outbreaks on cruise ships and limits of preparedness
items.summary: This paper examines a lethal hantavirus outbreak that occurred aboard the expedition cruise ship Hondius in 2026, representing an unusual cluster of zoonotic disease in a maritime travel setting. The authors analyzed the epidemiological circumstances of the outbreak, in which multiple confirmed and suspected cases, including several deaths, were identified among passengers and crew who had traveled through remote South Atlantic and sub-Antarctic regions. Because hantavirus is transmitted primarily through inhalation of aerosolized rodent excreta rather than person-to-person spread, the authors characterized the event as likely involving a point-source exposure—either during shore excursions, aboard the vessel, or prior to embarkation—rather than sustained onboard transmission. The paper discusses how this incident highlights the intersection of zoonotic disease risk with global expedition travel and ecological exposure in remote environments. The authors argue that the outbreak reveals significant gaps in infectious disease preparedness for maritime settings, and that definitive determination of exposure origin requires comprehensive epidemiological investigation combined with laboratory confirmation and viral sequencing.
items.citation: Alimuddin I. Zumla, Brian McCloskey, Giuseppe Ippolito et al.. Lethal hantavirus at sea: Infectious disease outbreaks on cruise ships and limits of preparedness. Travel Medicine and Infectious Disease. 2026

items.title: Andes virus outbreak linked to expedition cruise ship travel, multi-country investigation and response, April to June 2026
items.summary: The abstract describes an active outbreak investigation of Andes orthohantavirus linked to an expedition cruise ship, involving cases among both passengers and crew across many nationalities. Investigators conducted coordinated international contact tracing, medical evacuation, repatriation, isolation, quarantine, and laboratory testing to contain and characterize the event. The outbreak resulted in a notable case fatality rate, with cases identified among a minority of those aboard. Ongoing investigations are focused on determining the source of exposure, clarifying risk factors, and preventing further transmission.
items.citation: Oda E. van den Berg, UKHSA ANDV Team, Ettore Severi et al.. Andes virus outbreak linked to expedition cruise ship travel, multi-country investigation and response, April to June 2026. Eurosurveillance. 2026

items.title: Human infection with Andes hantavirus: an update for the general physician
items.summary: Andes virus, a zoonotic hantavirus endemic to South America, is unique among its family for its capacity for sustained human-to-human transmission via respiratory droplets, with a reproductive number exceeding two and an incubation period of up to forty days. This review updates general physicians on the clinical features, epidemiology, and management of Andes virus infection, with particular attention to its most severe manifestation, hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, which is characterised by acute respiratory failure, haemodynamic instability, and dysregulated immune responses carrying high lethality. Laboratory markers including neutrophilia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated lactate dehydrogenase correlate with disease severity, yet no approved antiviral therapy or vaccine exists, leaving supportive care as the only management strategy. A recent cruise ship outbreak involving passengers of multiple nationalities, resulting in confirmed deaths, is highlighted as an example of how a pathogen with limited but sustained human-to-human transmission can rapidly spread globally through mass international travel. The authors emphasise the urgent need for clinician awareness, prompt contact tracing, and internationally coordinated outbreak preparedness in response to this emerging infectious threat.
items.citation: Emanuele Durante‐Mangoni, Iolanda Cafarella, Silvia Mercadante et al.. Human infection with Andes hantavirus: an update for the general physician. European Journal of Internal Medicine. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review examines hantaviruses, rodent-borne pathogens responsible for two serious disease syndromes — hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome — that are increasingly recognized as global public health threats. The authors synthesize current knowledge across virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnostics, and surveillance, with particular attention to how climate change, urbanization, and land-use transformation alter rodent reservoir dynamics and spillover risk to humans. The review identifies notable gaps in surveillance and diagnostics in tropical and Caribbean regions where hantavirus circulation is likely underrecognized. Advances discussed include molecular and genomic diagnostic tools, vaccine candidates, monoclonal antibody therapies, and climate-based early warning systems. The authors conclude that integrated One Health surveillance frameworks uniting human, animal, and environmental monitoring — alongside strengthened laboratory capacity and regional collaboration — are essential for reducing the global burden of hantavirus disease and preparing for future zoonotic threats.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: From microbiomes to predictive ecosystems: challenges and opportunities in artificial intelligence-based approaches
items.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence is reshaping microbiome research, a field challenged by the vast scale and complexity of microbial systems across diverse ecological and host-associated niches. The authors outline how AI methods enable more integrative analyses of microbial genomes, community structure, and functional potential, pushing the field from purely descriptive work toward predictive modelling and hypothesis generation. Key opportunities highlighted include improved understanding of microbial function, host-microbe interactions, and ecosystem-level organisation, with multiomics and multicohort integration identified as promising strategies for deepening biological insight. The review also addresses persistent technical challenges such as model interpretability, generalisability, and causal inference. Finally, the authors argue that ethical considerations around data privacy, algorithmic bias, and equitable access must be resolved to translate AI-driven microbiome discoveries into robust and inclusive clinical applications.
items.citation: Wanqian Yu, Hua Qu, Shaopu Wang et al.. From microbiomes to predictive ecosystems: challenges and opportunities in artificial intelligence-based approaches. The Lancet Microbe. 2026

items.title: Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments
items.summary: This paper investigates intrinsic alignments of galaxies, which are a systematic contaminant in weak gravitational lensing surveys and a probe of galaxy formation physics. The authors developed model-agnostic methods to test two key aspects of intrinsic alignment modeling: the effect of density-weighting on alignment signals, and the validity of the tidal alignment paradigm that assumes galaxy shapes are determined by the local tidal field. Using data from the IllustrisTNG hydrodynamical simulation and an observational galaxy survey, they examined two-point correlation functions of galaxy shapes, tidal fields, and the background tidal field of the simulation. They found that density-weighting primarily amplifies the alignment signal on large scales, while its effect on small scales depends on the specific galaxy sample. Additionally, they found that central galaxies align linearly with the underlying tidal field even deep into the one-halo regime, supporting the tidal alignment framework even in the non-linear regime where it might not be expected to hold.
items.citation: Paul Rogozenski, Sukhdeep Singh, Jonathan Blazek et al.. Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary: This paper investigates why unified multimodal models fail to effectively use chain-of-thought reasoning for image generation, attributing the problem to a fundamental mismatch between discrete token-based reasoning and the continuous space in which image generation operates. To address this, the authors propose LARC (Latent Reasoning in Continuous space), a framework that shifts reasoning from discrete tokens to continuous hidden states through a two-stage training process: curriculum supervised fine-tuning that gradually transitions token-level reasoning to latent reasoning, followed by information-gain reinforcement learning that refines latent reasoning without ground truth supervision. Experiments on text-to-image generation benchmarks demonstrate that LARC improves generation quality, prompt following, and compositional fidelity compared to existing approaches. The framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on a standard evaluation benchmark and, notably, exhibits test-time scaling behavior under both parallel and sequential strategies, a property previously absent in reasoning-augmented unified multimodal models.
items.citation: Byungwoo Jeon, Yoonwoo Jeong, Hyunseok Lee et al.. Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of long-horizon planning for embodied agents, where cumulative errors and search complexity undermine performance in tasks requiring extended sequences of actions. The authors propose ID-WM, a hierarchical world model framework that separates high-level state-space reachability from low-level control by pairing a high-level model that samples feasible transitions across a state manifold with a low-level inverse dynamics model that translates those transitions into concrete actions. This decoupling allows the planner to identify reachable subgoals without being burdened by low-level execution details, and by emphasizing local physical feasibility rather than global behavioral patterns, the system can compose novel long-horizon plans from short segments that generalize beyond behaviors seen during training. The approach was evaluated across navigation and manipulation benchmarks, substantially outperforming both state-of-the-art policy and diffusion-based planners as well as single-level world model model-predictive control, with particularly large gains on complex, unseen configurations.
items.citation: Gaoyue Zhou, Yvonne Wu, Zichen Jeff Cui et al.. Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: SemEllipsoid: Semantic-aware Shape Abstraction with Ellipsoid
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of shape abstraction—representing 3D shapes using compact sets of geometric primitives—by introducing a new task variant called semantic-aware shape abstraction, where primitives must respect semantic part boundaries rather than spanning multiple parts. Prior geometry-focused methods achieve good geometric fidelity but produce primitives that often cross semantic boundaries, creating problems for part-level editing and manipulation. The authors propose SemEllipsoid, a method that uses ellipsoidal primitives and injects semantic constraints into the optimization process by leveraging semantic cues derived from large-scale foundation models. A differentiable projection-blending-evaluation scheme measures semantic divergence against input semantic masks, and an alternating optimization strategy iteratively refines both semantic assignments and primitive configurations. The approach requires no training data or network training, generalizes across arbitrary shape categories, and is validated on multiple 3D shape collections, demonstrating that it achieves both geometric faithfulness and semantic consistency.
items.citation: Kuankuan Cheng, Haocheng Yuan, Changjian Li. SemEllipsoid: Semantic-aware Shape Abstraction with Ellipsoid. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Dittany: Contribution-Guided Repair Framework for MAS Applications
items.summary: The paper introduces Dittany, a runtime repair framework designed to fix failures in large language model-based multi-agent system applications that produce incomplete or unsatisfactory results. The framework works by deriving expected contributions and acceptance conditions from task requirements and method specifications, organizing their dependencies into a contribution graph that guides both failure detection and repair. At runtime, Dittany identifies unmet conditions, preserves validated intermediate results, and applies either action-level correction when inputs are sufficient or graph-level recovery when prerequisite work needs revision. Evaluated across a large set of applications and tasks spanning multiple multi-agent frameworks, Dittany substantially improved task accuracy over both unassisted execution and competing recovery baselines while keeping additional token consumption well below that of alternative repair approaches. Ablation studies confirmed that combining the two repair scopes yields better accuracy and lower token cost than relying on graph-level repair alone.
items.citation: Hanqi Sun, Yuchen Shao, Hanyi Si et al.. Dittany: Contribution-Guided Repair Framework for MAS Applications. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Approximate Polynomial Satisfiability and Integral Closure Membership in the Counting Hierarchy
items.summary: This paper studies the computational complexity of two algebraic problems: approximate polynomial satisfiability (APS), which asks whether a polynomial system has solutions arbitrarily close to the origin but not exactly at it, and integral closure membership testing, which asks whether a polynomial is integral over a given polynomial ring. The authors place both problems within the Counting Hierarchy, significantly improving the previously known upper bound of PSPACE for APS. Their approach to APS combines Noether normalization with a geometric analysis of how points in the image of a polynomial map approach the origin, ultimately reducing the problem to a test on multivariate resultants that can be evaluated within the Counting Hierarchy. For integral closure membership, they use a global annihilator criterion together with an effective degree bound to reduce non-integrality to APS in polynomial time, thereby inheriting the same complexity upper bound. These results complement concurrent independent work by other groups and have implications for geometric complexity theory, particularly for constructing hitting sets for algebraic complexity classes in a more efficient complexity class than previously achieved.
items.citation: Sanyam Agarwal, Archit Hari, Anurag Pandey et al.. Approximate Polynomial Satisfiability and Integral Closure Membership in the Counting Hierarchy. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis
items.summary: This review examines the relationship between gut microbial-derived metabolites and kidney disease, focusing on how disruptions in the gut microbiome contribute to renal injury and fibrosis. Kidney damage triggers a cycle involving intestinal barrier dysfunction, microbial dysbiosis, and metabolite imbalance, characterized by reductions in beneficial short-chain fatty acids and accumulation of harmful uremic toxins such as indoxyl sulfate and trimethylamine-N-oxide. These metabolites exert their effects through multiple signaling pathways, with tryptophan metabolites identified as particularly important mediators of gut-kidney communication. The review synthesizes current knowledge across several kidney conditions, including acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease, diabetic kidney disease, and immunoglobulin A nephropathy, elucidating the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms. It also evaluates therapeutic strategies targeting gut dysbiosis, including natural products, prebiotics, probiotics, and renal replacement therapy, as avenues for more precise treatment of kidney diseases.
items.citation: Wan-Ying Zhang, Yu-Lu Zhang, Qing-Qing Yu et al.. Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis. International Journal of Biological Sciences. 2026

items.title: Editor's Choice – European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2026 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
items.summary: These guidelines from the European Society for Vascular Surgery address the clinical management of vascular graft and endograft infections, updating a prior version to reflect the best available current evidence. The guidelines were developed by synthesizing scientific evidence with expert opinion, with recommendations graded by strength and level of evidence according to an established classification system. A substantial set of recommendations was produced covering key domains including definitions, diagnosis, multidisciplinary team management, antimicrobial therapy, management of both intracavitary and extracavitary infections, and follow-up care. The guidelines also incorporate a chapter on shared decision-making with patient-facing information, as well as a discussion of unresolved clinical questions. The stated aim is to provide comprehensive, up-to-date guidance to assist clinicians and patients in selecting optimal management strategies for vascular graft and endograft infections.
items.venue: European Journal of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery
items.citation: Anne Lejay, Ben R. Saleem, Tara D. Barwick et al.. Editor's Choice – European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2026 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections. European Journal of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery. 2026

items.title: The gut-kidney axis in chronic kidney disease: a vicious cycle of microbial dysbiosis and uremic toxin accumulation
items.summary: This review examines the bidirectional relationship between the gut microbiome and kidney function in chronic kidney disease, focusing on how microbial changes drive disease progression. In patients with chronic kidney disease, gut microbial diversity is reduced, beneficial butyrate-producing bacteria are depleted, and pathogenic bacteria capable of generating uremic toxins are enriched, leading to overproduction of both protein-bound and non-protein-bound uremic toxins through altered amino acid metabolic pathways. These toxins compromise intestinal barrier integrity, promote systemic endotoxin translocation and inflammation, and at the kidney level induce oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and fibrosis through multiple signaling pathways. The authors describe a self-sustaining vicious cycle in which declining renal function causes toxin accumulation, which in turn accelerates further kidney deterioration and systemic complications. On the basis of this framework, the review highlights therapeutic strategies aimed at suppressing uremic toxin production or restoring beneficial microbial metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids as potential approaches to slow chronic kidney disease progression.
items.citation: Ruohan Guan, Jiaxuan Peng, Qianxi Gu et al.. The gut-kidney axis in chronic kidney disease: a vicious cycle of microbial dysbiosis and uremic toxin accumulation. Frontiers in Immunology. 2026

items.title: Gut Microbial Metabotypes Shape Polyphenol Bioactivity: Toward Precision Nutrition Strategies for Human Health
items.summary: This narrative review examined how gut microbiota-mediated biotransformation of dietary polyphenols shapes their biological effects and relevance for personalized nutrition. Because many polyphenols are poorly absorbed in the upper gastrointestinal tract, gut bacteria convert them in the colon into smaller metabolites such as urolithins, equol, and enterolignans, which can have distinct absorption and bioactivity profiles compared to their parent compounds. The review critically assessed the concept of microbial metabotypes, which classify individuals by their capacity to produce specific microbial-derived metabolites, and explored how variation in gut microbiota composition drives substantial interindividual differences in metabolite production. Evidence for biological effects related to mitochondrial function, inflammation, metabolic regulation, endothelial homeostasis, gut barrier integrity, and gut-brain communication was evaluated, with careful distinction between human and preclinical findings. The authors conclude that while metabotype-guided stratification holds promise for improving nutritional intervention studies, clinical translation is currently hindered by non-standardized methods, incomplete population validation, and insufficient long-term data, positioning microbial metabotypes as useful research biomarkers rather than established tools for routine personalized dietary prescription.
items.citation: Pasquale Perrone, Stefania D’Angelo. Gut Microbial Metabotypes Shape Polyphenol Bioactivity: Toward Precision Nutrition Strategies for Human Health. Nutrients. 2026

items.title: The Gut–Vagina Axis
items.summary: This review paper examines the emerging concept of the gut–vagina axis, which describes the bidirectional relationship between the gut and vaginal microbiomes and its implications for female health. The authors synthesize recent advances in microbiome research to characterize the mechanisms through which these two distinct microbial communities may interact, including microbial migration, hormonal and immune regulation, and metabolite exchange. The review highlights how communication between gut and vaginal communities may influence microbial composition, immune responses, hormonal balance, and metabolic activity at both sites. The authors emphasize that these interactions have consequences not only locally but also for systemic health, positioning the gut–vagina axis as a significant but underexplored dimension of female physiology.
items.citation: Lorenzo Agoni, Elena Roselletti, Giovanni Marasco et al.. The Gut–Vagina Axis. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
items.summary: This paper presents updated clinical guidelines on infection prevention, diagnosis, and management in patients with inflammatory bowel disease, developed by the European Crohn's and Colitis Organisation. The guidelines were motivated by the rapid expansion of immunosuppressive and biologic therapies for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, including newer small molecules and advanced biologics, which carry distinct infection risk profiles compared to older agents. The authors conducted a structured, evidence-based review integrating contemporary data on risk stratification and on viral, bacterial, mycobacterial, and vaccine-preventable infections relevant to immunocompromised IBD patients. The resulting guidance emphasizes a preventative strategy tailored to the modern IBD treatment landscape, updating previous consensus statements to reflect the evolving therapeutic armamentarium and its implications for opportunistic infection risk.
items.venue: Journal of Crohn s and Colitis
items.citation: Henit A. Yanai, Pierre Ellul, Bram Verstockt et al.. ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease. Journal of Crohn s and Colitis. 2026

items.title: GazeRIB: Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Reader Gaze-Guided Chest X-ray Learning
items.summary: This paper investigated how the composition of radiologist reader panels affects the utility of gaze-guided supervision for training chest X-ray classification models. The researchers developed and evaluated GazeRIB, a method that masks image regions not viewed by radiologists during model training while using complete images at inference, testing it across eight expert readers organized into panels of varying sizes, multiple neural network architectures, and random seeds. Panel-based gaze supervision consistently improved multi-class severity prediction over a no-gaze baseline, with even a three-reader panel capturing the majority of the performance gain achieved by the full eight-reader panel. External validation revealed that the benefit of gaze guidance was cohort-dependent, with panels improving performance on one external dataset but showing no significant advantage on another, while single-reader averaging actually degraded performance on the latter. The findings demonstrate that reader panel composition meaningfully influences model performance and that a relatively small panel can efficiently approximate the benefit of larger ensembles, though generalizability across datasets remains a key challenge.
items.citation: Nattakorn Kittisut, Roy M. Gabriel, Marly van Assen et al.. GazeRIB: Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Reader Gaze-Guided Chest X-ray Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments
items.summary: This paper investigates the intrinsic alignments of galaxies, which introduce systematic uncertainties in weak gravitational lensing measurements and probe galaxy formation and evolution. The authors developed model-agnostic methods to assess two aspects of intrinsic alignments: how density-weighting of galaxy samples affects alignment signals, and whether the tidal alignment paradigm accurately describes galaxy orientations. Using data from the IllustrisTNG cosmological hydrodynamical simulation and an observational galaxy survey, they found that density-weighting primarily amplifies alignment signals on large scales, while its effect on small scales depends on the specific galaxy sample. Their tests of the tidal alignment framework revealed that central galaxies align linearly with the underlying non-linear tidal field even down into the one-halo regime, supporting the validity of tidal alignment models at small scales within the precision of their measurements.
items.citation: Paul Rogozenski, Sukhdeep Singh, Jonathan Blazek et al.. Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary: This paper investigates why Unified Multimodal Models struggle to apply chain-of-thought reasoning effectively to image generation tasks, identifying a fundamental mismatch between discrete token-space reasoning and continuous-space image generation as the root cause. To address this, the authors propose LARC (Latent Reasoning in Continuous space), a framework that performs reasoning over continuous hidden states rather than discrete tokens, thereby eliminating the token-level bottleneck. The training pipeline proceeds in two stages: a curriculum supervised fine-tuning stage that gradually transitions from token-level to latent reasoning, followed by an information-gain reinforcement learning stage that refines latent reasoning without requiring ground truth supervision. Evaluated across multiple text-to-image generation benchmarks, LARC consistently improves generation quality, prompt adherence, and compositional fidelity, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the GenEval benchmark with a notable margin over prior work. Critically, unlike token-based approaches, LARC exhibits clear test-time scaling behavior under both parallel and sequential scaling strategies, bringing image generation closer to the scaling properties observed in large language models.
items.citation: Byungwoo Jeon, Yoonwoo Jeong, Hyunseok Lee et al.. Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational challenge of applying attention mechanisms to ultra-long context sequences exceeding one million tokens, where standard full attention becomes prohibitively expensive due to its quadratic scaling. The authors introduce Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), a method that hierarchically clusters keys in a learned latent space so that queries score clusters rather than individual keys, reducing the cost of prefill, decode, and training. Two variants are proposed: a distillation-based approach that can be applied to existing pre-trained models, and a natively trained variant that learns solely from next-token prediction. When applied to large language models at extreme context lengths, LSA achieves dramatic speedups in both prefill and decode stages compared to full attention and prior sparse attention methods, while maintaining comparable accuracy across diverse tasks. The work demonstrates that hierarchical indexing in a latent space offers a practical path toward subquadratic attention for models operating over ultra-long contexts.
items.citation: Ales Kubicek, Andrea Caciolai, Liangzu Peng et al.. Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of long-horizon planning for embodied agents, where cumulative errors and search complexity degrade performance in existing world model approaches. The authors introduce ID-WM, a hierarchical world model that separates high-level state-space reachability from low-level motor control by pairing a high-level model that samples feasible transitions across the state manifold with a low-level inverse dynamics solver that translates those transitions into precise actions. This decoupling allows the planner to identify reachable subgoals without being constrained by execution details, enabling the synthesis of novel long-horizon plans from short segments that generalize beyond behavioral patterns seen during training. The framework was evaluated across navigation and manipulation benchmarks, showing substantial improvements over both state-of-the-art policy and diffusion-based planners as well as single-level world model model-predictive control, particularly in complex, unseen configurations.
items.citation: Gaoyue Zhou, Yvonne Wu, Zichen Jeff Cui et al.. Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Non-sofic Tarski monsters
items.summary: This paper investigates the existence and structure of non-sofic groups, particularly those that are minimal with respect to this property. The authors construct non-sofic Tarski monsters of every sufficiently large prime exponent as well as torsion-free non-sofic Tarski monsters, combining results from the work of several predecessors on quotient theorems and properties of sofic groups. Because all proper subgroups of Tarski monsters are cyclic, these groups are minimal non-sofic, and additional results yield continuum many pairwise non-quasi-isometric torsion-free simple examples as well as non-simple minimal non-sofic groups of prime power exponent. The paper further studies descending chains of non-sofic subgroups in other group-theoretic constructions, establishing proper self-embeddings for several explicitly defined groups including Leavitt unit groups and higher Brin–Thompson groups. The authors show that certain wreath product and doubling constructions are locally graded and are characterized as being ω-non-sofic while containing no minimal non-sofic subgroup.
items.citation: Kıvanç Ersoy. Non-sofic Tarski monsters. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Revisiting the use of adenosine deaminase in cerebrospinal fluid analysis for infectious meningoencephalitis.
items.summary: This study investigated the diagnostic utility of adenosine deaminase levels measured in cerebrospinal fluid across a range of central nervous system infections, including in patients with HIV and tropical diseases where this biomarker had been insufficiently characterized. Researchers analyzed cerebrospinal fluid adenosine deaminase levels alongside other laboratory parameters in over two hundred patients with various confirmed microbiological diagnoses, comparing results against a non-infectious control group and defining optimal diagnostic cutoff values. Significantly elevated cerebrospinal fluid adenosine deaminase levels were found specifically in tuberculous meningitis and meningococcal meningitis compared to controls, while other infectious etiologies did not show the same pattern. The enzyme levels correlated positively with cerebrospinal fluid protein and weakly negatively with cerebrospinal fluid glucose, and higher cutoff values were identified in cases of central nervous system coinfection. The authors conclude that cerebrospinal fluid adenosine deaminase can serve as a supportive, though not definitive, diagnostic tool for suspected tuberculous meningitis, meningococcal meningitis, and central nervous system coinfections, with the caveat that its moderate sensitivity and specificity limit standalone diagnostic application.
items.citation: Farias LABG, Neto OMV, Sobrinho EPL et al.. Revisiting the use of adenosine deaminase in cerebrospinal fluid analysis for infectious meningoencephalitis.. Arquivos de neuro-psiquiatria. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic Performance of the FilmArray BCID2 Multiplex PCR Panel Applied to Excised Heart Valve Specimens from Patients with Infective Endocarditis.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether the FilmArray Blood Culture Identification 2 multiplex PCR panel, a tool designed for blood culture use, could be applied off-label directly to excised heart valve tissue from patients undergoing surgery for infective endocarditis. The researchers compared the panel's results against both blood culture and conventional valve culture results from a surgical cohort. When benchmarked against blood culture, the assay showed moderate sensitivity but low specificity and poor overall agreement, while comparison against valve culture revealed very low sensitivity alongside perfect specificity. The findings indicate that although the BCID2 panel may serve as a complementary diagnostic tool in certain patients, a negative result cannot reliably exclude infective endocarditis. The authors conclude that larger multicentre studies are needed before this off-label approach can be routinely recommended in clinical practice.
items.citation: Bilewska A, Skrzeczyńska J, Dorota M et al.. Diagnostic Performance of the FilmArray BCID2 Multiplex PCR Panel Applied to Excised Heart Valve Specimens from Patients with Infective Endocarditis.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: A Rapid Molecular Detection Method for Streptococcus agalactiae Based on Bacteriophage Lysin Lysis and Real-Time PCR.
items.summary: This study developed a rapid point-of-care molecular assay for detecting Group B Streptococcus, a leading cause of neonatal infections, to address the limitations of conventional culture methods that require up to two days. The method used a bacteriophage lysin to lyse bacterial cells and extract nucleic acids within five minutes, followed by real-time fluorescence quantitative PCR targeting the GBS cylA gene, completing the entire detection process in approximately thirty-five minutes. The assay was validated across two clinical cohorts using vaginal swab samples, with performance compared against conventional culture and antigen testing. The assay demonstrated complete sensitivity in both cohorts and high specificity, with adjusted specificity improving after sequencing confirmation of discordant samples, and substantially outperformed antigen testing in sensitivity. The authors conclude that this bacteriophage lysin-based molecular assay holds promise for intrapartum or near-patient GBS screening, though further validation in real-world clinical workflows is needed.

items.citation: Zhu H, Zeng X, Huang X et al.. A Rapid Molecular Detection Method for Streptococcus agalactiae Based on Bacteriophage Lysin Lysis and Real-Time PCR.. items.title: Temporal trends in pediatric group A streptococcal pharyngitis across the coronavirus disease 2019 era: A large retrospective cohort study.
items.summary: This study examined how the COVID-19 pandemic and its associated non-pharmaceutical interventions affected the epidemiology of Group A Streptococcus pharyngitis in children. Using a large retrospective cohort of pediatric patients presenting with suspected acute tonsillopharyngitis at a tertiary outpatient clinic spanning pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods, researchers compared positivity rates and used multivariable logistic regression to identify independent predictors of Group A Streptococcus infection. Positivity rates increased progressively across all three periods, rising from the pre-pandemic era through the pandemic and reaching their highest level in the post-pandemic period. Older age and male sex were also independently associated with a greater likelihood of testing positive. The authors conclude that these trends likely reflect a combination of shifting healthcare utilization, diagnostic practices, age distributions, and transmission dynamics, and emphasize the need for ongoing epidemiological surveillance.
items.venue: The Journal of international medical research
items.citation: Nas Y, Gözüküçük S, Bayırlı H et al.. Temporal trends in pediatric group A streptococcal pharyngitis across the coronavirus disease 2019 era: A large retrospective cohort study.. The Journal of international medical research. 2026

items.title: Clinical Relevance of Multiplex PCR for Respiratory Pathogens in Hospitalized Adults with Influenza-Like Illness.
items.summary: This study examined the clinical utility of multiplex PCR testing in hospitalized adults presenting with influenza-like illness by identifying a broad range of respiratory pathogens and correlating findings with clinical, laboratory, and radiological data. Researchers retrospectively analyzed patients admitted over a single respiratory season, using a multiplex real-time PCR assay capable of detecting numerous viral and bacterial pathogens, alongside disease severity scoring and imaging. Respiratory pathogens were identified in less than half of patients, with *Streptococcus pneumoniae*, influenza viruses, and seasonal coronaviruses being the most common, and influenza A co-detected with *S. pneumoniae* representing the most frequent co-infection. Among patients with pneumococcal PCR positivity, those who also had radiologically confirmed pneumonia were older, had greater disease severity, and more commonly had concurrent influenza infection compared to those without radiological evidence of pneumonia. The authors conclude that while multiplex molecular assays offer valuable pathogen detection, results for bacterial pathogens like *S. pneumoniae* must be interpreted in conjunction with clinical and radiological findings rather than in isolation.
items.venue: Journal of clinical practice and research
items.citation: Gülseren YD, Aydın D, Çetin Duran A. Clinical Relevance of Multiplex PCR for Respiratory Pathogens in Hospitalized Adults with Influenza-Like Illness.. Journal of clinical practice and research. 2026

items.title: Rapid molecular culture versus conventional culture for periprosthetic joint infection: diagnostic performance and clinical relevance.
items.summary: This study evaluated a rapid PCR-based assay called Molecular Culture as a diagnostic tool for periprosthetic joint infection, comparing its performance to conventional microbiological culture using sonication fluid collected during hip and knee revision arthroplasty. Samples were retrospectively analysed and classified according to established infection criteria, with results assessed both analytically and after clinical correlation incorporating antibiotic exposure history and all available microbiological data. The rapid assay delivered results within approximately four hours compared to the prolonged turnaround of conventional culture, and after clinical correlation demonstrated high negative percentage agreement, suggesting it reliably excludes infection. The assay also identified additional clinically relevant pathogens that conventional culture missed, particularly in patients who had received prior antimicrobial therapy. The authors conclude that Molecular Culture performs well as an adjunctive diagnostic tool, with its greatest utility in patients with uncertain infection status or prior antibiotic exposure, where rapid results could support earlier and more targeted antimicrobial decision-making.
items.venue: Journal of bone and joint infection
items.citation: Morreel E, Savelkoul P, van Loo I. Rapid molecular culture versus conventional culture for periprosthetic joint infection: diagnostic performance and clinical relevance.. Journal of bone and joint infection. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviews advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over a five-year period, with findings used to inform updated WHO policy guidance that consolidates recommendations for detecting tuberculosis disease and drug resistance into a single unified framework. Key diagnostic developments include the expanded role of digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection as a frontline screening tool, and the broadened deployment of decentralised molecular diagnostics such as low-complexity automated and manual nucleic acid amplification tests across diverse specimen types. Improvements in testing using non-sputum specimens, including stool, gastric aspirate, and nasopharyngeal samples, along with novel approaches such as tongue swabs and sputum pooling, have enhanced bacteriological confirmation particularly in children and others who cannot produce sputum. Drug-resistance testing has progressed through dedicated molecular platforms and targeted next-generation sequencing, now endorsed for comprehensive susceptibility profiling at reference laboratory level, while urine-based lipoarabinomannan assays provide incremental benefit in people with HIV and advanced disease. Despite these advances, the authors identify persistent performance, implementation, and equity gaps, and note that no biomarker has yet met WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027
