items.title: Finger-actuated microfluidic device for point-of-care circulating cell-free nucleic acid extraction.
items.summary: This paper developed a fully finger-actuated microfluidic device designed to extract low-abundance cell-free nucleic acids from plasma at the point of care without requiring external power or laboratory equipment. The device integrates manual valves, a finger-driven pump, and blister packs for reagent storage, enabling a complete sample-to-eluate workflow covering lysis, binding, washing, and elution through simple manual operation. Performance was benchmarked against both a commercial manual benchtop method and an automated robotic workflow using DNA-spiked aqueous samples and human pooled plasma, with the device achieving recovery rates comparable to or exceeding the bench extraction method, particularly at lower input plasma volumes. Clinical utility was demonstrated using patient samples positive for cytomegalovirus, monkeypox virus, and chikungunya virus, with quantitative PCR cycle quantification values closely matching those obtained by standard protocols. The authors conclude that this instrument-free extraction tool could help close the gap between existing nucleic acid amplification technologies and decentralized diagnostics in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Musaddaq G, Ehsan L, Yoga Y et al.. Finger-actuated microfluidic device for point-of-care circulating cell-free nucleic acid extraction.. Lab on a chip. 2026

items.title: Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.
items.summary: This review paper examines the current landscape and recent advances in molecular diagnostic methods used to identify and characterize pathogens responsible for infectious diseases. The two primary goals discussed are detecting pathogen genetic material through nucleic acid amplification techniques and characterizing pathogen properties using sequencing technologies. The paper covers developments in polymerase chain reaction variants optimized for speed, quantification, automation, and point-of-care use, as well as isothermal amplification methods that operate without thermal cycling and are therefore well suited to decentralized testing settings. CRISPR-based detection systems and their combination with isothermal amplification are highlighted as emerging diagnostic tools, alongside next-generation sequencing, which enables detection of novel pathogens, outbreak tracking, monitoring of pathogen evolution, and microbiome analysis relevant to disease susceptibility. The authors conclude that the future of molecular infectious disease diagnostics lies in integrating these complementary technologies into hybrid platforms that overcome the individual limitations of each approach.
items.citation: Takata M, Chikumi H, Yoshifuji A. Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.. Yonago acta medica. 2026

items.title: QMini: A Portable Device for Infectious Disease Testing.
items.summary: The paper studied the development of a portable device for nucleic acid-based infectious disease testing that could overcome the size limitations of conventional laboratory instruments. The researchers built the QMini by simplifying its fluidic module through direct connections between pumps and reaction chambers and shielding its optical module from ambient light using a three-dimensional-printed enclosure. They tested the device using a bead-based assay with quantum dot barcodes to detect synthetic nucleic acid sequences from respiratory syncytial virus B, SARS-CoV-2, and influenza A. The device successfully detected these pathogens at low copy numbers and showed limited cross-reactivity against nontarget viral nucleic acid sequences, demonstrating strong specificity. The authors conclude that the QMini advances the portability of quantum dot barcode-based nucleic acid testing through meaningful device miniaturization.
items.citation: Mahbub N, Osborne M, Chen H et al.. QMini: A Portable Device for Infectious Disease Testing.. ACS nanoscience Au. 2026

items.title: Molecular Detection of Feline Hemotropic <i>Mycoplasma</i> from Blood Samples of Sick Cats: A Comparative Study Between a Commercial Nucleic Acid Test Card and Conventional Polymerase Chain Reaction.
items.summary: This study evaluated a commercial nucleic acid test card for diagnosing feline hemotropic mycoplasmosis, a condition caused by blood-parasitizing *Mycoplasma* species that is difficult to detect reliably with conventional blood smear examination. Whole blood samples from clinically ill cats presenting to a veterinary teaching hospital in Thailand were tested using both the commercial card assay and conventional polymerase chain reaction targeting the 16S rRNA gene as a reference standard. Among the tested cats, *'Candidatus* Mycoplasma haemominutum' was identified as the predominant species, with *Mycoplasma haemofelis* and *'Candidatus* Mycoplasma turicensis'* also detected at lower frequencies. The commercial assay showed high sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy compared to conventional PCR, delivering results within thirty minutes, with false-negative results attributed to low bacterial burdens in discordant samples. The authors conclude that the Pluslife® FHM nucleic acid test card represents a practical and rapid point-of-care molecular diagnostic tool suitable for timely clinical decision-making in cats suspected of hemotropic mycoplasmosis.
items.citation: Nimsuphan B, Ruenphet S, Kengradomkij C et al.. Molecular Detection of Feline Hemotropic <i>Mycoplasma</i> from Blood Samples of Sick Cats: A Comparative Study Between a Commercial Nucleic Acid Test Card and Conventional Polymerase Chain Reaction.. Veterinary sciences. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review paper examines the intersection of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence as applied to precision drug discovery and clinical medicine. The authors survey how approaches such as genome-wide association studies, transcriptomic profiling, proteomic interaction mapping, and metabolomic sequencing generate deep insight into disease mechanisms, and how deep learning architectures can extract meaningful patterns from these complex biological datasets. The review covers the application of this combined framework across the drug development pipeline, including target identification, drug repositioning, de novo compound design, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. The authors highlight disease areas such as oncology, neurodegeneration, and cardiovascular conditions as illustrative domains, while also acknowledging persistent challenges including data harmonization, reproducibility, and algorithmic bias. Overall, the paper argues that the convergence of multiomics and artificial intelligence represents a foundational shift toward more precise, data-driven therapeutic development and translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective
items.summary: This paper examines the regulatory landscape governing cell-derived extracellular vesicles as therapeutic and diagnostic products across major global jurisdictions. The authors critically analyze how EVs map onto existing medicinal product frameworks, noting that their acellular nature creates classification ambiguities, particularly in light of recent European guidance clarifying that minimally modified EVs fall outside the advanced therapy medicinal products definition, while other regions apply their own jurisdiction-specific criteria. The review identifies key operational challenges including inconsistent classification criteria, undefined critical quality attributes, potency assessment strategies, and comparability requirements that complicate cross-regional clinical development. Rather than proposing new normative frameworks, the authors argue that EVs should be developed within existing biologics and related medicinal product instruments, provided these are applied consistently and areas of regulatory ambiguity are systematically clarified. The work is intended to support regulatory dialogue among international agencies and scientific societies to advance EV-based therapies toward safe, reproducible, and globally credible clinical use.
items.citation: Tania Limongi, Paola Milla, Barbara Stella et al.. Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective. Journal of Extracellular Vesicles. 2026

items.title: Lethal plague outbreaks in Lake Baikal hunter-gatherers 5,500 years ago
items.summary: This paper investigated the early history of plague caused by *Yersinia pestis* among prehistoric hunter-gatherer populations near Lake Baikal in Siberia. The researchers analyzed ancient DNA from individuals buried across four cemeteries, identifying plague infections and reconstructing kinship relationships among the affected individuals. They found evidence of two phases of lethal outbreaks beginning approximately five and a half thousand years ago, with an exceptionally high detection rate for plague infection and acute mortality particularly concentrated among children. The newly identified strains diverge ancestrally from all previously known *Y. pestis* lineages, pushing back the estimated emergence of the bacterium and revealing functional genetic differences including at a superantigen locus shared with the related bacterium *Yersinia pseudotuberculosis*. Critically, because these devastating outbreaks occurred among low-density hunter-gatherer communities rather than agriculturalists, the findings challenge the long-held assumption that increased population density and the Neolithic farming transition were necessary preconditions for plague epidemics.
items.citation: Ruairidh Macleod, Frederik Valeur Seersholm, Bianca De Sanctis et al.. Lethal plague outbreaks in Lake Baikal hunter-gatherers 5,500 years ago. Nature. 2026

items.title: Pulmonary inflammation in severe pneumonia is characterised by compartmentalised and mechanistically distinct sub-phenotypes
items.summary: This paper investigated the biological basis of severe pneumonia requiring critical care, an area where the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood despite the disease's global burden. The researchers performed comprehensive analysis of bronchoalveolar samples from patients with suspected severe pneumonia, examining transcriptomics, cytokines, microbiology, and clinical features together. They identified three distinct lung-restricted transcriptional endotypes, termed Pneumotypes, that share similar clinical presentations and severity of respiratory failure but differ markedly in their immunological and cellular characteristics and in patient outcomes. The most common endotype is defined by low alveolar cytokines, expanded tolerogenic macrophages, and epithelial damage; a second endotype shows the fastest resolution with a balanced immune response and repair signatures; and a third is characterised by immature neutrophil infiltration, IL-6-STAT3 pathway activation, and prolonged mechanical ventilation. The authors propose that these mechanistically distinct phenotypes could serve as the basis for personalised therapeutic strategies in severe pneumonia and acute lung injury.
items.citation: Mark Jeffrey, Josefin Bartholdson Scott, Shyamanova Mazumdar et al.. Pulmonary inflammation in severe pneumonia is characterised by compartmentalised and mechanistically distinct sub-phenotypes. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic yield of reflex multiplex PCR after a negative rapid antigen test in children hospitalized with presumed viral acute respiratory tract infection: a prospective cohort study.
items.summary: This study investigated whether adding reflex multiplex PCR testing after a negative rapid antigen test improves viral detection in children hospitalized with presumed viral acute respiratory infections. In a single-center prospective cohort, children first underwent a five-target rapid antigen test, and those who tested negative were selectively referred for broader multiplex PCR at physician discretion. Reflex PCR substantially increased the diagnostic yield, with the large majority of antigen-negative children who underwent PCR testing returning a positive result, and rhinovirus/enterovirus—not covered by the antigen panel—emerged as the most commonly identified pathogen. The study found that antigen testing alone captured only a minority of ultimately identified viral cases, demonstrating that a negative antigen test cannot reliably exclude respiratory viral infection in this population. Antibiotic use was high across the cohort regardless of whether a virus was detected, though the authors note that appropriateness of antibiotic prescribing could not be fully evaluated without systematic bacterial testing.
items.citation: Bedir AZ, Saf C, Yörük MA. Diagnostic yield of reflex multiplex PCR after a negative rapid antigen test in children hospitalized with presumed viral acute respiratory tract infection: a prospective cohort study.. Irish journal of medical science. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of the RapidFor™ RSV/ADV Rapid Test Kit Compared with PCR for the Detection of Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Adenovirus in Nasopharyngeal Swab Samples
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of the RapidFor™ RSV/ADV Rapid Test Kit for detecting respiratory syncytial virus and adenovirus in children presenting to a pediatric emergency department with acute respiratory symptoms. Using multiplex real-time PCR as the reference standard, researchers prospectively collected paired nasopharyngeal swabs from pediatric patients and compared point-of-care rapid antigen test results against PCR findings, also examining diagnostic performance by age group and identifying clinical predictors of each pathogen. The rapid test demonstrated very high sensitivity and specificity for both adenovirus and RSV, with excellent agreement with PCR for each pathogen. Age-related patterns were observed, with RSV predominantly affecting infants under one year and adenovirus peaking in school-aged children; conjunctival injection and fever independently predicted adenovirus positivity, while cough and infant age predicted RSV positivity. The authors conclude that this dual-pathogen rapid test may reliably support timely clinical decision-making in pediatric emergency settings without requiring laboratory-based PCR infrastructure.
items.citation: Ates B, Kacar A, Kok S et al.. Diagnostic Accuracy of the RapidFor™ RSV/ADV Rapid Test Kit Compared with PCR for the Detection of Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Adenovirus in Nasopharyngeal Swab Samples. 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examines a central controversy in exercise immunology: whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection, independent of confounding factors. The paper contrasts the established view that moderate, short-duration exercise benefits immune defense with the observation that high-performance athletes and military personnel experience high infection burdens, which has traditionally been attributed to arduous training suppressing immunity. Opposing expert groups contested whether athletes are genuinely more infection-prone than the general population, whether exercise alone can drive increased infection risk separately from co-occurring stressors such as sleep disruption, nutritional deficits, anxiety, and travel, and whether the biomarkers and study designs used in the field adequately capture immune health. Both sides agreed that infection susceptibility is multifactorial in origin, but could not resolve whether exercise is itself a causative factor in elevated infection risk among athletes. The authors conclude that the question remains open and call for more rigorous empirical research to disentangle the specific immunological effects of arduous exercise from the broader lifestyle and environmental context in which it occurs.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Spinal cord injury: Known and possible influences on the immune response to exercise
items.summary: This review paper examined how spinal cord injury affects immune function, with a particular focus on the immune response to exercise. The authors conducted a comprehensive literature search to gather existing studies on exercise immunology across patient, recreationally active, and athlete populations with spinal cord injury. The paper found that spinal cord injury can suppress immunity through multiple pathways, including reduced lymphocyte numbers, autonomic dysfunction, and altered catecholamine concentrations, with these effects being especially pronounced in individuals with tetraplegia. However, certain immune responses to exercise, such as increased natural killer cell cytotoxicity and mucosal immunity in tetraplegic individuals, appeared to be preserved or even comparable to able-bodied populations, suggesting that compensatory mechanisms such as sympathetic reflex activity, receptor hypersensitivity, or neuroendocrine adjustments may offset some disability-related immune deficits. The authors conclude that exercise and rehabilitation therapy hold potential as tools to maintain or improve immune and autonomic function in individuals with spinal cord injury, while calling for further research to clarify the underlying mechanisms.
items.citation: Christof A. Leicht, Victoria Louise Goosey-Tolfrey, NICOLETTE CLAIRE BISHOP. Spinal cord injury: Known and possible influences on the immune response to exercise. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Understanding graft-versus-host disease. Preliminary findings regarding the effects of exercise in affected patients
items.summary: This paper examines graft-versus-host disease, a serious multi-systemic complication arising when donor lymphocytes attack host tissues following allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, with particular focus on its chronic form and the resulting physical impairments. The authors reviewed the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the disease alongside available evidence from both animal and human studies on exercise as a potential adjunct therapy. Their synthesis suggests that exercise training holds promise for improving physical fitness, attenuating fatigue, and possibly enhancing immune function in affected patients. However, the authors conclude that the current evidence base is insufficient and that well-designed randomized controlled trials specifically targeting this patient population are needed to confirm these preliminary findings.
items.citation: Carmen Fiuza‐Luces, Nuria Garatachea, Nathan A. Berger et al.. Understanding graft-versus-host disease. Preliminary findings regarding the effects of exercise in affected patients. PubMed. 2026

items.title: EHA Guidelines on management of chronic lymphocytic leukemia and Richter transformation
items.summary: These guidelines address the clinical management of chronic lymphocytic leukemia and, for the first time explicitly, Richter transformation, representing an updated and restructured framework developed under the European Hematology Association rather than its previous sponsoring body. The guidelines adopt a holistic approach spanning initial diagnosis and active surveillance through treatment decision-making, with emphasis on integrating both disease-specific and patient-specific factors. New treatment recommendations incorporate recently approved therapies, including a time-limited combination regimen for first-line treatment and a next-generation inhibitor for patients who have progressed after covalent Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy. Notably, the guideline development process involved patient advocacy representatives alongside medical experts from multiple European countries for the first time, and the guidelines are intended to be updated annually to reflect the rapidly evolving evidence base in this field.
items.citation: Barbara F. Eichhorst, Paolo Ghia, Francesc Bosch et al.. EHA Guidelines on management of chronic lymphocytic leukemia and Richter transformation. HemaSphere. 2026

items.title: Human lung organoid modelling of tissue-resident antiviral T cell responses
items.summary: This paper investigated tissue-resident immune responses in human lung, particularly the behavior of tissue-resident memory T cells during respiratory viral infection. The researchers developed long-term adult human distal lung organoids from intact tissue fragments using a three-dimensional air-liquid interface culture system that preserved both the epithelial and stromal architecture as well as endogenous resident immune cells including T, B, NK, and myeloid cells. The organoid T cells maintained residency and memory markers, responded to cytokine support, and retained T cell receptor repertoires matching those of fresh donor tissue. When the organoids were infected with SARS-CoV-2, the virus productively infected the lung epithelium, triggered inflammatory cytokine production, and elicited virus-specific tissue-resident T cell responses without input from secondary lymphoid organs. These findings demonstrate that the lung itself is autonomously sufficient to mount adaptive memory T cell responses to pathogens, and the platform offers a physiologically relevant system for studying tissue-resident immunity in human respiratory disease.
items.citation: Joseph K. Rathkey, S. S. Choi, Vincent van Unen et al.. Human lung organoid modelling of tissue-resident antiviral T cell responses. Nature. 2026

items.title: Survival and physiological status of Escherichia coli in lake water under different nutrient conditions
items.summary: This study investigated how *Escherichia coli* survives in lake water under varying nutrient availability, temperature, and stress conditions, using both natural and sterile microcosms. The researchers measured bacterial survival counts alongside physiological indicators including metabolic enzyme activities, cell size, respiratory activity, and protein expression patterns over extended incubation periods. Temperature was found to be a critical determinant of survival, with the longest persistence occurring at low temperatures and the shortest at body temperature, while predation by protozoa played a negligible role. Despite viable counts dropping below detectable limits under starvation, a substantial proportion of cells retained respiratory activity, providing evidence that *E. coli* enters a viable but non-culturable state in lake water. Starvation and other stress conditions triggered specific proteomic responses, including alterations in outer membrane protein composition and induction of particular stress proteins, suggesting that survival under environmental stress is linked to coordinated changes in protein expression.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Reşit Özkanca. Survival and physiological status of Escherichia coli in lake water under different nutrient conditions. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments
items.summary: This paper investigates intrinsic alignments of galaxies, which represent both a systematic contaminant in weak gravitational lensing surveys and a probe of galaxy formation physics. The authors developed model-agnostic tests to examine how density-weighting affects alignment signals, applying these to data from the IllustrisTNG cosmological hydrodynamical simulation and an observational galaxy survey. They found that density-weighting primarily amplifies alignment amplitude on large scales, while its effect on small scales depends on the specific galaxy sample examined. Additionally, by correlating galaxy shapes with tidal fields derived from the simulation, they assessed whether the standard tidal alignment paradigm holds, finding that central galaxies align linearly with the underlying non-linear tidal field even within the one-halo regime. These results suggest that the linear tidal alignment model captures galaxy orientation behavior across a broader range of scales than previously assumed, while also highlighting density-weighting as an important consideration for alignment modeling.
items.citation: Paul Rogozenski, Sukhdeep Singh, Jonathan Blazek et al.. Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary: This paper investigates why Unified Multimodal Models struggle to benefit from chain-of-thought reasoning during image generation, identifying a fundamental mismatch between discrete token-space reasoning and continuous-space image generation as the core problem. To address this, the authors propose LARC, a Latent Reasoning in Continuous space framework that performs reasoning over continuous hidden states rather than discrete tokens. The training approach comprises two stages: a curriculum supervised fine-tuning stage that progressively transitions token-level reasoning into latent reasoning, followed by an information-gain reinforcement learning stage that refines latent reasoning without requiring ground truth supervision. Evaluations across text-to-image generation benchmarks demonstrate that LARC improves generation quality, prompt following, and compositional fidelity, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the GenEval benchmark with a notable gain over a strong baseline. Critically, LARC exhibits test-time scaling behavior under both parallel and sequential strategies, a property previously absent from reasoning-augmented unified multimodal models.
items.citation: Byungwoo Jeon, Yoonwoo Jeong, Hyunseok Lee et al.. Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently running decision models—a class of lightweight language model agents designed for rapid categorical reasoning—within existing inference infrastructure. The authors identify that current generation-oriented inference engines impose severe prefix recomputation overhead or introduce numerical distortions in output probabilities when handling the tree-structured branching logic characteristic of decision workloads. To solve this, they developed Flide, an inference engine that separates the logical tree structure of a decision request from its physical execution by flattening it into a single token stream and using a mechanism called ForkAttention, which navigates branch dependencies via GPU-resident indices across both standard attention and recurrent network layers. Flide encodes branch topologies directly in GPU metadata and supports resumption from checkpoints, enabling efficient handling of diverse and evolving agent histories. Evaluations on hybrid and decision models show that Flide achieves substantially faster query answering than existing systems while maintaining numerical fidelity closest to a high-precision reference, positioning it as a principled foundation for latency-critical agent decision-making at scale.
items.citation: Bobo Li, Jiajia Song, Hao Fei et al.. Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of long-horizon planning for embodied agents, where cumulative errors and search complexity degrade performance in existing world model approaches. The authors introduce ID-WM, a hierarchical world model framework that separates high-level state-space reachability from low-level control by pairing a high-level model that samples feasible transitions across the state manifold with a low-level inverse dynamics solver that grounds those transitions into concrete actions. This decoupling allows the planner to identify reachable subgoals without being constrained by low-level execution details, enabling the system to compose novel long-horizon plans from short segments and generalize beyond behavioral modes seen during training. Evaluated across navigation and manipulation benchmarks, the framework substantially outperforms both state-of-the-art policy and diffusion-based planners, with particularly large gains over single-level model predictive control in complex, unseen configurations.
items.citation: Gaoyue Zhou, Yvonne Wu, Zichen Jeff Cui et al.. Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Approximate Polynomial Satisfiability and Integral Closure Membership in the Counting Hierarchy
items.summary: This paper studies the computational complexity of two algebraic problems: approximate polynomial satisfiability (APS), which asks whether a polynomial system is nearly satisfiable over the complex numbers, and integral closure membership testing, which asks whether a polynomial is integral over a given polynomial ring. To place APS in the Counting Hierarchy for rational polynomials represented by arithmetic circuits, the authors combine Noether normalization with a geometric analysis of how points in the image of a polynomial map approach the origin, ultimately reducing APS to a decision problem about multivariate resultants that can be solved within the Counting Hierarchy. For integral closure membership, they apply a global annihilator criterion together with an effective degree bound to reduce non-integrality to APS in polynomial time, thereby placing this problem in the Counting Hierarchy as well. These results improve upon the previously known upper bound of PSPACE for APS and carry implications for geometric complexity theory, where APS had been used to construct hitting sets for an algebraic complexity class. The work complements independent and concurrent results by other research groups addressing related questions.
items.citation: Sanyam Agarwal, Archit Hari, Anurag Pandey et al.. Approximate Polynomial Satisfiability and Integral Closure Membership in the Counting Hierarchy. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Instance-dependent sequential limits as an exact information ledger
items.summary: This paper studies the fundamental performance limits of sequential decision-making problems, including bandit regret, sequential hypothesis testing, best-arm identification, and Markov decision processes. The authors construct a unified proof chain that derives instance-dependent lower bounds across all these settings by linking divergence decompositions, data processing inequalities, and optimization over alternative problem instances. A key contribution is formulating this chain as an exact "ledger" that tracks precisely where information is lost at each step, showing that data processing loses exactly a conditional divergence that vanishes for natural exponential family reward distributions under standard sufficient statistics. The framework also introduces a one-parameter family of martingale identities that extends the decomposition across all tilts between problem instances, with classical lower bounds recovered as relaxations whose associated defects are named and quantified. Empirical analysis on several published datasets reveals that the gap between standard algorithms and classical limits is most commonly dominated by the uniform quantification step, particularly for model selection and Wald's sequential test.
items.citation: Akshay Balsubramani. Instance-dependent sequential limits as an exact information ledger. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Advances in Diagnostic Technologies of Major Avian Respiratory Viruses: A Review.
items.summary: This review examines the diagnostic landscape for four major avian respiratory viruses—avian influenza virus, Newcastle disease virus, infectious bronchitis virus, and infectious laryngotracheitis virus—which pose significant threats to global poultry production and, in some cases, public health. The authors synthesized and compared a broad range of molecular and immunological diagnostic approaches, evaluating them across performance metrics such as sensitivity, multiplexing capability, turnaround time, and suitability for point-of-care use. Molecular methods covered include quantitative PCR and its multiplex formats, isothermal amplification strategies, and CRISPR-Cas-based detection systems, while immunological advances encompass assays enhanced by nanomaterials, recombinant proteins, and single-domain antibodies. High-throughput sequencing, microarray platforms, and integrated portable systems such as microfluidics and smartphone-assisted diagnostics are also assessed. The review concludes by identifying future directions in avian diagnostic technology, aiming to support more efficient and accessible disease surveillance and early warning infrastructure.
items.citation: Hu Z, Hailai A, He H et al.. Advances in Diagnostic Technologies of Major Avian Respiratory Viruses: A Review.. Veterinary sciences. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviews advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over roughly the first half of the 2020s, synthesizing evidence that has informed updated WHO policy guidance consolidating recommendations for tuberculosis detection and drug-resistance testing. Key developments include the expanded role of digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection as a frontline screening tool, and the broadened deployment of decentralised molecular diagnostics such as low-complexity automated and manual nucleic acid amplification tests across diverse specimen types and populations. Progress in drug-resistance testing is highlighted through new molecular platforms and the endorsement of targeted next-generation sequencing for comprehensive susceptibility profiling at reference laboratory level, while expanded use of non-sputum specimens has improved bacteriological confirmation in children and others unable to produce sputum. Host blood transcriptomic and other biomarker classes show promise for prognosis and triage, but no biomarker has yet met WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis. The paper concludes that substantial gaps in diagnostic performance, implementation, and equity remain and identifies these as priority areas for further development.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: Direct RNA Targeting by CRISPR/Cas12: Emerging Mechanisms and Diagnostic Applications.
items.summary: This review examines the emerging capability of CRISPR-Cas12 enzyme variants to directly detect RNA targets, a function previously attributed primarily to Cas13 within CRISPR-based diagnostics. The authors address limitations of conventional RNA detection methods such as RT-PCR, which require reverse transcription, thermal cycling, and complex workflows that hinder rapid and point-of-care applications. The review synthesizes recent findings on how multiple Cas12 variants, including Cas12a, Cas12a2, Cas12a3, Cas12f, and Cas12g, can directly recognize RNA through mechanisms such as RNA-triggered DNase activity, thereby enabling reverse-transcription-free detection. The authors also describe strategies to enhance detection performance, encompassing guide and activator engineering, nanomaterial-assisted signal readouts, and autocatalytic amplification approaches. The review concludes by outlining applications in infectious disease diagnosis, cancer biomarker detection, and environmental monitoring, while identifying key challenges remaining for clinical translation and point-of-care deployment.
items.citation: Hall T, Jia Z, Cai K et al.. Direct RNA Targeting by CRISPR/Cas12: Emerging Mechanisms and Diagnostic Applications.. Critical reviews in analytical chemistry. 2026

items.title: Concordance Between Fingerprick and Venous Whole Blood CD4 Counts Using the Visitect CD4 Advanced Disease Platform.
items.summary: The study evaluated whether fingerprick blood sampling could serve as a reliable alternative to venous whole blood for CD4 testing using the Visitect CD4 Advanced Disease platform, a rapid semi-quantitative assay that classifies CD4 counts as above or below a clinically important threshold. Researchers conducted a prospective validation study directly comparing results obtained from the two sampling methods on the same patients. They found very high agreement between fingerprick and venous whole blood results, supporting the conclusion that fingerprick collection with this platform is a dependable point-of-care diagnostic approach. This finding is particularly relevant for resource-limited settings where conventional venous blood collection and laboratory infrastructure may not be readily available.
items.citation: Adzemovic T, Nalintya E, Onencan P et al.. Concordance Between Fingerprick and Venous Whole Blood CD4 Counts Using the Visitect CD4 Advanced Disease Platform.. The Journal of infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: Quantum Sensing Technologies for Ultrasensitive Biomarker Detection in Biomedical Diagnostics from Fundamental Principles to Clinical Translation.
items.summary: This review examines quantum sensing technologies as emerging tools for ultrasensitive biomarker detection in biomedical diagnostics, synthesizing findings from a large body of research literature. The authors survey the fundamental quantum mechanical principles underlying several sensor platforms, including nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond, quantum dots, and superconducting quantum interference devices, and assess their applications in detecting biomarkers relevant to cancer, cardiovascular disease, neurological disorders, and infectious diseases. Quantum-enhanced biosensors are reported to achieve detection limits orders of magnitude below those of conventional diagnostic methods, reaching single-molecule and attomolar sensitivity. The review also critically evaluates the technical barriers impeding clinical translation of these platforms and highlights progress toward point-of-care diagnostics, early disease detection, and personalized medicine, including early commercialization efforts for select technologies.
items.citation: Krishnamoorthy U. Quantum Sensing Technologies for Ultrasensitive Biomarker Detection in Biomedical Diagnostics from Fundamental Principles to Clinical Translation.. ACS sensors. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping the drug discovery and precision medicine landscape. The authors synthesize how genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic approaches generate deep molecular insights into disease mechanisms, and how deep learning architectures can decode these complex, high-dimensional datasets to reveal biological patterns and build predictive models. The review analyzes the combined application of these tools across the drug development pipeline, covering target identification, drug repositioning, de novo compound discovery, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment, with particular focus on oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions. The authors argue that this convergence accelerates therapeutic innovation and enables more precise clinical trial design, while also acknowledging persistent challenges including harmonization of disparate omics data, reproducibility concerns, and mitigation of algorithmic bias. Overall, the paper presents a forward-looking vision for translational medicine in which multiomics and artificial intelligence together enable a more comprehensive molecular understanding and more targeted therapeutic interventions.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective
items.summary: This paper examines the regulatory landscape governing cell-derived extracellular vesicles as therapeutic and diagnostic products, with a focus on inconsistencies between jurisdictions that complicate clinical development. The authors analyzed how existing medicinal product frameworks in the European Union, United States, Japan, and other regions classify and oversee extracellular vesicle-based products, noting that their acellular nature does not map cleanly onto established regulatory categories. A recent European guideline clarifying that minimally modified extracellular vesicles fall outside advanced therapy medicinal product definitions contrasts with the approach of other regulators, producing heterogeneous classification criteria, quality standards, and comparability requirements across regions. The paper identifies operational grey zones—including critical quality attributes, potency strategies, and comparability assessments—that need clarification without prescribing new normative frameworks. The authors argue that consistent application of existing biologics and related medicinal product instruments, combined with greater international regulatory dialogue and methodological convergence, is necessary to advance extracellular vesicle therapies toward safe and reproducible clinical use.
items.citation: Tania Limongi, Paola Milla, Barbara Stella et al.. Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective. Journal of Extracellular Vesicles. 2026

items.title: A framework for developing university policies on generative AI governance: a cross-national comparative study
items.summary: This study examined how universities in the United States, Japan, and China are developing institutional policies to govern the use of generative AI in higher education, focusing on ethical, pedagogical, and institutional dimensions. The researchers conducted a cross-national comparative analysis of guidelines issued by leading universities across these three countries, applying an extended Technology Acceptance Model as an analytical lens and using thematic coding to identify key themes across five policy domains. The analysis revealed distinct national orientations: universities in the United States prioritized faculty autonomy, practical application, and policy flexibility; Japanese institutions adopted a government-aligned approach emphasizing ethics and risk management but offering limited implementation guidance; and Chinese institutions reflected a centralized, government-led model oriented toward technology application and active integration in education and research. Drawing on these comparative findings, the researchers proposed the University Policy Development Framework for Generative AI, which integrates technological, organizational, and social dimensions to help institutions balance innovation with risk and build capacity for sustainable governance. The framework is intended to support universities globally in assessing policy priorities and navigating the evolving challenges of AI governance in higher education.
items.citation: Ming Li, Qin Xie, Ariunaa Enkhtur et al.. A framework for developing university policies on generative AI governance: a cross-national comparative study. Studies in Higher Education. 2026

items.title: Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support
items.summary: This review paper examines the application of federated learning as a privacy-preserving approach to training artificial intelligence models across diverse healthcare data modalities, including biomedical imaging, electronic health records, wearable sensor outputs, and clinical decision support systems. Rather than centralizing sensitive patient data, federated learning allows institutions to train models locally and share only model updates, reducing direct exposure of raw clinical information while maintaining regulatory alignment across distributed healthcare environments. The authors conducted a broad literature review spanning multiple healthcare domains, including chronic disease management, elder care, and physiological signal analysis, synthesizing both the demonstrated successes and the persistent limitations of federated learning in practice. Key barriers identified include system heterogeneity, data imbalance across participating institutions, communication bottlenecks, vulnerability to attacks such as gradient leakage and model inversion, and fairness concerns that complicate equitable deployment. The paper concludes by offering practical recommendations directed at regulators, developers, and healthcare systems to advance the safe and equitable implementation of federated learning across geographical boundaries in medicine.
items.venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
items.citation: Shon G. Nemane, Vaishnavi M. Sarad, Dhiraj P. Tulaskar et al.. Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support. Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering. 2026

items.title: Think in 360°: Benchmarking and Bootstrapping Panoramic Video Reasoning
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of understanding panoramic videos, where relevant visual evidence can appear in any direction and at any point in time, requiring models to integrate observations across the full viewing sphere and temporal dimension. The authors introduce a manually annotated benchmark comprising a thousand questions across multiple categories and question types, along with diagnostic annotations designed to probe spatial search and panoramic-specific capabilities. Evaluating a diverse set of proprietary, open-source, and panoramic-specialized models revealed that cross-view tracking and sphere-time evidence integration represent the most significant weaknesses across existing systems. To address these gaps, the authors constructed a large reasoning dataset grounded in real panoramic video by converting verified panoramic observations and successful agentic explorations into question-answer chain-of-thought pairs, then trained a model using panoramic chain-of-thought supervised fine-tuning combined with an evidence-privileged on-policy self-distillation approach in which a teacher with access to verified perspective views guides student reasoning trajectories. The resulting model substantially outperforms both its backbone and the previous state of the art, with gains concentrated precisely in the spatial, cross-view, and temporal reasoning capabilities that the benchmark identified as deficient, demonstrating that grounded sphere-time supervision can effectively instill panoramic reasoning in a general video multimodal language model.
items.citation: Lidong Lu, Lidong Zou, Xinyi Mao et al.. Think in 360°: Benchmarking and Bootstrapping Panoramic Video Reasoning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Knowledge Layer Model (KLM): Evidence-Visible AI Output, Routing Diagnostics, and Negative Results
items.summary: This paper introduces the Knowledge Layer Model (KLM), a specification designed to make the evidential basis of AI-generated outputs inspectable and auditable, addressing the problem that apparent correctness in AI answers is insufficient without transparent reasoning records. The model provides a framework for versioned epistemic assessments, evidence relations, and explicit representation of unknowns, with a reference implementation described through an associated knowledge and evidence architecture. The paper reports a series of internal empirical experiments, including a routing classification benchmark, configuration tests, diagnostic evaluations, and text-retention checks, though many of these experiments produced null, negative, or methodologically compromised results—such as diagnostic metrics far below acceptable thresholds and capacity comparisons rendered unreliable by defective tooling. The authors explicitly flag limitations throughout, distinguishing historical observations from later reproductions and noting that evidence visibility alone does not establish correctness, causal reliance, or regulatory compliance. Independent replication and a complete public audit package are identified as necessary future work, and the abstract is candid that several proposed evaluations remain unexecuted.
items.citation: Omer Asim Ozturk, Cihan Aydiner. The Knowledge Layer Model (KLM): Evidence-Visible AI Output, Routing Diagnostics, and Negative Results. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice
items.summary: This paper investigated whether large language models provide consistent smoking-cessation advice regardless of who is asking, examining potential disparities driven by user persona characteristics. The researchers systematically audited six widely deployed language models by posing identical cessation questions to twelve distinct user personas varying in life stage, self-described expertise, and smoking history, generating thousands of responses for comparison. They found that model outputs varied substantially based on perceived user identity, with all models mentioning FDA-approved prescription medications far less frequently to teen personas than to adult personas, and most models providing fewer clinical facts to personas presenting healthcare expertise compared to those presenting none. The researchers tested a simple intervention—a system prompt specifying a minimum set of core medical facts to be included for all relevant queries—and found it reduced persona-based disparities across all models, though its effects on overall fact coverage were inconsistent and non-transferable across different systems. The authors caution that uniform mention rates are not always the appropriate clinical target, since prescription pharmacotherapy is genuinely contraindicated for minors, meaning any equitable factual floor must incorporate age-aware rather than blanket standardization.
items.citation: Artin Yousefi, Aizierjiang Aiersilan, Lorien C Abroms et al.. Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting
items.summary: Chronos-2 is a time series foundation model designed for zero-shot multivariate forecasting that can model interactions among multiple time series and heterogeneous covariates without requiring domain-specific training. Unlike most existing time series foundation models that treat each series independently, Chronos-2 infers relationships among variables directly from historical context and generates probabilistic forecasts in a general-purpose manner. The model was evaluated across diverse scientific domains, including infectious-disease forecasting, macroeconomic modeling, carbon-flux prediction, and runoff simulation, where it was benchmarked against both task-specific and general forecasting baselines. Chronos-2 achieves state-of-the-art average accuracy, improving skill scores and win rates relative to the strongest baselines, while also being substantially faster than competing probabilistic and point forecasting methods on a single mid-range GPU. The results demonstrate that a single pretrained model can capture shared temporal structure across disparate scientific domains, matching or surpassing specialized methods developed for each individual application.
items.citation: Abdul Fatir Ansari, Oleksandr Shchur, Jaris Küken et al.. Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Epidemic Forecasting and Behavioral Response Estimation with a Behavior-Coupled SEIR Model
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of forecasting epidemic dynamics that exhibit multiple infection waves driven by the interplay between disease spread and changing human behavior. The researchers developed a forecasting framework coupling a standard compartmental epidemiological model with an evolutionary model of behavioral adaptation, in which population compliance with protective measures shifts in response to perceived infection risk and the costs of compliance. Forecasting was framed as an inverse problem in which behavioral incentive parameters were inferred from hospitalization time series data, and the resulting parameter estimates were then used to generate rolling monthly predictions of infection levels. The approach was validated on both synthetic data and real hospitalization records from several U.S. states, demonstrating its ability to reproduce multi-wave epidemic patterns. Beyond predictive accuracy, the framework offers interpretable estimates of population-level behavioral incentives, providing insight into the feedback mechanisms that shape epidemic trajectories.
items.citation: Sungi Hong, Soham Das, Hossein Khazaei et al.. Epidemic Forecasting and Behavioral Response Estimation with a Behavior-Coupled SEIR Model. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Nonequilibrium Transient Centers in Continuous-Time Systems
items.summary: This paper examines long transient dynamics in continuous-time mathematical models relevant to ecology and epidemiology, where systems may behave slowly and nearly stationary for extended periods before undergoing rapid transitions, even when no true equilibrium is nearby. The authors argue that such transient behavior, rather than asymptotic outcomes like stable equilibria or attractors, is often more relevant on the finite time scales of real-world observation and intervention. To capture this phenomenon, they introduce the framework of nonequilibrium transient centers, defined as points in state space where an observable quantity remains nearly constant for a prolonged time despite the system not being at equilibrium. They develop finite-time escape criteria that provide practical conditions for identifying when trajectories near these centers will eventually leave the slow regime. The framework is illustrated using an epidemic model exhibiting delayed stability loss, in which infectious populations can linger near a disease-free state for a long time before resurging, behavior the theory describes as slow evolution near a nonequilibrium transient center followed by finite-time escape.
items.citation: Anthony Pasion, Felicia Magpantay. Nonequilibrium Transient Centers in Continuous-Time Systems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Plastics embedded with enzymes degrade readily in the sea
items.summary: This paper investigated whether plastics engineered to contain embedded enzymes capable of breaking ester bonds could biodegrade effectively in marine environments. The approach involved incorporating these ester-cleaving enzymes directly into compostable polyester materials, allowing the plastics to carry their own degradation mechanism rather than relying on environmental microorganisms. The researchers found that this method enabled rapid and complete biodegradation across a range of marine settings, including coastal seawater and deep-sea environments, even where microbial communities are sparse. The findings suggest that enzyme-embedded polyesters could represent a meaningful contribution to addressing the global problem of plastic pollution in the oceans.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it demonstrates that compostable plastics embedded with bond-breaking enzymes can degrade rapidly and completely in ocean environments, including even the deep sea where microbes are scarce. The approach offers a potential solution to marine plastic pollution by making the degradation process self-contained rather than dependent on environmental microorganisms.
items.citation: Plastics embedded with enzymes degrade readily in the sea. Nature. 2026

items.title: Cave stalagmites document global patterns in monsoon rainfall over the past 450,000 years
items.summary: Cave stalagmites from the Amazon Basin were used to reconstruct a long-term record of monsoon rainfall, which was then compared with existing records from Asia. The study found that the global monsoon system has oscillated in a regular pattern over nearly half a million years, with monsoons strengthening in one hemisphere while weakening in the other. However, this antiphased relationship broke down during warm and warming climate intervals, when monsoons in both hemispheres simultaneously weakened for extended periods lasting millennia. The findings suggest that both the South American and Asian monsoon systems have historically faltered during episodes of rapid warming, with implications for understanding how contemporary climate change may affect global monsoon dynamics.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because stalagmite records spanning hundreds of thousands of years reveal a previously documented hemispheric seesaw in monsoon strength, while also uncovering that warm and warming periods caused monsoons in *both* hemispheres to fail simultaneously for millennia—a finding with potentially alarming implications for understanding future rainfall under climate change.
items.citation: Cave stalagmites document global patterns in monsoon rainfall over the past 450,000 years. Nature. 2026

items.title: The contribution of salt marshes to wave attenuation during extreme storms
items.summary: Salt marshes are known to protect coastlines by dampening wave energy through their elevated platforms and above-ground vegetation, but how extreme storms affect this protective function has not been well quantified. Researchers conducted a large-scale flume experiment using intact transplanted salt marsh, exposing it to progressively increasing wave heights to simulate extreme storm conditions. The study found that marsh substrates remained remarkably stable with negligible erosion even under sustained wave exposure, while vegetation suffered progressive damage that gradually reduced its wave-attenuating capacity. Vegetation proved most effective at attenuating waves under low-energy conditions, where reductions exceeded ten percent and could reach as high as fifty percent, but at higher wave energies the attenuation dropped below ten percent. A global assessment corroborated these experimental findings, leading to the conclusion that while marsh platforms can withstand extreme storms, meaningful wave attenuation by vegetation is essentially limited to low-energy coastal settings.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it clarifies the actual protective limits of salt marshes during extreme storms, revealing that while the marsh platform itself resists erosion, vegetation damage compromises wave attenuation and meaningful protection from vegetation is largely confined to low-energy coastal settings. These findings have important implications for how much coastal communities can rely on salt marshes as natural buffers against severe storm waves.
items.citation: Pim Wilhelmus Johannes Maria Willemsen, Victoria G. Mason, Vincent T. M. van Zelst et al.. The contribution of salt marshes to wave attenuation during extreme storms. Nature. 2026

items.title: Cold activates a BH2 metabolic network promoting longevity and proteostasis
items.summary: This study investigated how cold temperature extends lifespan and improves protein quality control, focusing on the molecular mechanisms in the roundworm *Caenorhabditis elegans*. The researchers discovered that cold activates a multi-tissue metabolic signaling network centered on the biopterin pathway, wherein cold upregulates a biopterin-synthesis enzyme in muscle to produce dihydrobiopterin, which is then transported to distal tissues such as the intestine and neurons, where it is converted into the bioactive cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin. Tetrahydrobiopterin acts as a cofactor for a phenylalanine hydroxylase enzyme to promote tyrosine synthesis, and this axis was found to extend lifespan and prevent disease-related protein aggregation and neuronal dysfunction during aging. Notably, boosting dihydrobiopterin production specifically in muscle was sufficient to confer these benefits throughout the organism even at normal or elevated temperatures. In human cells, supplementation with dihydrobiopterin or tyrosine reduced aggregation of proteins associated with Huntington's disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, suggesting translational relevance of this cold-induced metabolic network for proteostasis and longevity.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it identifies a multi-tissue signalling network through which cold temperature promotes longer lifespan and improved protein homeostasis, revealing a mechanistic link between environmental temperature and fundamental aging processes.
items.citation: Hyun Ju Lee, Cansu Doğan, Seda Koyuncu et al.. Cold activates a BH2 metabolic network promoting longevity and proteostasis. Nature. 2026

items.title: WEE1 opposes APC/CCDH1 activity to promote S phase entry
items.summary: This study investigated previously unknown functions of WEE1, a kinase best known for preventing mitotic entry by inhibiting cyclin-dependent kinases. The researchers discovered that WEE1 also promotes cell cycle re-entry from quiescence by phosphorylating CDH1 at residues critical for its interaction with the APC/C ubiquitin ligase complex, thereby opposing APC/C-CDH1 activity during G0/G1. When WEE1 function is lost during this early cell cycle phase, cells exhibit delayed S phase entry, impaired G1/S transition, abnormal accumulation of the cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p21 during S phase, and a p21-dependent G2 arrest. The team further showed that reducing APC/C-CDH1 or p21 expression increases cellular sensitivity to acute WEE1 inhibition, while both pathways are downregulated in cells that have acquired resistance to WEE1 inhibitors. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism of cell cycle control that may help explain the toxicity and variable efficacy of WEE1 inhibitors in clinical settings, including in tumours with wild-type TP53.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals an unexpected role for WEE1 in driving quiescent cells back into the cell cycle, which could explain why WEE1 inhibitors used in cancer therapy cause harmful side effects in normal tissues.
items.citation: Luc-Alban Vuillemenot, L. Morales, Calin-Mihai Dragoi et al.. WEE1 opposes APC/CCDH1 activity to promote S phase entry. Nature. 2026

items.title: A single archaeon couples long-chain fatty acid oxidation to methanogenesis

items.title: An environmentally regulated dichotomy in cell lineages of the root
items.summary: Using single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcript mapping in Arabidopsis roots, this study investigated whether root cell types progress along a single developmental trajectory as traditionally assumed. The researchers found that most root cell lineages instead display a stereotyped bifurcating topology, where one branch is defined by a transcriptional program enriched for environmental response genes, particularly those associated with abscisic acid signalling. This environmentally responsive state occurs reproducibly across multiple distinct cell types independently of their developmental lineage, constituting an additional layer of cell identity superimposed on the canonical developmental programme. The state is conserved across different Arabidopsis ecotypes, is diminished in abscisic acid-deficient and abscisic acid-insensitive mutants, and becomes more prevalent under water-deficit conditions. These findings reveal a previously unrecognised source of environment-associated transcriptional heterogeneity that is broadly shared across root cell types and modulated by environmental signals.
items.why_notable: This work draws attention by uncovering that multiple distinct cell types in the root tip share a common, environmentally regulated cellular state, revealing an unexpected unifying dichotomy across different cell lineages. The finding suggests that environmental signals can broadly coordinate cell identity or behavior across diverse root cell populations.
items.citation: Marina Oliva, Tim Stuart, Dave T. P. Tang et al.. An environmentally regulated dichotomy in cell lineages of the root. Nature. 2026

items.title: CD51 delineates functionally distinct astrocyte subtypes in neural circuits
items.summary: This study investigated whether molecular diversity among astrocytes reflects functionally distinct cell subtypes with specialized roles in neural circuits. To do this, the researchers generated a transgenic mouse line that allowed direct comparison of CD51-positive and CD51-negative astrocyte subpopulations in vivo. They found that these two subpopulations differ in their morphological, physiological, and developmental properties in both the cortex and hippocampus. CD51-positive astrocytes were shown to selectively promote synapse formation in the developing cortex via glypican 6, drive circuit plasticity in the hippocampus through CD51 itself, and enhance functional recovery after stroke through synaptic remodelling. Together, these findings establish that astrocytes comprise specialized functional subtypes with distinct roles across brain development, maturity, and injury.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it identifies a surface marker that distinguishes functionally distinct astrocyte subtypes, revealing that one subtype plays specific roles in synapse formation, circuit plasticity, and recovery after brain injury.
items.citation: Junsung Woo, Michael R. Williamson, DongJoo Choi et al.. CD51 delineates functionally distinct astrocyte subtypes in neural circuits. Nature. 2026

items.title: Persistent neuronal stress signalling underlies Angelman syndrome phenotypes
items.summary: This paper investigated the molecular mechanisms underlying Angelman syndrome, a severe neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss of the ubiquitin ligase UBE3A. Using gain- and loss-of-function mutations combined with unbiased proteomics in mouse models and human neurons, the researchers identified asparagine synthetase as a substrate targeted by UBE3A for degradation. They found that when UBE3A is absent, asparagine synthetase accumulates abnormally in the brain, activating stress signalling pathways and broadly suppressing neuronal protein synthesis. Correcting this overabundance genetically rescued microcephaly and many behavioural deficits, suggesting that loss of UBE3A locks neurons in a persistent stress state that stunts growth during critical developmental windows. The findings propose that asparagine synthetase and the associated stress response represent promising therapeutic targets for treating Angelman syndrome.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it identifies a specific molecular mechanism — loss of a ubiquitin ligase leading to an overabundance of a stress-related enzyme — that connects to the broad range of neurological features seen in Angelman syndrome, potentially opening new therapeutic avenues for this condition.
items.citation: Kwang‐Soo Kim, Cory Gardner, Alissa Cullen et al.. Persistent neuronal stress signalling underlies Angelman syndrome phenotypes. Nature. 2026

items.title: Amazon carbon emissions driven by human actions amplified by droughts
items.summary: The Amazon rainforest is transitioning from a carbon sink to a carbon source, and this study examined the drivers and magnitude of that shift over a decade and a half of atmospheric carbon dioxide measurements. Using atmospheric monitoring to derive regional carbon fluxes, the researchers quantified the overall carbon balance of Amazonia and identified fires as the dominant emissions source, with forest uptake increasingly unable to compensate. The analysis revealed three distinct year types: wetter years with low human pressure, during which the Amazon remained close to carbon neutral; years dominated by human activities such as deforestation and degradation under moderate climate conditions, which produced substantial net emissions; and drought years amplified by large-scale climate events such as El Niño, which produced the highest emissions through widespread biomass burning. The findings demonstrate that human-driven land-use change and climate stress act as compounding factors, with droughts amplifying the carbon losses already caused by deforestation and degradation, pushing the Amazon toward a persistent and growing net carbon source.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it provides long-term observational evidence that the Amazon is losing its capacity to absorb carbon, with human-driven disturbances such as fires and deforestation compounding the effects of drought to push the region toward becoming a net carbon source.
items.citation: Luciana V. Gatti, Camilla L. Cunha, Juan C. G. Blas et al.. Amazon carbon emissions driven by human actions amplified by droughts. Nature. 2026

items.title: The proteome of Middle Pleistocene Xujiayao and common Denisovan morphology
items.summary: This paper investigated the taxonomic and phylogenetic position of Xujiayao, a key Middle Pleistocene hominin assemblage from East Asia whose evolutionary relationships have long been uncertain. The researchers combined palaeoproteomics with morphological comparisons, extracting and analysing ancient proteins from two Xujiayao specimens and comparing their skeletal features with those of other late Middle Pleistocene archaic humans from East Asia. Proteomic analysis recovered numerous endogenous proteins, and a Denisovan-specific amino acid substitution in collagen provided strong molecular evidence that the Xujiayao individuals belonged to the Denisovan lineage. Extended morphological analysis further identified a suite of shared cranial traits linking Xujiayao and the Harbin fossil with other East Asian archaic specimens such as Jinniushan, Dali, and Hualongdong, supporting their collective placement within the Denisovan lineage. Together, these findings define a broader Denisovan morphological profile that combines features reminiscent of Homo erectus and modern humans alongside traits shared with Neanderthals, while also exhibiting distinctive characteristics such as a low cranial profile with near-parallel lateral walls, a massive supraorbital torus, a flat zygomaxillary region, and weak prognathism.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it uses ancient protein analysis to link Middle Pleistocene fossils from East Asian sites to Denisovans, and it characterizes a distinctive Denisovan facial and cranial morphology that had not previously been well defined for this group.
items.citation: Song Xing, Zhongyou Wu, Qingfeng Shao et al.. The proteome of Middle Pleistocene Xujiayao and common Denisovan morphology. Nature. 2026

items.title: Drought and disease trigger novel interactions among top predators
items.summary: This study investigated how climatic and disease-related disturbances can fundamentally alter predator-predator interactions that had previously been stable. The researchers found that when an emergent disease caused a sharp decline in rabbits, a shared prey species, a lynx population began actively preying on a top raptor species after decades of neutral coexistence, with these predation events occurring specifically under drought conditions and near raptor nests where rabbit remains were present. The lynx predation reduced the raptors' lifetime reproductive success and caused territory abandonment and dispersal, suggesting the emergence of a new competitive dynamic between the two apex predators. This novel interaction also had detectable cascading effects on lower trophic levels, as declining raptor abundance was associated with an increase in an insectivorous bird. The findings highlight how synergistic anthropogenic stressors, including disease and climate-driven drought, can reshape ecological roles and interactions among apex predators with potentially broad consequences for entire ecosystems.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals how climate-driven drought and disease can force top predators into entirely new predatory interactions, with lynx preying on raptors in a way that diminishes raptor populations and sends ripple effects cascading through the broader food web.
items.citation: Fabrizio Sergio, Haruki Natsukawa, Alessandro Tanferna et al.. Drought and disease trigger novel interactions among top predators. Nature. 2026

items.title: Enzyme-embedded polyesters for accelerated biodegradation in the deep sea
items.summary: This paper investigated whether embedding degradative enzymes directly into compostable polyester plastics could accelerate their breakdown in marine environments, including the challenging deep-sea conditions where conventional compostable plastics degrade poorly. The researchers thermally incorporated enzymes into four types of compostable polyesters and deployed the resulting materials at ocean depths ranging from shallow coastal waters to abyssal depths exceeding five thousand meters. They found that enzyme-embedded polyesters achieved near-complete degradation at intermediate deep-sea depths within five months, and measurable biodegradation even under the extreme pressures and cold temperatures of the deepest deployment sites. In coastal seawater, only trace quantities of embedded enzyme were sufficient to drive rapid film degradation. The enzyme-embedded materials retained mechanical properties comparable to enzyme-free polyesters, and chemical analyses confirmed genuine mineralization of the plastic rather than mere fragmentation, supporting the approach as a viable strategy for reducing marine plastic pollution.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it demonstrates that embedding enzymes directly into compostable polyesters can achieve near-complete breakdown in deep-sea environments, a setting where conventional biodegradable plastics typically persist. The findings suggest this approach could meaningfully address ocean plastic pollution without sacrificing the material's functional performance.
items.citation: QiuYuan Huang, Noriko Iida, Noriyuki Isobe et al.. Enzyme-embedded polyesters for accelerated biodegradation in the deep sea. Nature. 2026

items.title: The anatomy of a personal health agent
items.summary: This paper developed a comprehensive personal health agent designed to reason over multimodal data from consumer wellness devices and medical records to deliver personalized health support. The researchers first identified four key user journeys — general health knowledge, personal data interpretation, wellness advice, and symptom assessment — through analysis of web searches, health forum queries, and user-centred research with both end users and health experts. These journeys informed a multi-agent architecture comprising three specialist sub-agents: one for analysing longitudinal wearable and medical data in population context, one for integrating personal data with health knowledge to generate insights, and one for coaching, multi-turn interaction, goal setting, and progress tracking. The full system was evaluated across numerous benchmark tasks using a large-scale combination of automated and human annotation, representing what the authors describe as the most comprehensive evaluation of a personal health agent to date. The work is released as an open-source framework and is presented as a concrete foundation for broadening access to high-quality personalized health support.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it presents a structured framework in which multiple specialized AI agents work together—combining data science, medical reasoning, and health coaching—to deliver comprehensive, ongoing personal health support using wearable and clinical data over time.
items.citation: A. Ali Heydari, Ken Gu, Vidya Srinivas et al.. The anatomy of a personal health agent. Nature. 2026

items.title: From Sewers to Surveillance: Monitoring Salmonella Through Wastewater.
items.summary: Wastewater surveillance offers a population-level approach to infectious disease monitoring that can detect cases missed by clinical reporting, including asymptomatic and unreported infections. This study developed and validated methods for detecting Salmonella in wastewater, combining sample concentration through polyethylene glycol precipitation, magnetic bead-based nucleic acid extraction, and quantitative PCR. These methods were deployed across a statewide surveillance network to track Salmonella transmission over a two-year period. The surveillance system revealed seasonal transmission patterns, provided approximately one week of advance warning relative to clinical case reporting, and detected outbreak activity that passive surveillance systems failed to capture. While limitations such as low pathogen concentrations and difficulty resolving serovars remain, the findings support wastewater surveillance as a valuable early-warning and outbreak detection tool when used alongside traditional public health approaches.
items.citation: Kuhn KG, Shelton K, Rimal B et al.. From Sewers to Surveillance: Monitoring Salmonella Through Wastewater.. Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.). 2027
